News.title: Moment two cops wrestle with crowbar–wielding drug dealer who tries to escape into bin before striking officer in face
News.content:
THIS is the moment two cops wrestle with a crowbar-wielding drug dealer who tries to escape into a bin before he strikes an officer in the face.

The shocking incident occurred after officers had stopped a man speeding on a moped in Brixton, South London, before he fled the scene.



In CCTV footage shared by the Met Police, the man can be seen running down Somerleyton Road with an plainclothes officer in close pursuit.

He then turns into a bin yard where he attempts to climb into an communal bin before one officer grabs his foot and drags him to the ground.



The man can be seen writhing desperately to escape as an officer is struck in the face with a crowbar before his colleague arrives and they wrestle the man on the floor.

The crowbar is eventually thrown beyond the man’s reach as they put the man in cuffs and he is led to an unmarked police car.



Cops said the man had discarded a bag on the road during the pursuit which was later found to contain Class A drugs.

He was arrested on suspicion of possession with intent to supply and grievous bodily harm and has since been bailed pending further enquiries.



The arrest marked a Met Police operation in Lambeth and Southwark aiming to crack down on gang violence.

These areas were targeted “due to a rise in gang-related tensions and a number of serious, high-profile incidents in recent months”.

The force said that over the course of a week they made 297 arrests and seized 38 dangerous weapons.

Detective Chief Superintendent Emma Bond, who led the week-long operation, said: “This activity is part of an ongoing campaign to drive down violence and make our neighbourhoods safer.

“That sustained approach is already delivering results, with knife crime down by 18 per cent across Lambeth and Southwark.



“But we know that despite this success, gangs continue to do harm to London’s communities. In recent weeks and months, more families have had to endure the unimaginable pain of losing a loved one to senseless violence.

“We do not want to see another life lost which is why we’re so determined to keep taking robust action.

“Those driving serious violence across London should be under no illusion. We are targeting them relentlessly, and we will use every power available to take weapons, drugs and dangerous offenders off our streets.”

News.title: Sick women, 25 & 26, lured disabled friend into forest & battered her with log on camera in horror ‘revenge attack’
News.content:
VILE ATTACK Sick women, 25 & 26, lured disabled friend into forest & battered her with log on camera in horror ‘revenge attack’

A TWISTED pair of friends beat a disabled woman with a log and spat on her in a “revenge attack” that was filmed to humiliate the victim.

Rebecca Cass, 26, and Channye Sweeny 25, orchestrated the ambush in Dagnam Park, near Romford, London, after alleging the victim had texted Sweeny’s ex-boyfriend.



The Old Bailey heard that Cass, who the victim thought was her friend, lured her to a secluded wooded area of the park before she and Sweeny set upon her.

The pair, who have both been convicted of assault, ordered three of their pals to film them as they beat and verbally abused the victim.



They had the intention of inflicting “maximum humiliation” on her, according to prosecutors.

Speaking at the Old Bailey on Tuesday, prosecutor Helen Owen said: “This was a premeditated assault, it was planned with the intention of humiliating the lady.

“The victim believed herself to be a good friend of Miss Cass’s. She primarily lured her from her house.

“She was taken to a wooded and secluded area where the sustained beating took place.



“The Crown say it was a revenge attack. The victim is extremely vulnerable and has learning difficulties.

“There’s phone footage (of the attack) which is rather disturbing. It shows a sustained beating of her. She was repeatedly hit with a log, spat and kicked.

“You can hear a commentary on the assault during the video.”

The attack took place after Cass texted the victim, who she had known for five years, and invited her out for the day on May 30 last year.

When the victim met Cass at the bus stop, she realised she was not alone – and had instead turned up with Sweeny and three others.



The group told the victim there had been a change of plan and they were going to Dagnam Park. When they arrived, they led her to a secluded wooded area before ambushing her.

The pair grabbed the victim and forced her to the ground, with Sweeny then kicking her and accusing her of texting her ex-boyfriend.

Sweeny picked up a log and hit the victim multiple times, aiming for her head and face, before the log finally broke.

Despite the victim being curled up in a ball, she continued kicking the defenceless woman.

Sweeny then grabbed a stick and hit her on the head with it before snatching her phone, telling her “mine, mine now”.



The assault was documented over several video recordings, the Old Bailey heard.

Cass, who was under the influence of cannabis at the time, can be seen in one of the clips picking up a log and holding it high above the victim’s head, suggesting she was going to slam it down on her.

Sweeny can also be heard demanding the truth from the victim, telling her she has seen the text messages with her former partner.

Eventually, the pair allowed the victim to leave the park and a shopkeeper helped the injured woman to call her mum. Sweeny – who was an acquaintance of the victim – had taken her phone but returned it that evening.

The victim suffered nerve and muscle tissue damage to her left hand in the attack. She also sustained bruising to the face, head, arms, ribs and back.



She received medical treatment at Queen’s Hospital in Romford on May 31.

RECOMMENDED STORIES

Sentencing of Cass, of Arlington Road, Camden Town, London, and Sweeny, of Grantham Road, Manor Park, London, was due to take place on Tuesday (August 4).

However, Judge Judy Khan KC adjourned sentencing until August 14 at Snaresbrook Crown Court to give the prosecution time to get a victim personal statement

News.title: Epstein’s ‘last refuge’ Zorro Ranch at center of new lawsuit after bombshell claim victim bodies were buried on site
News.content:
A SPRAWLING desert ranch dubbed Jeffrey Epstein’s “last refuge” is at the center of a new legal war over files that could expose further horrors linked to the convicted sex offender.

New Mexico has sued the Justice Department, accusing federal officials of blocking access to evidence needed for its criminal investigation into alleged abuse, trafficking and other sex crimes.



The probe centers on Zorro Ranch, Epstein’s isolated property south of Santa Fe, New Mexico, where survivors have alleged they were abused over several decades.

It follows a disturbing anonymous claim that two “foreign girls” were strangled and buried in the hills near the estate.



The 2019 email was allegedly written by a former ranch employee and later forwarded to the FBI.

Its claims have not been proven, but the message was included among the Epstein records released by the federal government and helped fuel demands for the property to be searched.

The allegation originated in an email purportedly sent in November 2019 by someone claiming to have previously worked at the ranch.

The writer claimed two “foreign girls” were strangled during “rough, fetish sex” and buried on the orders of “Jeffrey and Madam G,” apparently referring to Epstein and Ghislaine Maxwell.

The message alleged their bodies were hidden “somewhere in the hills outside the Zorro.”

Its claims have not been substantiated, and authorities have not announced the discovery of any human remains.



The sender also claimed to possess seven videos taken from Epstein’s home and offered to provide them on a flash drive in exchange for one bitcoin.

Conservative radio host Eddy Aragon said he forwarded the message to the FBI after receiving it and did not accept the offer.

“It felt very legitimate to me,” Aragon previously told The U.S. Sun. “That’s why I forwarded it.”

The lawsuit reveals that New Mexico formally sought the burial-related file from then-Deputy Attorney General Todd Blanche on February 13.



Exactly one month later, Attorney General Raúl Torrez wrote to then-US Attorney General Pam Bondi demanding five additional Epstein records.

According to the complaint, they include accounts from Epstein survivors who said they were brought to New Mexico and grand jury testimony from an FBI witness about abuse in the state.

Torrez told federal officials that complete versions of the records were “essential” to moving the investigation forward.

He even offered to send a New Mexico team to Justice Department headquarters in Washington to inspect the materials in person under any required security measures.



The lawsuit says no response arrived by the state’s March 27 deadline.

The New Mexico Department of Justice reopened its investigation into the ranch in February after reviewing previously sealed FBI records.

State investigators then searched Zorro Ranch on March 9 with help from New Mexico State Police and a fire department K-9 team.

It was the first law-enforcement search of the sprawling property during the renewed criminal probe, according to state officials.

Former ranch workers have since reportedly been questioned about visitors, activity at the estate and what they witnessed while working for Epstein.



One former employee said investigators were asking detailed questions about high-profile guests, including Andrew Mountbatten-Windsor, and their movements around the property.

Those questioned were being treated as potential witnesses rather than suspects and were reportedly instructed not to destroy records from their time at the ranch.

Andrew has strongly denied wrongdoing.

Torrez has now filed a federal lawsuit against Acting Attorney General Todd Blanche and the US Department of Justice.

The case was lodged Wednesday in the US District Court for the District of Columbia.



Torrez is demanding access to unredacted investigative files that he says could reveal victims, witnesses and other people tied to Epstein’s activities in New Mexico.

The complaint alleges federal officials are unlawfully obstructing the state’s power to investigate crimes committed within its borders.

The state says it is investigating potential felonies that include homicide, kidnapping, human trafficking and sexual offenses.

Its formal request highlighted nine Epstein records that allegedly show patterns of criminal conduct involving Epstein, Maxwell and their associates in New Mexico.

The lawsuit says one federal prosecution memo describes an alleged sexual assault at Zorro Ranch involving a woman other than Maxwell.



Another FBI summary reportedly recounts a survivor saying her first assault occurred in New Mexico while Epstein and another person were in the room.

New Mexico argues that redactions are concealing the identities of people in Epstein’s “inner circle,” ranch visitors and employees who may have witnessed or participated in abuse.

The complaint says publicly released Epstein files contain more than 13,000 references to Zorro Ranch and another 5,000 mentions of New Mexico.

State officials say the records include evidence concerning grooming, trafficking and sexual abuse involving Epstein, Maxwell and others associated with them.

Documents previously reviewed by The U.S. Sun suggested Epstein spent about 50 days each year at the remote compound, sometimes staying for weeks with little advance notice to staff.



The estate contained a Spanish-style mansion, airstrip, hangar, helipad and a collection of guest buildings known as Ranch Central.

Epstein was said to bring assistants, bodyguards, friends, trainers and masseuses to the estate, which employed about five or six permanent workers.

News.title: Horror moment daredevil, 22, plummets from monument in top Brit getaway city leaving him fighting for life
News.content:
THIS is the terrifying moment a man falls approximately 30ft from a protected monument leaving him with life-threatening injuries.

Footage captured the moment the 22-year-old fell from the bronze statue in Belgium after losing his balance.



The young man then plunged from the great height, hitting the stone base at the bottom of the monument before crashing onto the hard ground below.

He was rushed to hospital with life-threatening injuries.



The shocking incident occurred at the Brabo statue on the Grote Market square in the city of Antwerp, shortly before 3.30am on August 1.

The man is believed to have been “under the influence” at the time of the fall according to the cops.



The Brabo Fountain stands in front of Antwerp’s historic city hall and is a protected monument.

It has received official heritage status from Belgian authorities on 27th October 1982 due to its historical, artistic and cultural importance.



Police were investigating whether the incident caused any damage to the structure.

The man may face criminal processing’s if he is found responsible for any ruin.

He could also be slapped with an administrative fine under Antwerp city regulations.



Antwerp police spokesman Wouter Bruyns warns people not to attempt similar stunts on statues or monuments.

He said: “It is obvious that you should not climb on things that are not intended for that purpose.”

“There are no safety measures around the Brabo statue. The ground underneath is also hard. We advise everyone not to attempt such stunts.”

The incident was not the first time someone had tried to climb the famous landmark, with another stunt involving the statue going wrong almost exactly 10 years earlier.

Police said they had received no further updates on the mans current condition.



It comes as a tourist was killed in Italy after a heavy statue was hurled from a balcony by a teen boy.

Chiara Jaconis, 30, was fatally struck in the horrific freak accident.

News.title: Moment hysterical woman faceplants into kerb after being repeatedly attacked by a deranged CROW
News.content:
THIS is the bizarre moment a woman is chased down a street and attacked by a belligerent crow.

The recording shows the bird dive-bombing the woman as she steps onto the pavement.



As the two stare each other down, the woman steps cautiously into the road, not taking her eyes off the crazed crow.

The bird then makes a beeline for her again as she ducks behind the car in a frenzied panic to dodge its claws.



The woman shrieks in fear as she tries to flee the feathered fiend before tripping and hitting her head on the kerb.

The combative crow continues tormenting her until she finally makes a getaway, leaving one onlooker baffled by the encounter.





The video, thought to have been filmed in Burnley and appearing in local Facebook groups, has left the internet similarly amused, with some pointing out the crafty bird’s capacity for grudges.

One user said: “Crows remember faces. She did something to it previously, I guarantee you.”

Another wrote: “I wonder what she did to the crow? The crow doesn’t forget nor forgive.”

One quipped: “At least she didn’t overreact!”

The highly intelligent species has been known to recognise faces and hide food from other animals, as well as fashion tools out of twigs and wire.



Crows will also become significantly more aggressive during nesting season, especially during the fledgling phase when the young birds are learning to fly.

It comes after locals in Leicestershire reported one dive-bombing buzzard’s reign of terror, which left one man’s scalp shredded.

Residents in the quiet village of Coleorton live in fear of the buzzard’s daily strikes.

The man was caught on video being attacked from above, with the large bird swooping down and scratching his head.

News.title: Tragic mum-of-four, 38, recorded heartbreaking final video message to boyfriend while trapped in burning building
News.content:
FINAL GOODBYE Tragic mum-of-four, 38, recorded heartbreaking final video message to boyfriend while trapped in burning building

A MUM of four recorded a tragic final video message to her boyfriend as she fought in vain to escape a raging inferno, an inquest heard.

Laura Foulis, 38, captured her last moments on camera after being caught in a stable fire that would claim her life.



The 38-year-old died on July 3 after she became trapped inside the burning outbuilding and her body was only identifiable by her fingerprints.

An inquest into her death opened at Rochdale Coroners Court heard that the horse-loving mum used her final moments to contact her partner.



The heartbreaking footage showed several bottles and containers on fire and that Laura could be heard saying that she is “in a set of stables and cannot get out”, the inquest opening on July 28 heard.

Firefighters attended the scene and extinguished the fire, but Laura was tragically found dead in the farm stables in Milnrow, Greater Manchester.

Despite the fire damage, authorities were able to identify Laura by her fingerprints, which secured a match against the national fingerprint database.

Assistant Coroner Michael Salt said a full inquest would be held at a later date to establish the full circumstances.



“The circumstances of the lady’s death are not yet fully known, however given the information we have already it is clearly an unnatural death and therefore a full inquest is needed,” he said.

A neighbour said that the mum had been renovating the barn and was living in a mobile home nearby while making use of the stables.

At the time of her death, the coroner recorded that Laura was single and unemployed.



However, she did have a partner, to whom she sent the tragic video of her last moments after she became trapped in the burning building – but the man remains unnamed.

A man in his 40s was arrested following her death.

He has since been released with no further action taken as police now believe there was no third-party involvement.



Images taken by bystanders showed that the building had been all-but reduced to its skeleton as the inferno tore through it.

Thick clouds of black smoke billowed into the air as the fire raged.

Moving tributes were paid to Laura on social media, where she was remembered as an ‘amazing person who will be deeply missed.’

Ex-partner David Jacobs, with whom she has a son, wrote that the pair were “devastated” by the news of her death.

Another friend wrote ‘I’m absolutely shocked, I used to see Laura and the kids every morning and night walking past our house up the lane!



RECOMMENDED STORIES

“I’m so sorry for your loss and huge love goes out to her beautiful children!! Heartbreaking!”

A date for the full inquest has not yet been set.

News.title: ‘Suitcase killer’ claims he gave Brit’s body to mysterious ‘old man’ & insists his Christianity is proof he’s innocent
News.content:
THE Afghan boxer accused of killing a Brit charity worker and stuffing her body in a suitcase claims he handed her remains to an “old man”.

Sharif Ahmadzai, 26, allegedly murdered Elisabeth-Jane Ross, 38, in Athens, Greece, but has claimed his Christian faith is proof he is innocent.



He appeared in court today for an initial hearing in an unmarked grey Hyundai i30 car, alongside a number of masked police officers.

During the session, he told authorities of his “panic” when he discovered Elisabeth’s body at the apartment she was staying at in Kypseli on July 15.



Ahmadzai told court officials the same story he recited to police after his arrest – but this time added the detail of “an elderly man” who he gave the suitcase to.

The suspect claimed he met the old man, who “worked at hospitals”, at a bus stop outside the flat on the day he found Elisabeth’s body.

The mystery man supposedly advised him to dump the remains in an abandoned building – but Ahmadzai went home and left the body in the flat.

The suspect said he went back to the apartment the next day, July 16, and placed Elisabeth’s body in a suitcase.



When he arrived at an abandoned building opposite the Panhellenic University, Ahmadzai found the same man who had advised him the day before.

The suspect said: “He told me to leave the suitcase with him and he would take care of it.

“Of course, he asked me for money in return.



“I explained to him that at that moment I didn’t have any and that I would find it and give it to him.”

Ahmadzai told authorities that his Christian faith meant he was innocent of any wrongdoing.

He said: “It was from the love for my family that I drew the strength to tell you the truth.



“My wife and I are Evangelical Christians, and at the same time, we do volunteer work and charitable activities.”

He is expected back in court tomorrow.

The suspect has already admitted to putting Elisabeth’s body into a suitcase and taking her to the abandoned site.

Ahmadzai also confessed to withdrawing €10,000 (£8,500) from ATMs in Greece using stolen credit cards that belonged to the victim.



But he has continued to deny murdering Elisabeth.

In a statement, the defendant said: “I never did anything bad to anyone.

“I want you to understand me and believe me. I was just in a panic.”

He claims he saw Elisabeth, who he knew as Lisa, lying on the floor of her bathroom on July 15 before leaving her and walking home.



Racked with guilt, Ahmadzai says he returned the next day and placed the Brit’s body inside a suitcase and drove away with her in the trunk.

His version of events in court are the same as what he initially told police when arrested.

Ahmadzai is due to be formally charged with intentional homicide, robbery and illegal possession of a weapon tomorrow.



Investigators have already managed to put together several lines of enquiries linking Ahmadzai to the crime.

It comes amid fears the suspect will use “every trick in the book” to delay the murder probe against him.

Legal experts told The Sun Ahmadzai would “almost certainly” request 48 hours to prepare a testimony today – almost immediately ending the hearing.

He was seen being bundled into a car just an hour later after being assigned a court-appointed lawyer who reportedly asked for extra time.

Court officials told The Sun the suspect’s legal team was only granted 24 hours due to the “suspicion of his actions”.



Ahmadzai was taken back to a holding cell in Athens where he has already been locked up for six nights.

Chilling CCTV footage showed a man matching the Afghan’s description wheeling a black suitcase through the streets of Athens on July 16.

Several text messages were also sent to Elisabeth’s friends and family after her death which are believed to have been sent from her suspected killer.

In an attempt to cover his tracks Ahmadzai pretended to be an unnamed jihadist who killed the Scottish national because she was trying to convert people to Christianity, Greek news outlet Proto Thema reports.

Ahmadzai fled Afghanistan in 2016 after his entire family were wiped out by the Taliban.



He reportedly paid smugglers to bring him to Britain, but later crossed through Pakistan, Iran, and Turkey before eventually settling in Greece.

After converting to Christianity in 2017, he met his wife Alaina Hall, from Georgia in the US, and they married in 2023.

Elisabeth reportedly met Ahmadzai and Alaina while volunteering for a refugee charity in Greece.

Old Facebook posts from an account believed to be Ahmadzai’s speak about the man’s disdain for certain charity work.

Back in May, a post reads: “Shame on corruption dressed like charity.



“Shame on business wearing the name of Christ. In the name of Christ, people are being used.

“Volunteers, students, churches, and families from America and Europe are giving their time, money, and trust but many of them never stop to ask the most important question: ‘Where is the money really going?’

“I have met good people there. I will never deny that. But good volunteers do not automatically make a corrupt system holy.”

Bombshell testimony from Alaina in recent days suggests her husband visited Elisabeth’s apartment on the night of her disappearance.

She claimed she woke up in the early hours of July 15 to find him missing – and when she traced his location using Find My Friends it showed him at her apartment.



George Kalliakmanis, an ex-cop who heads the police union in Athens, told The Sun: “He went to the flat where she was staying for a reason.

“What was it? Nothing can be ruled out. Did she reject him? Nothing can be ruled out.”

RECOMMENDED STORIES

Alaina, who gave birth to the pair’s child a few years ago, raised suspicions with police after receiving a series of flashy gifts.

Ahmadzai had given her €2,550 (£2,200) and a new iPhone 17 Pro which Alaina feared may have been purchased using Elisabeth’s stolen bank cards.

News.title: A fifth of over-50s go on more nights out now than they did thirty years ago
News.content:
A FIFTH of over-50s go on more nights out now than they did 30 years ago.

A poll of 1,500 over 50s found those who came of age in the rave culture of the late 1980s and early 1990s are still going strong when it comes to attending nightclubs, bars, and gigs.



Research shows that around 75 per cent of over 50s polled are still attending these, with four in 10 confirming they would love to see their favourite 80s or 90s artist perform live again.

Around 27 per cent of those polled claim that live music and nightlife remain a core part of their identity and nearly half (46 per cent) say music has shaped the person they are today.



Specsavers has since created The Testlist, the first club guestlist unlocked by its free three-minute online screener and open exclusively to the over 50s across the UK and Ireland.

Groove Armada will headline the inaugural Testlist launch at London’s Phonox on Thursday, October 15.

The intimate DJ set coincides with the 25th anniversary of their Superstylin’ anthem.

Tom Findlay from Groove Armada said: “We’ve been blessed to spend 30 years in the music scene, and nothing compares to that feeling of being in a crowd with sound so powerful you can feel it in your bones.

“Our generation was the first to rave and they’re still on the dancefloor now. We put our ears to very good use and were way too busy having fun to think about the cost of it.

“I’ve experienced hearing loss and occasionally wear a hearing device so I can really relate to this campaign.”



Andy Cato from Groove Armada commented: “People put off getting their hearing checked but they do want to get on the guestlist.

“That’s where The Testlist comes into its own. And we are very proud to be part of that.”

Research from OnePoll.com found that 42 per cent of over 50s polled feel they are not given enough credit for their generation’s pioneering rave scene.

But 27 per cent say they have experienced a decline in their hearing and this has reduced the amount of live music events they attend.

Many say they experienced ringing in their ears (42 per cent), muffled hearing (22 per cent), and temporary hearing loss (11 per cent) after attending a night out.



Despite these problems, 38 per cent of people don’t take any preventative steps to protect their hearing when attending live music events.

There could be an alternative in mind as 22 per cent of those polled say they would visit a venue designed with their generation in mind.

As a supporter of the Listen for Life campaign, a first of its kind healthy hearing initiative for the music industry, championed by the Night Time Industries Association (NTIA), the Testlist event will help give fans the best listening experience that doesn’t exceed safe limits.

Sonam Sehemby, Specsavers hearing expert, said: “Hearing loss often develops gradually, making it easy to miss.

“In fact, according to The Royal College of General Practitioners (RCGP), nearly half of people aged 50 and over experience some degree of hearing loss, yet NHS data tells us people wait around 10 years before seeking help.



RECOMMENDED STORIES

“Our free online hearing screener takes just a few minutes and is a simple first step.

“We’re hoping to encourage more music fans to check their hearing, so they can continue enjoying the artists they love exactly as they were meant to sound.”

News.title: Covent Garden stabbing live: Police arrest woman in London as four men attacked
News.content:
A woman has been arrested after four men were stabbed 'with scissors' in Covent Garden in central London - the men were taken to a major trauma centre

A 47-year-old woman has been arrested after four men were stabbed in London's Covent Garden sparking a massive emergency services response.

The London Ambulance Service was called at 12.29pm today to reports of stabbings on Endell Street. Medics treated four people at the scene before taking them to a major trauma centre.

The four men are aged 34, 39, 42 and 52, the Metropolitan Police said. Two of them have now have been discharged from hospital while the other two are still being treated for injuries not believed to be life-threatening or life-changing.

The woman was arrested on suspicion of possession of an offensive weapon and assault. She was taken to police custody where she remains. The Met Police believe the incident was mental health-related and that they "seized a pair of scissors at the scene".

A Covent Garden restaurant manager Arjan Gjorga said the attacker appeared to stab "random people walking by".

News.title: Aoibheann Clarke, 16, dies after collapsing while playing in football cup final in front of dad
News.content:
Aoibheann Clarke, 16, dies after collapsing while playing in football cup final in front of dad

Aoibheann Clarke, 16, collapsed as the match entered extra time and was rushed to hospital in an ambulance — her dad was officiating the game in Taghmon, Ireland as assistant referee

View 2 Images Aoibheann Clarke, 16, died after collapsing during a final (Image: Wexford Youths Womens Football Club/Facebook)

A 16-year-old girl has tragically died after collapsing during a football final.

‌



Aoibheann Clarke, 16, was given CPR on the pitch while playing in the Girls Minor Division 6 Shield Gaelic football final in Taghmon, Ireland on Tuesday night. She was rushed to hospital in ambulance, but died a short time later.

‌



Eyewitnesses told local media that spectators' attention had been on an on-field clash between two players as the game went into extra time, before the alarm was raised over the 16-year-old girl's condition at the other end of the pitch.

‌



A number of people rushed on to the pitch to help, with Aoibheann said to have started breathing again after several minutes of chest compressions.

View 2 Images The talented youngster played for a Gaelic Athletic Association team and a football side (Image: Declan Clarke/Facebook)

Her dad had been officiating as linesman during the game, reported Irish national broadcaster RTE.

‌



Paramedics, police , fire crews, and an air ambulance all attended the scene.

The game was abandoned and her teammates at Taghmon Camross Gaelic football team stayed back at the club to wait for further news, before coaches told them she had died in hospital.

She was not known to have any underlying health conditions.

‌



In a statement, her club Taghmon Camross said: "At this incredibly difficult time, we would like to express our sincere gratitude to everyone who responded so quickly and compassionately to the emergency.

"Our heartfelt thanks go to the spectators who assisted, the first responders, the ambulance service, garda and the fire crew for their professionalism, care, and support.

"Our thoughts and prayers remain with our player's family, friends, teammates, coaches, and all who knew and loved her. We ask that everyone respects the family's privacy as they grieve this devastating loss.

‌



Aoibheann was also a talented footballer, and played for All Blacks AFC and Wexford FC.

A few weeks before she died, she had helped Wexford FC to victory in the Football Association of Ireland's Women's U19 Inter-League title.

Local sports club Wexford Camogie wrote in a tribute on Facebook: "Today, our thoughts are firmly with our friends in Wexford Ladies Football and with everyone in the Taghmon Camross Club.

‌



"Wexford Camogie is deeply saddened by the heartbreaking passing of Aoibheann Clarke, a talented 16-year-old player with her whole life ahead of her.

"We extend our heartfelt and sincere condolences to Aoibheann's family, her friends, her teammates, her club, and to everyone who had the privilege of knowing her.

"Wexford Camogie also has the Ferns Club and the Referee in our thoughts today. We acknowledge that it was a very difficult evening for all concerned, and we are thinking of them also at this incredibly sad and difficult time.

Article continues below

"May Aoibheann rest in eternal peace. She will forever be remembered by those who loved her, played alongside her, and cherished her.

"The final whistle has blown, but your spirit will forever live on in every game played."

News.title: Newcastle finally confirm Matthias Jaissle as new manager to replace Eddie Howe
News.content:
Newcastle finally confirm Matthias Jaissle as new manager to replace Eddie Howe

Newcastle quickly identified Al-Ahli boss Matthias Jaissle as their top target to replace Eddie Howe, but the announcement of his appointment was delayed - until now

View Image Matthias Jaissle has been confirmed by Newcastle (Image: FC Red Bull Salzburg via Getty Images)

Newcastle have finally confirmed the appointment of Matthias Jaissle as their new manager. Jaissle, 38, arrives from Saudi Arabian club Al-Ahli, with Newcastle paying a £9.5million compensation fee.

‌



The German replaces Eddie Howe, who shockingly resigned midway through pre-season last week. Jaissle has already been working with Newcastle's squad in La Manga, Spain for the last few days.

‌



But Al-Ahli wanted to delay the announcement until 7pm on Wednesday. Jaissle spent three years in Saudi Arabia following spells with Red Bull Salzburg and Liefering in Austria.

‌



In each of the last two seasons, Al-Ahli won the Asian Champions League. But the 38-year-old has decided to move to St James' Park, kicking off a new era at the Saudi-owned club.

"When Newcastle United comes your way, you take notice," Jaissle commented in Newcastle's announcement. "The ambition of the club, the vision for the future and the opportunity ahead made this an incredibly compelling place to be.

"I have followed the club's journey closely in recent years and the progress that has been made is clear for everyone to see. I am incredibly excited about the future. I fully and unreservedly believe in this project, the ambition and the direction the club is taking.

‌



"There is a clear vision, strong leadership and an exceptional platform to build on. My teams are built on togetherness, hard work, intensity and a passion to improve every single day.

"I will bring full commitment, full energy and a determination to give everything I have to help this club achieve its ambitions. I believe there is enormous potential within this squad and throughout the football club. I am excited to work with the players, staff and leadership team to help take the club forward.

"I cannot wait to get started and will attack this opportunity. I give my complete commitment and total energy to bringing further success to Newcastle United."

‌



Sporting director Ross Wilson added: "Matthias' leadership style and football philosophy are strongly aligned with our sporting vision. His teams play high-energy football and we could feel his passion during all of our discussions throughout the recruitment process.

"He has consistently demonstrated an ability to improve players, build cohesive teams and create elite performance environments in his coaching career.

"His successes at Salzburg and Al-Ahli underline his ability to deliver results while developing a clear football identity. We believe he is uniquely positioned to build on the strong foundations already in place and help take Newcastle United forward."

Article continues below

There will be more to follow on this breaking news story and Mirror Sport will bring you the very latest updates, pictures and video as soon as possible.

Please check back regularly for updates on this developing story.

News.title: M60 traffic: Motorway closed clockwise near Stretford after 'police incident'
News.content:
A stretch of the M60 clockwise in Greater Manchester was shut due to a police incident, with traffic building near Stretford

A serious police incident forced the closure of the M60 clockwise in Greater Manchester.

Long queues built up between Junction 3 for the A34 Kingsway and Junction 7 for the A56 Chester Road at Stretford, with traffic held within the closure. The motorway has since reopened and the queues have cleared.

National Highways said at the time: "Traffic is held on the M60 clockwise between J5 Manchester & J6 Stretford due to a Police-led incident. Current delays 30 mins on approach, 3 miles of congestion."

Traffic monitoring service Inrix said: "Congestion to just after J1 (Stockport Pyramid), with traffic slowing on the opposite carriageway past the scene due to onlookers. The A5103 Princess Parkway is also stationary heading north on approach to J5. Cameras show the road is closed across all junctions for a police incident located between J5 and J6. Trapped traffic is being taken off at J5."

News.title: Spotify down: Major website outage as music listeners 'get error trying to load'
News.content:
Spotify users reported issues with the music services website, app, and the server connection, according to Downdetector

Spotify down: Major website outage as music listeners 'get error trying to load'

Spotify's web player was down for hundreds of account users across the UK with people reporting error messages when trying to load.

According to Downdetector, a website which tracks online outages, people also experienced problems with the music service's app and server connection.

Searches for issues with Spotify's Web Player rose. One user commented on Downdetector that they were "getting an error message when loading both the website and app".

News.title: No public inquiry into Jeffrey Epstein's actions in UK planned - but PM will meet victims
News.content:
No public inquiry into Jeffrey Epstein's actions in UK planned - but PM will meet victims

The government said Andy Burnham is committed to meeting victims of paedophile financier Jeffrey Epstein - but said an inquiry into his actions in the UK is not being considered

Victims' hopes of a public inquiry into disgraced paedophile Jeffrey Epstein's actions in the UK were dashed on Wednesday - after initially being raised.

Andy Burnham is considering meeting victims and look at possible options forward, but no inquiry is actively being considered by Downing Street.

Confusion erupted on Wednesday after Victims Minister Alex Davies-Jones said the new Prime Minister is “looking into” a possible public inquiry into the UK actions of Epstein, as well as into the alleged actions of former Harrods owner Mohamed Al Fayed.

Ms Davies-Jones said she has “been assured that the Prime Minister is taking this very seriously" and had agreed to meet with the late American financier's victims.

Ms Davies-Jones, an ally of Wes Streeting, resigned as Victims Minister in May, criticising a lack of “bold, radical action” under former prime minister Keir Starmer. She returned to the position when Mr Burnham took office, saying she had received assurances he "will work with us to look at systemic change across the system for all victims, whether that be the Epstein victims, Harrods survivors, grooming gangs victims".

Former neo-Nazi withdraws as Tory council election candidate after Kemi Badenoch offers him job READ MORE :

View Image Andy Burnham is committed to meeting Epstein's victims, the government said (Image: Annabel Lee-Ellis/PA Wire)

But a statement from the Ministry of Justice later said: "Our thoughts are firmly with the victims of Jeffrey Epstein, who have survived devastating trauma. As Minister Davies-Jones said, we are reviewing what is possible and will look at all options to support victims and survivors.

"The Prime Minister is committed to meeting with victims, but a public inquiry is not being actively considered."

According to the BBC, leading Labour campaigners on Violence Against Women and Girls sent Mr Burnham a document calling for full public inquiry into the UK activities of Epstein. He reportedly received the document as he was finalising plans to become PM.

Asked if a public inquiry into Epstein is a possibility, Ms Davies-Jones told BBC Newsnight on Tuesday: “We are looking into this, we are reviewing what is possible… same with Harrods survivors.

“We already have a now statutory inquiry underway for the grooming gangs victims. I have been assured that the Prime Minister is taking this very seriously.

“He will meet with those victims and he is looking at what is possible, now he has access to all of the information as Prime Minister to see what action we can take.”

Ms Davies-Jones, who was re-appointed as Victims' Minister last month when Mr Burnham entered No10, said she received assurances from him before deciding to take the job again. “I was having multiple conversations with him and his team," she said.

“He agreed to meet with the Epstein victims. He was in close contact with them throughout that period where he was becoming Prime Minister, and he has assured me that he will meet them now he’s Prime Minister and will work with us to look at systemic change across the system for all victims, whether that be the Epstein victims, Harrods survivors, grooming gangs victims.”

She continued: “What more can we do to truly make sure that our criminal justice system is taking victims seriously, that they can rebuild that faith and trust in the system again? And I have had assurances from the Prime Minister that he’s willing to do that and make that happen.”

After Ms Davies-Jones's comment about an inquiry, Anoushka di Georgiou, an Epstein survivor, admitted: “Survivors have heard promises before, so what matters now is action, not headlines.

"If there is to be a public inquiry, it must include all three cases." Asked about a public inquiry on Wednesday morning, Justice minister Jake Richards said Mr Burnham would take his time to decide the "best route for victims". He said: "Well, I know that Alex and the Victims Minister have discussions with the Prime Minister about it. It's right that we look into what we can do.

"No stone should be left unturned when we consider these horrific crimes that seem to have happened at a huge scale. The Prime Minister will look into it. He'll take his time, no doubt, to think about the best route for victims, but also to crucially ensure lessons are learned to make sure that these sorts of things never happen again."

Article continues below

Regarding Epstein, the document reportedly calls for the scope of any Epstein inquiry to focus on UK borders and question how he was able to fly in and out of UK military bases on his private jet – often with women who had allegedly been trafficked.

News.title: Olympic stadium provides shelter for dogs rescued from Greece wildfires
News.content:
Olympic stadium provides shelter for dogs rescued from Greece wildfires

More than 100 dogs rescued from the wildfires in Greece are being looked after by volunteers at Megara Olympians Municipal Stadium as a running track is turned into a temporary home

View 3 Images An athletics stadium in Attica, Greece is being used to shelter dogs rescued from the wildfires (Image: Getty Images)

A stadium built for Olympic athletes has been turned into an emergency shelter to house dogs rescued from wildfires in Greece.

‌



Dry weather and ferocious winds of up to 78mph have spread fires across the Attica region surrounding Athens.

‌



Hundreds of firefighters continued to battle the blaze on Wednesday after homes burnt to the ground in the villages of Porto Germeno and Psatha.

‌



At the Megara Olympians Municipal Stadium, volunteers have turned a running track into a makeshift home for pups caught up in the disaster.

Rescued dogs could be seen catching some much-needed rest after being fed and given bowls of water.

View 3 Images Dogs are being given food, water and a place to sleep on the running track (Image: Getty Images)

‌



England transformed into barren Western-like frontier as dramatic photos capture horror extent of drought READ MORE :

Supermarkets including Tesco and Sainsbury's pull disposable BBQs from sale after wildfire warning READ MORE :

More than 110 animals have been housed at the arena since the wildfires began last week, with vets looking over each of the dogs as they come in to check for any injuries or signs of illness.

Some of those rescued are strays, while others were seen wearing their owner's collars.

Charities have warned that the fires are devastating the habitats of Greece's wild animals, including wild horses and deer.

‌



The Attica region has lost 42% of its forests to wildfires in the last 10 years, figures released this week showed.

Prime Minister Kyriakos Mitsotakis said: "I would like to reiterate once again that when a forest burns, this does not mean that the forest is lost forever. Forests that burn, especially those consisting of Aleppo pine, undergo a process of natural regeneration, which must of course be supported and protected. This is happening to a large extent in Attica.

"I would ask the competent authorities to present the relevant data so that the impression is not created that ‘almost all the forests of Attica have been destroyed’ and that ‘the damage caused is irreversible’.

‌



View 3 Images Rescued animals are being checked over by vets (Image: Getty Images)

"Clearly, we are dealing with major environmental damage, and we will do everything within our power to support nature as it proceeds, at its own pace, through the process of natural regeneration."

Authorities say 33 people were arrested across Greece between June 29 and August 2 for starting fires, including 30 through negligence and three on suspicion of arson.

‌



Most of the negligence cases involved farm work, including welding, which has been carried out despite local bans.

Planes and helicopters have been used to dump water on the hotspots when winds allow.

Costas Tsingas, head of the Greek Firefighters Association, said yesterday: "The goal is for the day to end better than it started.

Article continues below

"There is a huge fire load in the area and the risk goes up as the day progresses."

News.title: FBI opened probe into whether Trump was 'Russian agent', bombshell memos show
News.content:
FBI opened probe into whether Trump was 'Russian agent', bombshell memos show

The FBI was concerned US President Donald Trump was working in coordination with Russia during his first term when he fired former FBI Director James Comey, declassified documents have revealed

View 2 Images The FBI looked into whether Trump was a 'Russian agent', according to newly declassified documents (Image: Getty Images)

The FBI opened an investigation into whether Donald Trump was acting as an asset for Russia when he fired FBI Director James Comey, newly declassified documents show.

‌



The probe, known as "Oxferd Comma," was linked to Crossfire Hurricane, the Bureau's probe into whether Trump's 2016 campaign worked with the Kremlin to get the 45th president elected.

‌



An administration official has said the agent theory was not back up by any evidence. The investigation was closed on April 9, 2019, with no charges against Trump.

‌



Trump has long railed against the investigation into his campaign and Russia, repeatedly calling it a hoax and a witch hunt.

View 2 Images James Comey was fired by Donald Trump (Image: AP Photo/Andrew Harnik)

‌



After Trump fired Comey in May 2017, the FBI grew suspicious that the President could be obstructing justice, which then led to former Special Counsel Robert Mueller's appointment and investigation into the President.

Trump said that he fired Comey over his handling of former Secretary of State Hillary Clinton's email scandal that year.

But some FBI officials believed that the Republican could have fired the director at the behest of Russia.

Article continues below

"Based on the facts and circumstances provided to date, the FBI believes that opening this investigation is the least intrusive method to address the serious national security risk posed by the activities alleged," one of the declassified bureau memos says.

John Solomon, who is currently serving in the Trump administration on a task force focused on election integrity, announced the files release on X, before asking users: "Should Special U.S. Attorney Joe diGenova treat the opening of Oxferd Comma as an overt act in a criminal conspiracy to violate President Trump’s civil liberties."

News.title: Ex neo-Nazi activist withdraws as Tory election candidate
News.content:
A former neo-Nazi selected by the Conservatives to fight a council election next year has pulled out after a backlash against his candidacy.

Joshua Bonehill-Paine was convicted of racially harassing Jewish former Labour MP Luciana Berger in 2016, while already serving a separate jail sentence for sharing antisemitic posts.

Tory leader Kemi Badenoch had defended the decision to select him as a candidate for the new Somerset Council seat of Crewkerne South, saying he had been rehabilitated and her party "believes in second chances".

But Bonehill-Paine said he had now withdrawn his candidacy, and had been offered a position as an anti-extremism adviser to the party.

In a social media post, he said the position with the Conservative Party's Culture and Integration Commission would focus on advising on how to prevent young men from being radicalised.

Berger, who now sits as Baroness Berger in the House of Lords, branded the appointment an "insult," adding that making him a party adviser was "no better than allowing him to stand as a council candidate".

Bonehill-Paine spent three years in prison after he was jailed in 2015 for posting antisemitic material ahead of a planned neo-Nazi rally. He was convicted of racially harassing then-Labour MP Berger the following year.

He has described his past views as "indefensible" and says he has spent years opposing antisemitism since leaving prison in 2018.

But the party's decision to pick him for the Somerset seat sparked a huge political backlash, with Jewish groups declining the offer of a meeting with him.

Baroness Berger, who attended court at the OId Bailey in London to give evidence in Bonehill-Paine's trial, has said his past behaviour fell "very, very short" of the standard required to stand for public office.

Speaking earlier, she said Bonehill-Paine's harassment "affected my life in lots of different ways because of the volume of the material that he was disseminating and putting out, the extremity of it in terms of just frankly how shocking and awful it was".

In sentencing remarks, the judge said it was "difficult to envisage a worse case than this of racially aggravated harassment of this kind", adding Bonehill-Paine had "sat in the dock smirking throughout the trial" and had "plainly enjoyed" Baroness Berger's discomfort.

News.title: Woman arrested after four stabbed in central London
News.content:
A 47-year-old woman has been arrested after four men were stabbed in Covent Garden in central London, the Metropolitan Police said.

The men, aged 34, 39, 42 and 52, were taken to hospital after emergency services were called to reports of a stabbing in Endell Street at about 12:30 BST.

The force said two men remain in hospital with injuries not thought to be life threatening or life changing while the other two have been discharged.

The woman was arrested on suspicion of possession of an offensive weapon and assault. The Met said it was believed to have been a mental health-related incident.

News.title: Family 'devastated' by death of girl, 9, as man charged with murder
News.content:
The family of a nine-year-old girl who died after being found seriously injured in Arbroath have said they are "devastated" at her loss, as a man appeared in court charged with her murder.

Minnie Merriman, from West Yorkshire, died in Dundee's Ninewells Hospital on Monday.

A 35-year-old man, who police said was known to the girl, has appeared in court charged with her murder.

Christopher Rice from Wakefield, West Yorkshire, made no plea during an appearance in private at Forfar Sheriff Court and was remanded in custody.

News.title: Anthropic AI used fake profiles to target people in hack then hid the evidence
News.content:
Two of the world's most powerful AI tools created fake human profiles to try and trick people in attempted cyber-attacks, the UK's AI Security Institute (AISI) has revealed.

In the most serious case, Anthropic's Mythos AI tried to gain access to a service by sending private messages, having set up fake accounts mimicking real people - then hid the evidence.

It comes shortly after the two companies involved in the AISI testing - Anthropic and OpenAI - separately revealed in recent weeks instances of their tech hacking into other companies.

The firms said, in this latest case, the AISI's test had reduced or removed normal safeguards.

The AISI said on that Tuesday Mythos - and OpenAI's Sol - AI models had engaged in a level of "autonomy and deception" it had not seen before.

It clarified most of the malicious actions were carried out by Mythos.

AISI evaluators first noticed "unusual data transfers leaving our research systems" during a test, then found that "some of the agents being tested had engaged in sustained, potentially harmful activity directed at real people and organisations".

In the most serious case, a Mythos agent followed the routine of a human cyber-attacker by trying to trick people into giving it access to GitHub, a large platform where technology developers store software code.

The agent was trying to insert "malicious code" into GitHub's system.

It identified and researched the people who maintained GitHub and created a series of fake accounts based on those real people.

It sent messages and files through a file-sharing service as part of an effort to pressure and trick the people into approving its malicious code.

When challenged, "it edited its earlier activity to appear harmless and considered adopting a fresh identity to continue," AISI said.

Throughout the attempts, it was human review that stopped the agent from succeeding in delivering the malicious code to GitHub.

While AISI said the Mythos agent had not been instructed specifically to avoid or carry out such behaviour, it was "the first time we have seen risks around autonomy and deception manifest this clearly, without specific prompting, in the real-world".

The rival AI companies, which are poised to be listed on the public stock market, have been in the headlines in recent weeks after announcing their tools were responsible for several cyber-hacking incidents.

News.title: See the Sun like never before with most detailed images yet
News.content:
Scientists using the world's most powerful solar telescope have captured the surface of our Sun in new, unprecedented detail.

Images and footage show "whirlpools" of activity that it has not been possible to see before.

It is the Sun's magnetic field being twisted and moved by the motion of hot gas.

That constant swirling is a driving force behind bursts of energy from the Sun, creating so-called space weather, that can disrupt Earth's power grids and satellites, and could even injure astronauts.

"The Sun is the source of that energy and of all of that space weather," explained Dr David Boboltz from the US National Solar Observatory, external (NSO).

Capturing more detailed pictures of our solar system's star will help in responding to that weather, he said.

"To figure out and eventually predict space weather, we want to understand the physics of the Sun, all the way down to the smallest scales."

News.title: Student loan repayment rates an 'unsustainable burden', chancellor told
News.content:
More than 120 MPs and peers have asked the chancellor to carry out an "urgent review" of the student loan repayment system.

An open letter coordinated by the campaign group Rethink Repayment says the current set-up places an "unsustainable burden on the next generation of workers".

Among the cross-party signatories are MPs with their own Plan 2 student loans, which have come under particular scrutiny this year.

Last week, Education Secretary Lucy Powell said the interest rate on those loans was "egregious" and the issue was at the top of her in-tray.

Current and former students have different student loan plans depending on where they live in the UK and when they went to university.

The letter to Chancellor John Healey does not specify a particular plan signatories would like to be reformed, nor does it name a particular nation.

However, the debate has centred around Plan 2 loans, which were taken out by students in England between September 2012 and July 2023 and are still issued in Wales. Graduates pay back what they earn above the repayment threshold at a rate of 9%.

The letter says that "successive governments' adjustments to repayment thresholds â together with high interest and marginal tax rates â are placing an unsustainable burden on the next generation of workers".

It says many middle-income graduates "see less than half of any hard-earned pay rise due to a combination of income tax, national insurance and student loan repayments".

It adds: "We are united in the belief that the current repayment framework requires urgent review... to ensure it is fair, sustainable, and supportive of aspiration."

News.title: After deadly Kyiv strike, Ukraine warns interceptor shortage is costing lives
News.content:
At the Kvitneva railway station near Kyiv, workers lift white body bags from the pockmarked platform and carry them to waiting ambulances.

Shoes, glasses and some pieces of clothing mark the spot where eight people were killed during Russia's latest massive aerial attack on Ukraine.

Overnight, Moscow fired 115 drones and 24 ballistic missiles. Most of the drones were shot down, but Kyiv's depleted air defences did not intercept any of the missiles.

Twenty-one people were killed and dozens more were injured.

As the medics leave the scene, another team moves in quickly to repair the power lines above the track so train services can resume. This is the rapid recovery and clear-up Ukrainians have become all too familiar with.

The latest Russian barrage destroyed storage and logistics facilities - from online retailer warehouses to a postal sorting centre.

In Kvitneva, it is not clear if the target was the railway itself or the warehouse beside it, which was also hit and was still smouldering hours later. Down the road, another warehouse was still ablaze more than 12 hours after the attack.

The attack started just after midnight, with very little warning. It was one of the most intense nights of bombardment Kyiv has endured in recent months.

Nearby, Anastasiia Dudley's house was almost totally destroyed but she and her mother survived â shaken but unharmed.

News.title: Police chief considers joining legal action over PC Harper killers' early release
News.content:
The driver of the vehicle, Henry Long, received a 16-year sentence and is not eligible for early release.

Speaking on the Today programme, Thames Valley Police chief Jason Hogg urged the government to reconsider its position.

Only prisoners convicted of murder, rape, grooming, and serious child sex offences will be excluded from the scheme in England and Wales - while those convicted of manslaughter remain eligible.

"I fully understand the challenges around the crisis in the prison system," he said.

"But the decision made and where that line has been drawn, I do not believe that people responsible for taking the life of another citizen in our country should be released early."

He said: "I was informed yesterday that the Police Federation are considering legal action, I am in discussions with the Police Federation with regards to this matter".

Asked whether this meant he would join them, he said: "I think we need to get some legal advice in relation to this. This is something I certainly would consider."

Following PC Harper's death and a campaign by his widow Lissie, Parliament passed "Harper's Law", which gives mandatory life sentences to the killers of emergency services workers. It also doubles the maximum penalty from 12 months to two years for those who assault police or other emergency workers.

But the new rules - introduced in 2022 - did not apply retrospectively to the sentencing of PC Harper's killers, and so do not prevent them from being released early.

Hogg said: "The law isn't retrospective and we all understand that, but the fact that they are released early simply seems perverse."

Aileen O'Connor, branch chairman of Thames Valley Police Federation told BBC Breakfast her organisation was exploring whether legal action was an option.

"If it is an avenue we can explore then I'll get behind that 110%," she said.

As for what shape a potential legal challenge might take, she said: "Ultimately that's for the specialists, the barristers and those in that legal sector to make that decision whether there is a challenge there.

"If there is a challenge then we will look to take that challenge."

Sentencing minister Jake Richards told the BBC it would be wrong to pick out individual cases and block two of PC Harper's killers from early release.

Although the government had reviewed what sentences would be excluded from the early release scheme, he confirmed "manslaughter is not one of those offences".

On Wednesday the Ministry of Justice released a new list of exclusions that will be exempt from the early release scheme.

It said rapists, as well as criminals sentenced for child sex offences and grooming and conspiracy offences for these crimes, will no longer be eligible to leave prison early.

Murderers and terrorists were already not eligible for the early release scheme.

Richards said: "It would be wrong to pick out individual cases within different offending cohorts. That wouldn't be right. It wouldn't be lawful either. So it is correct that those two individuals will be subject to the new regime from October".

News.title: Miliband says reopening Strait of Hormuz 'essential' as he meets Rubio
News.content:
Reopening the Strait of Hormuz is essential to bringing down the cost of living in the UK, Foreign Secretary Ed Miliband has said as he met his US counterpart Marco Rubio.

The Labour minister is in Washington for his first official one-on-one meeting with Rubio.

The pair were expected to discuss the war in Ukraine and the humanitarian crisis in Gaza.

Miliband was invited to the US capital by Rubio after they met on the sidelines of a foreign ministers' summit in the Philippines, where the former Labour leader made his debut as foreign secretary.

The White House was reported to be concerned about Prime Minister Andy Burnham's decision to hand Miliband the Foreign Office brief, given his previous criticism of US President Donald Trump as a racist and a misogynist.

Trump is also a trenchant opponent of wind farms and supports the opening up North Sea oil and use of fossil fuels, whereas in his former role as UK energy secretary, Miliband championed net zero and renewables.

Burnham has signalled a shift in North Sea oil policy, earning praise from the Oval Office, but the dynamic between Miliband and Rubio was set to be closely watched.

Last month, Washington's top diplomat in London, Warren Stephens, said Miliband had been "wrong" in 2016 to call Trump "a racist, misogynistic self-confessed groper" and added "hopefully his views have changed".

Speaking ahead of the talks, Miliband said: "The government is committed to nurturing our strong, enduring and essential alliance with the US.

"I am greatly looking forward to my second meeting with Secretary of State Marco Rubio, in which we will discuss the ongoing work to reopen the Strait of Hormuz and secure a lasting ceasefire, which is essential to ease cost-of-living pressures on British families."

The strategic sea route, which had been open before the US and Israel launched the war in February, has been a flashpoint in the Middle East conflict and disruption to trade has driven up fuel and food prices.

Miliband added: "We will also discuss how we can continue to stand shoulder to shoulder with Ukraine against Russia's war - as well as the importance of addressing the dire humanitarian situation in Gaza and working towards a lasting peace for Palestinians and Israelis."

In the face of erratic US support, the UK foreign secretary was set to stress that Ukraine's security is inseparable from European and transatlantic security and restate the UK's commitment to stand with Kyiv for as long as it takes.

Following their meeting, US state department spokesman Tommy Pigott said: "The two discussed the importance of Europe taking on a greater role in its own security.

"They reiterated their shared commitment to safe transit in the Strait of Hormuz and ensuring Iran never develops or obtains a nuclear weapon."

Miliband will be taking the UK's seat on the World Bank board, so he will also meet its president Ajay Banga during his visit to discuss development, climate change and strengthening global resilience

Separately on Wednesday, new Defence Secretary Wes Streeting visited Ukraine for the first time since he started in the role.

He met President Volodymyr Zelensky at the National Security Defence Council meeting in Kyiv earlier today, which is a meeting with all the military and civil officials and ministers in government.

In a post on Telegram, Zelensky said he and Streeting discussed how London and Kyiv could jointly protect people who face "ballistic threats" from Russia.

He said: "We discussed how the UK could help Ukraine better protect our cities and communities from such ballistic threats - both bilaterally and multilaterally - just as it has done many times before by helping secure supplies of scarce defensive equipment.

"In particular, we discussed opportunities to establish co-production of certain types of weaponry, as both the UK and Ukraine possess strong battle-proven capabilities.

"We also discussed sanctions against Russian enterprises involved in the production of ballistic missiles."

He added: "I am grateful to the United Kingdom, His Majesty, the Prime Minister, and the British people for their unwavering support."

News.title: Gary Glitter appears in court over historical sex offence charges
News.content:
Dressed in a blue shirt and wearing sunglasses, Glitter appeared by video link from His Majesty's Prison Channings Wood for the 11-minute hearing.

Under his real name, Gadd was told of the charges against him and spoke only to confirm his name and date of birth.

The prosecutor, Jonathan Polnay KC, told the court that Gadd said in a police interview he did not know the complainant, and that the allegations against him were false.

He also told the court that the offences involved one person, and are said to have taken place between the years of 1978 and 1981 when the complainant was eight to 11 years old.

He said she lived near where Glitter lived and that was how he came to know her. She says he gave her chocolate and that he invited her into his house where the offences occurred.

The allegations were first reported to the Metropolitan Police on 9 January 2025 and an investigation into the circumstances was launched.

Gadd was first interviewed on 22 July last year in relation to the investigation.

The 82-year-old was one of the biggest pop stars of the 1970s with a string of number one hits.

The Met said in July that the alleged victim was being supported by specialist officers and had been made aware that Glitter had been charged.

The singer is currently being held in HMP Channings Wood in Devon.

News.title: Traitors star Joe Marler to become BBC's first celebrity Gladiator
News.content:
Former rugby star Joe Marler is to become the first ever celebrity Gladiator on the BBC's popular entertainment series.

The 36-year-old, who also took part in the first series of Celebrity Traitors, will be known as Mauler and face contenders when the fourth series of Gladiators begins in 2027.

"Mauler will see you now," Marler said in a video posted on Instagram, external announcing the news, recorded in the Gladiators dressing room.

The BBC said Marler will make his debut with a series of "special appearances packed with power, personality and plenty of surprises".

Filming for the fourth series is currently under way in Sheffield, the BBC confirmed in a statement.

"Known for his uncompromising style of play and larger-than-life sense of humour, Joe has built a reputation as one of the UK's most entertaining sporting personalities," the corporation said.

"Now, he's taking on an entirely new challenge as he joins the ranks of the Gladiators, bringing his trademark physicality and competitive spirit to one of television's toughest arenas."

The former England rugby international star, who is from Heathfield, Sussex, will join fellow Gladiators such as Nitro, Viper, Diamond and Sabre in battle when the show returns next year.

Gladiators was a hugely successful show on ITV in the 1990s, and saw members of the public take on a group of elite athletes who each had their own on-screen persona.

Olympic swimmer Sharron Davies, who like Marler was already known as a famous sports personality, joined that iteration of the show in 1995 as the character Amazon.

The format was revived by Sky for two series in 2008, before the current iteration launched in 2024, quickly becoming a hit for BBC One.

A celebrity spin-off is separately in the works, featuring contestants including presenter AJ Odudu, comedian Sara Pascoe, podcaster Chris Ramsey and social media star George Clarke.

News.title: No misconduct case for officer who shot Chris Kaba
News.content:
The Met police officer who shot Chris Kaba will not face misconduct proceedings, the Independent Office for Police Conduct (IOPC) has said.

Sgt Martyn Blake shot the 24-year-old in Streatham, south London, in 2022 after Kaba tried to ram his way past police cars. Blake was cleared of murder following a trial in 2024.

A decision was made in January to pause any proceedings involving Blake until a law change relating to the use of force in misconduct cases was introduced and its impact was clear, the IOPC said.

Commissioner Sir Mark Rowley said the IOPC's decision brought an end to "almost four years of uncertainty" for Blake, calling the accountability process for police officers "disgraceful".

In June the use of force test in such cases changed from the civil law test to the criminal law test, meaning actions that did not amount to a crime should not amount to misconduct either.

Referring to Blake by his cypher NX121, Rowley said: "Today's decision finally brings to an end almost four years of uncertainty for NX121, his family and the wider firearms command, with all the considerable worry and stress that has brought.

"We also recognise the profound impact on Chris Kaba's family, who continue to grieve their loss."

News.title: Restrict sale of pet flea treatments, government urged
News.content:
Pet flea treatments should be banned from general sale, a Lords committee has urged, after an inquiry raised concerns about their impact on their environment.

Spot-on treatments to prevent parasite infestations in fur and on skin are currently widely available for pet owners to buy in supermarkets and online.

But the House of Lords environment committee said their sale should be restricted, adding widespread use posed a potential threat to natural ecosystems.

The government said it was continuing to assess the availability of the treatments in order to ensure "correct usage by owners".

Currently, dog and cat owners are frequently advised to use preventative spot-on treatments every month to avoid parasite infestations.

But in a series of evidence sessions, the committee heard such blanket usage is not supported by robust scientific evidence and is likely to be harming the environment.

Many vets do not treat their own pets monthly, the committee heard, instead regularly checking their pets' fur with flea combs and restricting use to when fleas were spotted.

The committee heard that high volumes of fipronil and imidacloprid, common active ingredients in spot-on treatments, have been found in UK streams and rivers, killing off aquatic life, with a knock-on effect on wildlife higher up the food chain.

These chemicals have already been banned for use as agricultural pesticides because of their impact on wildlife such as bees, while the committee said "very little is known" about the impacts of newer chemicals such as isoxazolines.

In a report, external, the cross-party committee recommended that only vets, pharmacists and other qualified professionals should be able to sell such treatments, with pet owners advised to take a precautionary approach to using them.

News.title: Man gets third-degree burns from hot sand after using disposable beach BBQ
News.content:
Warning: This article contains a distressing image

A man who suffered third-degree burns from hot sand after using a disposable barbecue on a beach has warned others to be aware of the dangers.

Sam Knight had been using it on Cefn Sidan Beach, Carmarthenshire, with his family and stepped on sand that was still hot.

The 27-year-old had to be carried off the beach after suffering badly blistered feet and needed weeks of treatment.

Experts at a burns centre say injuries such as this are becoming increasingly common and warned beach goers to take precautions.

Knight told Radio Wales Breakfast he was not aware that sand could be a "real hazard".

He had used tongs to move the barbecue to one side and extinguished it, so he thought it was safe.

"When I returned to the area, I stepped on a boiling hot patch of sand, and had to be carried off the beach," he added.

Knight was taken to Neath Port Talbot Hospital referred to a burns specialist.

"I couldn't walk for a couple of weeks so I had to take a fortnight off work," he added.

David Fligelstone and Menna Davies are physiotherapists who work with the burns centre at Swansea Bay University Health Board.

Fligelstone said the number of incidents they are seeing is "going up year on year".

"The key thing is that people don't understand is that sand stays hot for such a long time after a barbecue is moved," he said.

"When you look at the evidence it's always the sand that hasn't been cooled that ends up causing that injury."

Davies said injuries like this can be "quite painful" and need to be dressed for a "long period of time".

News.title: Dewormer and scabies drugs being sold as cancer treatments, BBC investigation finds
News.content:
Animal dewormer and a drug used to treat scabies are being sold and promoted as unproven cancer treatments, a BBC investigation has found.

Following a tip off, an undercover journalist was able to buy fenbendazole and ivermectin from a stairlift salesman in south Wales, and also found them for sale on Amazon.

Macmillan Cancer Support said it was concerned by the findings and that a growing number of people were asking about the medicines, despite "no clinical evidence" that they work.

Amazon said it had "proactive measures in place" to stop prohibited products being listed by third-party sellers.

Senior doctors are worried vulnerable patients could be put at risk by taking the medicines, as they say it could harm or delay conventional treatment.

Six months ago, Rebecca Holder contacted the BBC after a visit from stairlift salesman Jason Sarver.

She said Sarver and her father Bob, who had a brain tumour, lung cancer and needed help with his mobility, had been discussing stairlifts when the salesman changed the topic to talk about the drugs.

News.title: Afghan boxer appears in court in connection with death of Scottish woman
News.content:
The man suspected of killing a Scottish aid worker in Greece has appeared in court in Athens.

The body of Elisabeth Ross was found in a suitcase at an abandoned building on 18 July, days after she had been reported missing.

Sharif Ahmadzai, who is 26 and from Afghanistan, was told during the private court hearing that he faces charges of homicide with intent, robbery and weapons offences.

He made no comment and the case was deferred until Thursday, when it is expected that Ahmadzai will be formally charged.

Homicide with intent is equivalent to a murder charge in Scots law.

Ahmadzai was driven to court in a grey Hyundai i30 with blacked out windows for the hearing.

Multiple people were killed Wednesday morning in a mass shooting at a home in North Carolina, authorities said.

The Caswell County Sheriff’s Office responded to a call at a home located at 352 Brooks Road in Prospect Hill, a town about 28 miles north of Durham, just before 8 a.m., the North Carolina State Bureau of Investigation said.

Deputies found multiple people who had been shot in the home. One person was transported to Duke University Hospital with a gunshot wound, but there are multiple other fatalities, the agency said.

Authorities did not share any details about the victims, including their names, ages or how many people were killed. It was also unclear if authorities had identified a suspect or suspects in the shooting.

“SBI Crime scene investigators are on the scene processing evidence and conducting interviews,” North Carolina SBI said. “There is NO THREAT to the general public, and the event is contained to the above address.”

open image in gallery Multiple people were killed Wednesday in a mass shooting at a home in North Carolina, authorities said ( Google Maps )

The Caswell County Sheriff’s Office says it is working to notify the victims’ next of kin, the agency noted in a Facebook post.

Authorities did not say whether the people involved knew each other.

The sheriff’s office is the lead agency on the case. They are receiving assistance from the SBI, the North Carolina State Highway Patrol, the Prospect Hill Fire Department, Caswell County 911 and the Person County Sheriff’s Office.

“Additional information will be released as it becomes available through press releases and the SBI and Caswell County Sheriff's Office social media platforms,” SBI said.
