The Trump administration has detained dozens of parents and spouses of active-duty U.S. troops, an Associated Press investigation has revealed, as it rolls back immigration protections for military families in pursuit of its mass deportation agenda.

This marks a significant departure from decades of bipartisan consensus that shielded such individuals from deportation.

More than 50 parents and spouses of active-duty service members have been detained since Trump took office, with at least six already deported, according to the AP’s first accounting of these cases, which the government does not track.

Currently, at least eight immediate family members of U.S. service members remain in federal immigration custody.

Experts warn that this reversal could undermine military preparedness, even as the U.S. is engaged in conflict abroad.

The policy has left military personnel without crucial emotional support and caretakers for their children, delayed deployments, and forced some to take leave.

"How can I even focus on my military career because I have to worry about how my wife is doing?" said Army Sgt. Hedar Leonel Turcios Juarez, whose wife was detained in front of their 6-year-old daughter in July while he was stationed at Fort Bliss, Texas.

The Department of Homeland Security (DHS) states it does not compile data on these cases.

open image in gallery ‘How can I even focus on my military career because I have to worry about how my wife is doing?’ said Army Sgt. Hedar Leonel Turcios Juarez ( AP )

The AP obtained its information by analyzing thousands of federal court records, reviewing existing media coverage, and verifying details with family members and attorneys, suggesting the actual number of affected families is likely higher than the 51 cases identified.

While DHS did not provide specific information for most cases, it noted that at least seven individuals had been removed from the U.S. previously, at least eight had removal orders, and at least two had drunken driving or drug-related convictions.

"DHS and ICE value the contributions of all those who have served in the U.S. military," DHS said in a statement. "U.S. military service alone does not automatically grant lawful immigration status, or exempt aliens from the consequences of violating U.S. immigration laws."

open image in gallery Army Sgt. Hedar Leonel Turcios Juarez’s wife was detained in front of their 6-year-old ( Copyright 2026 The Associated Press. All rights reserved )

The Pentagon declined to comment on the AP’s findings.

Air Force Tech. Sgt. Wendy Gbeve, 30, described her anguish after her father, Luis Alberto Ramirez Zavala, was detained and deported to Mexico last month during a routine interview about his pending legal status application. "It’s the most frustrating, helpless feeling," Gbeve said.

Her father, who spent most of his life in the U.S. as a ranch hand, was removed quickly, leaving his wife of 30 years, a legal permanent resident, contemplating a return to Mexico.

This would leave Gbeve, whose husband is also in the Air Force, without their "entire safety net" for their two young children if both were deployed.

Army Staff Sgt. Alexis Jaramillo, an aviation operations specialist with over a decade of service, is now on administrative leave, caring for his 5-year-old stepson after his Brazilian wife, Maisa Lopes Eliaser, was detained in early July during what they believed was a routine appointment.

open image in gallery Army Staff Sgt. Alexis Jaramillo poses with a photo of his wife, Maisa Lopes Eliaser ( AP )

"It is really overwhelming because I need to take care of my kid by myself. No one is here to help me out," Jaramillo said. In another instance, an active-duty soldier halted an imminent deployment after her husband’s detention left no one to care for their then-5-year-old son.

A new policy, implemented in April 2025, explicitly states that "military service alone does not exempt aliens from the consequences of violating U.S. immigration laws."

Experts in military immigration law, including Dan Gividen, who served as ICE’s deputy chief counsel from 2016 to 2019 under Trump, describe this as a stark shift.

open image in gallery Army Staff Sgt. Alexis Jaramillo shows photos of his wife, Maisa Lopes Eliaser, a Brazilian national ( AP )

Gividen stated that during his tenure, immigration authorities rarely detained service members' immediate family members unless they had committed violent crimes.

"We would not place them into removal proceedings, period. That’s insane," Gividen said.

"The fact that they’re doing it now is just outrageous." Margaret Stock, an immigration attorney and retired lieutenant colonel, noted that previous administrations typically canceled past removal orders to ensure troops could focus on their duties. "If soldiers are preoccupied with detained or deported family, they're not concentrating on their job anymore," she explained.

Even some congressional Republicans, generally supportive of Trump’s immigration policies, have advocated for the release of service members' relatives. Florida Republican Rep. Maria Elvira Salazar stated, "The immigration system is failing the honorable and good Americans."

While DHS does not track data for active-duty troops, it has released figures for former service members.

From Jan. 20, 2025, through Jan. 26, 2026, immigration authorities detained 125 military veterans and arrested over 150 immediate family members. Anh Dung Cong Tran, whose father and son both served, was deported in July after living in the U.S. for decades.

His son, Antonio Tran, who enlisted at his father’s urging, said, "He has a totally different view on America now."

Military recruiters frequently tout immigration benefits, such as "military parole-in-place," as a selling point for enlistment.

This policy, implemented under Republican President George W. Bush and codified under Democratic President Barack Obama, allows spouses, children, and parents of service members and veterans to obtain legal immigration status from within the country.

However, under Trump, the average processing time for military parole-in-place has more than doubled to 12 months, leaving families more vulnerable to detention.

The AP found that immediate family members have repeatedly been detained by ICE while applying for parole-in-place or seeking to adjust their status, sometimes even during immigration appointments.

Marine Cpl. Jose Manuel Vilchis-Valle’s mother, Ursula Borja Valle, was detained at an appointment in August 2025 and deported to Mexico within a week, despite living in the U.S. since the 1990s without a known criminal record.

Vilchis-Valle, who was honorably discharged shortly after his mother’s deportation, said, "They basically told me that if you serve, and if you served honorably, you can help your parents." He added, "In a perfect world, I wished, because of my service, they could have pardoned her."

In June 2025, the Marine Corps officially stopped advertising enlistment as a way to protect immigrant family members.

However, Army and National Guard recruiters continue to promote these benefits. An Instagram post from an official Army recruiter in late July read, "For some service members, enlisting isn’t just about serving their country. It’s also about doing everything they can to help protect their parents who sacrificed everything for them."

For U.S. Army Specialist Romero Ralios, his father’s detention has led to remorse over his nine-month deployment last year to the Joint Task Force Southern Border, where he supported U.S. Customs and Border Patrol. His father, Sebastian Ralios Tino, a Guatemalan landscaper with no known criminal record, was detained this summer after living in the U.S. for nearly two decades without legal status. Ralios’ commanding officer, Capt. Mohamed Elmaola, emphasized the need to support soldiers and their families, stating, "It’s very hard to communicate and to have credibility as a leader when your own subordinates are unable to get support." Ralios now struggles with stress and regrets his involvement in immigration enforcement. "It was karma. I should’ve known," Ralios told the AP. "All those families I broke. I have regrets."

Celebrity blogger Perez Hilton has been rushed to hospital after his TikTok followers reported a concerning livestream.

Worried viewers reportedly saw Hilton, 48, self-harm in a video streamed on the social media app on Tuesday (2 August), following which emergency services swiftly arrived at his house in Miami.

He was “safely recovered” and transported by Miami-Dade Fire Rescue to a local hospital, where he is receiving medical attention.

open image in gallery Perez Hilton has been rushed to hospital after concerning TikTok followers ( Getty )

Without naming Hilton, the Miami-Dade sheriff’s office released a statement saying they received reports of a man “livestreaming acts of self-harm on social media”, and confirmed he was at home alone.

Addressing their handling of the situation, they said they had “tactically disengaged”, adding: “In many incidents involving a person experiencing a mental health crisis or actively harming themselves, deputies prioritise de-escalation by creating time, distance, and opportunities for communication.

“Unless there is an immediate threat to others, slowing the situation and utilising crisis intervention techniques can reduce the likelihood of a suicide-by-cop encounter and minimise the risk of injury to the individual, deputies and the public.”

The former Celebrity Big Brother contestant’s managers released a joint statement to TMZ, confirming they were “aware of the concerning content circulating online”.

Dante Rusciolelli and Rebekah Kochan said they had “not been able to make direct contact with him, despite our ongoing efforts to reach him”, and that their “primary concern” was Hilton’s health and well-being, “as well as the well-being of his family”.

open image in gallery In 2020, Perez Hilton expressed regret for the nature of his 2000s blog posts ( Getty )

They continued: “Until we have confirmed information, we will not speculate or comment further. We appreciate everyone’s concern and ask that his privacy be respected during this time.”

The Independent has contacted Hilton’s reps for additional comment.

Hilton – real name Mario Armando Lavandeira Jr – is known for his eponymous gossip blog, which, in the 2000s, caused controversy for its no-holds-barred posts as well as its practice of outing celebrities who were keeping their sexuality private.

He himself expressed regret for his actions in the book TMI: My Life in Scandal, which was published in 2020. “I regret that I thought it was OK to out celebrities,” Hilton wrote. “That is something I no longer believe.”

open image in gallery Perez Hilton was a contestant on 'Celebrity Big Brother' in 2015 ( Channel 5 )

Hilton has three children, born via surrogacy. He appeared on Celebrity Big Brother in 2015 and became the seventh housemate to be evicted, two days before the final.

If you are experiencing feelings of distress, or are struggling to cope, you can speak to the Samaritans, in confidence, on 116 123 (UK and ROI), email jo@samaritans.org, or visit the Samaritans website to find details of your nearest branch.

If you are based in the USA, and you or someone you know needs mental health assistance right now, call the National Suicide Prevention Helpline on 1-800-273-TALK (8255). This is a free, confidential crisis hotline that is available to everyone 24 hours a day, seven days a week.

If you are in another country, you can go to www.befrienders.org to find a helpline near you.

A former far-right activist, who has a string of convictions including for harassing a Jewish MP, has stood down as a Conservative candidate in upcoming local elections after major backlash.

Withdrawing from the race, Joshua Bonehill-Paine said he acknowledged that “my previous actions continue to cause pain in the Jewish community”.

But he hit out at other political parties, saying that if he did stand they would “spend all their time focusing on my past rather than the work I'm doing today, or even fighting antisemitism in their own midst”.

He revealed that Tory leader Kemi Badenoch, who had previously defended his selection, has offered him a role as an adviser on how to tackle the radicalisation of young men.

Labour peer Luciana Berger hit out Ms Badenoch on X, saying: “The decision to welcome this individual as an adviser to the Leader of the Opposition is no better than allowing him to stand as a council candidate.

“It is a privileged and influential national role. As a victim of this man's heinous crimes this appointment is an insult.”

open image in gallery Joshua Bonehill-Paine was jailed for racially aggravated harassment against Labour peer Luciana Berger ( Metropolitan Police )

Mr Bonehill-Paine said in a statement on X: “Rather than standing as a local council candidate, I believe that my experience is better used supporting Kemi Badenoch in her ongoing mission to combat the antisemitism and extremism that is dividing our nation.”

“I have therefore informed the party of my decision to withdraw from next year’s council election and Kemi has instead offered that I become an adviser to the Conservative Party’s Culture and Integration Commission, specifically focusing on how young men become radicalised.”

In response, Ms Badenoch said she was “sad” about his decision but “glad he is going to work with me and the party”.

But Reform UK said it “beggars belief” that he had been appointed as an adviser.

Earlier, Mr Bonehill-Paine said he was “tremendously proud” to have been selected to stand as a candidate for Crewkerne South in next year’s Somerset Council elections.

open image in gallery Conservative Party leader Kemi Badenoch defended his selection ( Reuters )

Mr Bonehill-Paine, who now runs a political satire account on social media posting AI videos, is a former neo-Nazi activist who has several convictions, including posting anti-Semitic material ahead of a planned neo-Nazi rally.

In 2016 he was found guilty of harassing former MP Luciana Berger in a string of anti-Jewish rants, posting articles online calling her a "dominatrix" and "an evil money-grabber" with a "deep-rooted hatred of men".

He was previously jailed for producing an advert for a neo-Nazi rally illustrated with a picture of Nazi concentration camp Auschwitz which promised “an absolute gas”.

Since then he has apologised for his past offending, and said he was now dedicated to “challenging the wave of hatred British Jews continue to face”.

Hours before he stood down, Jewish leaders rejected Ms Badenoch’s offer of a meeting with him, as she defended his selection as a council candidate.

In a joint statement, the Board of Deputies and the JLC said they had declined an invitation to meet Mr Bonehill-Paine, describing him as “a former neo-Nazi with criminal convictions for antisemitic hatred”.

open image in gallery Mr Bonehill-Paine was jailed in 2016 over antisemitic abuse of Lady Berger (Jonathan Brady/PA) ( PA )

They said: “The severity of Joshua Bonehill-Paine’s crimes targeting Luciana Berger and others mean that he still faces ongoing legal restrictions.

“Whilst we do believe in the possibility of rehabilitation, this should not in this case entail selection as a candidate for a major political party, and the impact of this decision on the victims ought to be a central consideration.”

Ms Badenoch defended his selection on Wednesday, saying she believed he had been rehabilitated.

She told BBC Radio 4’s Today programme: “I am extremely worried about antisemitism and what I feel is that if we can’t have the people who have previously been radicalised, who understand what went wrong and are part of the fight against antisemitism now. If we’re saying: ‘No, no, no, you’re untouchable,’ then how can we pretend that we believe in rehabilitation?”

But she suggested she would not allow him to stand for Parliament, and that as a councillor he would mainly be in charge of issues such as bins.

She said: “I’m not giving him a national platform, he is standing to be a councillor in Somerset… it is a local platform looking at parking, sorting out bins. I have much higher thresholds for what it takes to be a Conservative MP.”

Newcastle United have officially confirmed Matthias Jaissle as their new head coach. succeeding Eddie Howe.

The 38-year-old, who succeeds Eddie Howe, has already joined the squad at their La Manga pre-season training camp after his paperwork was finalised.

The club are understood to have paid the former Al-Ahli boss over £9 million in compensation to secure his services.

The former RB Salzburg boss said: “It is an incredible honour to become head coach of Newcastle United. This is one of the biggest clubs in European football, with a unique history, identity and supporter base, and I am excited to experience that passion and connection first-hand.

“When Newcastle United comes your way, you take notice. The ambition of the club, the vision for the future and the opportunity ahead made this an incredibly compelling place to be. I have followed the club’s journey closely in recent years and the progress that has been made is clear for everyone to see.”

Jaissle arrives at St James’ Park with a promising pedigree having guided Salzburg to back-to-back Austrian titles before heading for the Saudi Pro League in 2023 and winning successive Asian Champions League crowns with Al-Ahli.

Saudi Arabia’s Public Investment Fund, Newcastle’s majority owner, bought a controlling share in four Pro League clubs, including Al-Ahli, in 2023.

Newcastle chief executive David Hopkinson said: “Matthias is one of the most exciting and highly regarded young coaches in football and I’m thrilled to welcome him to Newcastle United.

“We have conducted a thorough process, and he has emerged as the clear candidate for the role. He possesses all the qualities we were looking for.”

Jaissle has big shoes to fill on Tyneside following Howe’s decision to step down from his role on Friday after almost five years in charge.

open image in gallery Jaissle replaces Eddie Howe in the Newcastle dugout ( Getty )

The former Bournemouth boss was handed the reins in November 2021 just weeks after Amanda Staveley’s consortium had completed its takeover, and aided by a significant cash injection he dragged the Magpies back from the brink of relegation from the Premier League.

In the process, he restored the connection between the fans and the club and created an optimism which was rewarded by a return to Champions League football and a first major domestic trophy in 70 years when they lifted the Carabao Cup in March 2025.

However, Howe departed after a difficult 2025-26 campaign, which was derailed before a ball had been kicked by Alexander Isak’s defection to Liverpool.

This summer’s departures of Kieran Trippier, Anthony Gordon and Sandro Tonali – and the reported likely exit of skipper Bruno Guimaraes to Arsenal – have left the squad in a state of flux.

Jaissle faces the task of steadying the ship off the pitch before Newcastle open the new campaign at home to Liverpool on August 23.

He added: “I am incredibly excited about the future. I fully and unreservedly believe in this project, the ambition and the direction the club is taking.

“There is a clear vision, strong leadership and an exceptional platform to build on.”

Volodymyr Zelensky has pleaded with Ukraine’s allies to send more missile defences after a major Russian air attack on Kyiv killed at least 17.

“Ballistic interceptors are what could have saved the lives of those killed today,” the Ukrainian president said on social media, adding that Kyiv has been supplied with just a third of the air defence missiles in 2026 compared to a year earlier.

“It is very important for our partners to understand that delays in supplying them, or a reluctance to hand over anti-ballistic systems, lead directly to such horrific casualties and destruction.”

open image in gallery Kyiv was once again bombarded by Russian missiles ( AP )

Some 44 others were wounded as Russia pummelled Ukraine’s capital region with ballistic missiles and drones in one of the deadliest attacks this year, officials said.

Russia’s attack came after Ukraine targeted the logistics hub of leading online retailer Wildberries and large warehouse fires burned in the city of Brovary and the villages of Velyka Dymerka, Kvitneve and Peremoha.

The overnight barrage on Kyiv, which lasted about two hours, was the latest in a series of large-scale Russian missile strikes that have become increasingly common this summer. Moscow is exploiting Ukraine’s critical shortage of interceptors for the US-made Patriot systems, the sole air defence weapon capable of shooting down ballistic missiles.

If the US does not send more Patriots, Mr Zelensky said he wants the ability to make Patriot ammunition in Ukraine or win permission from Elon Musk to use his Starlink satellite communications system to guide strikes inside Russia to hit missile launchers.

open image in gallery At least 17 people were killed in the latest attacks ( AFP/Getty )

The US is pressing ahead with talks on allowing Ukraine to make Patriot missiles, sources told Reuters news agency, even after Donald Trump cast doubt on such a deal, four sources familiar with the discussions said.

The discussions include an option for Ukraine to build some components for final assembly elsewhere in Europe, the sources added.

It’s unclear how many interceptors Ukraine has left. Mr Zelensky said after a Russian aerial attack last Friday that air defences shot down only one ballistic missile “solely because there are no missiles for the Patriots”.

The targets hit in the latest barrage included a brewery, a warehouse for construction material, and a mail sorting office that had nothing to do with the war, Mr Zelensky said. But Russia’s defense ministry claimed the businesses had military ties.

open image in gallery Another 42 people were injured by Russia’s attacks on the capital ( AP )

Thursday has been declared an official day of mourning for the 17 people killed, said Tymur Tkachenko, head of Kyiv’s regional military administration.

With US-led peace efforts apparently stalled, Ukraine has stepped up its deep strikes on key Russian targets such as oil refineries to try to compel Vladimir Putin to negotiate. Mr Zelensky has accepted an unconditional ceasefire demanded by Trump but Putin has refused.

Ukraine has struck more than a dozen Wildberries facilities in under three weeks, saying the company provides goods that can be used by the military. Kyiv is also keen to unsettle the Russian public with high-profile attacks. A strike on a Russian-occupied Crimean beach over the weekend killed seven.

In response, the Russian Defense Ministry said its forces downed 475 Ukrainian drones overnight over 16 Russian regions, as well as in Crimea and the waters of the Sea of Azov and the Black Sea.

It said it struck transport, logistics and distribution centres involved in war-related activity, four of which were in Kyiv.

“The enemy is attacking everything indiscriminately – retail warehouses, food storage facilities, logistics hubs, enterprises, building materials warehouses,” Mr Zelensky adviser Serhii Beskrestnov, said on Facebook.

It was not immediately possible to independently reconcile the different Russian and Ukrainian accounts of the military value of the targets.

open image in gallery A general view of a shopping centre damaged by Russian strikes in the Lukianivska district of Kyiv ( PA )

Kyiv warehouse worker Mykhailo Hukov said an air raid warning that included a ballistic missile threat sounded just after midnight.

“So everyone started running,” he said. “I turned everyone around so they wouldn't go back inside for their backpacks.”

In an underground shelter minutes later, they heard “very loud explosions”.

Ukraine’s largest private postal operator, Nova Poshta, said a Russian cluster munition destroyed one of its sorting centres in Kyiv.

The Russian defense ministry claimed the centre was “storing and distributing dual-use goods, including those used in the production of long- and medium-range uncrewed aerial vehicles, as well as robotic systems and electronic warfare systems.” It claimed that two other logistics centers in the Kyiv region stored drones or components for drones.

Separately, Russia said its forces hit three bulk carriers on the Black Sea south of Odesa that it claimed were transporting Ukrainian weapons and military equipment. Ukrainian officials didn’t comment on the claims.

News.title: Hotel made famous by The Shining movie at risk of burning down in Oregon wildfire
News.content:

The Oregon hotel made famous by The Shining may be at risk of burning down as one of dozens of wildfires in the state pushes toward the iconic lodge.

The Grasshopper Fire burned over 36,600 acres in Mount Hood National Forest and was only 19 percent contained as of Wednesday morning, edging closer and closer to the Timberline Lodge.

The hotel’s exterior became famous after it was used as the haunted Overlook Hotel in Stanley Kubrick’s beloved film, and is backdropped by Mount Hood’s snow-covered peaks.

While the legendary lodge is currently under a Level 1 “Be Ready” evacuation notice, the Grasshopper Fire continues to push west toward Mount Hood, leaving locals concerned they may eventually have to evacuate, KATU 2 reported.

The encroaching blaze has left Mt Hood Meadows, a ski resort slightly east of the Timberline Lodge, under a Level 3 “Go Now” evacuation order, prompting skiers to evacuate Tuesday morning as firefighters work to protect the resort.

open image in gallery The Timberline Lodge, known from The Shining, is located near one of the wildfires burning in Oregon ( Kkmd/CC BY-SA 3.0 )

The Timberline Lodge said that it will close the hotel if evacuation levels increase to a Level 2.

“Right now, people shouldn’t be traveling around the mountain unless it’s absolutely necessary,” said John Burton, the lodge’s director of marketing and public affairs. “There’s a Level 1 notice on our side of the mountain and a Level 3, which is a mandatory evacuation, around the corner on the other side of the mountain.”

While the lodge is still open, Burton said that the declining air quality due to the fire has driven many visitors away.

“It’s obviously tough on business,” Burton said. “It’s tough on guests. It’s tough on employees when the conditions just aren’t good, when it isn’t comfortable to breathe.”

The fire creeping closer toward Timberline Lodge has even left some longtime employees concerned about the threat.

open image in gallery A wildfire called the Bench Fire burns above Pelton Reservoir in Jefferson County, Oregon. Dozens of wildfires are currently burning across the state ( AP )

“It’s definitely scary,” Emma Hall told KATU 2. “Especially all the memories we’ve built up here. A lot of skiers and snowboarders have come up here for the longest time. It’s an epicenter. If anything were to happen, it’d be pretty sad, especially with Meadows being so close.”

The Grasshopper Fire began July 23 following multiple lightning storms over the forest in the weeks before, and spread quickly east and north due to winds and hot and dry conditions, officials said.

As of Wednesday, more than 1,300 personnel were responding to the blaze, which destroyed a century-old fire lookout tower in Mount Hood National Forest on Friday, according to The Oregonian.

Firefighters made significant efforts to save the Flag Point Lookout, the first fire lookout in the area, before fire conditions became too dangerous on Friday, forcing crews to abandon their protection efforts.

However, the Grasshopper Fire is just one of 32 fires currently burning across Oregon, according to KATU 2.

As of Monday morning, those fires accounted for 1,812,575 of the 2,014,481 acres that have burned in the state so far this year.

News.title: Ebola outbreak outpacing containment effort, WHO chief warns
News.content:
Caused by the rare Bundibugyo strain of Ebola, for which there are no vaccines or treatments, it has been extremely difficult to contain, according to experts on the ground.

“The outbreak is spreading faster than our scale-up of the response, with new cases doubling in some hotspots over the past week alone,” Dr Tedros said on X.

Part of the difficulty is that the virus was circulating undetected for weeks before the outbreak was formally declared in mid-May, leaving health officials even now racing to catch up with the spread.

Prof Placide Mbala, director of research, clinical trials and innovation at Africa CDC, told the Telegraph: “It’s mostly the fact we arrived a bit late. It took us some time before we detected this virus outbreak. And when we detected the outbreak, we already had a total of I can say more than 200 suspected cases. It’s been difficult to catch up. That’s where we are.”

While the DRC has a wealth of experience in tackling haemorrhagic fever outbreaks, the effects of that initial delay are still being felt.

Prof Mbala said: “We have some experience dealing with the cases, the labs, the communication, the infection prevention and control.

“We have some experience... But my observation is that we were very slow, and it’s why we’re in this situation.

“We are slow detecting the people, slow responding, we are slow deploying people, we are slow to recruit the community healthcare workers to improve contact tracing, we are slow to deploy the safe burials.”

DRC’s largest outbreak had previously been from 2018 to 2020, when 3,481 cases were recorded.

The West Africa outbreak recorded 28,616 cases and 11,310 deaths according to the WHO.

Prof Mbala said insecurity was also severely hampering attempts to curb the virus. The outbreak epicentre is in Ituri province, which has been wracked by ethnic strife for decades and is also home to militias competing to control mining.

He said: “There are many, many mining groups controlling most of the mining places. We have a big issue with those places, because they are places where the response team cannot go.”

Medics and aid workers have also been undermined by violent public distrust of their efforts.

Locals in the area have either doubted the existence of the virus, or have accused health teams of deliberately spreading the infection, or somehow benefiting from it.

More than a dozen health facilities have been set alight and several health workers have been killed.

Prof Mbala said: “The local people, they also sometimes are very upset, because they believe that it’s a kind of a business, and people who are coming here, they are getting a lot of money, [so] don’t want this disease to stop.”

He said he hoped that immunity was starting to rise in some areas and this would start to curb transmission.

However there was also a risk that people fleeing the outbreak would spread the virus further afield.

He said: “The second scenario is the fact we are seeing people moving from the affected area to new areas, to run away from the response team because they do not want to go to the treatment centre.

“And in complicity with their family members living in other areas, they are now the ones who are spreading the disease to new areas

“So we’ll see new places affected because people are moving around from the affected zone to the non-affected zone.”

News.title: Mykhailo Mudryk returns as Chelsea slip to Juventus defeat
News.content:
Chelsea 0 Juventus 1

Mykhailo Mudryk made his first Chelsea appearance since November 2024 as Xabi Alonso’s team succumbed to their second pre-season defeat.

Mudryk replaced Nicolas Jackson in the 82nd minute against Juventus, marking his return to competitive football after a long doping ban that was resolved this week thanks to changes in Wada regulations.

There were a couple of crosses delivered from the left flank by the Ukrainian winger, who could yet leave Chelsea on loan or on a permanent basis before the close of the transfer window.

Juventus were the victors though, thanks to a sumptuous 68th-minute goal by Kosovo winger Edon Zhegrova.

Alonso had 21 players on his bench, and made 12 second-half substitutions.

Levi Colwill and Cole Palmer featured in the defeat by 10-man Spurs on Saturday, but sat this game out as they continue to build fitness. Danny Welbeck did start though, reunited with former Brighton team-mate Joao Pedro up top.

Chelsea scored just one goal against Spurs and Juventus, but the thrust provided by right-back Marco Palestra in tandem with first Geovany Quenda and then Estevao was a bright spot for Alonso.

Chelsea continue their pre-season against AC Milan on Saturday, before they host Real Sociedad at Stamford Bridge on August 15.

They begin their Premier League campaign at Fulham in the Monday night slot on the opening weekend.

News.title: The underground lab where ‘princess mosquitoes’ are treated like royalty
News.content:
Beneath the grand Art Deco headquarters of the London School of Hygiene and Tropical Medicine lies a vast labyrinth inhabited by weird and wonderful creatures.

In this maze of subterranean labs, store rooms and corridors live colonies of disease-bearing insects and arachnids from all over the world, from bed bugs, sand flies and microscopic dust mites to the so-called kissing bugs that spread Chagas disease – a sinister condition that can cause its victims to drop dead of heart failure without warning, albeit decades after the first (silent) infection.

Behind a series of doors, contained in stacks of mesh boxes, you can even find the flies that spread trachoma, the Dickensian eye disease that is still a leading cause of blindness around the world. But be warned: entering the room is not for the faint of heart – the flies feed on human excrement and the smell is impossible to forget.

There are also many varieties of mosquito, including several species of the Anopheles genus that spread malaria, Culex and Aedes mosquitoes that are also vectors for human and animal diseases, and even Toxorhynchites, perhaps better known as the elephant mosquito, a friendly giant which doesn’t bite people but preys on other mosquitoes.

These animals have been studied intensely since the insectaries were established in the building’s vaults in the 1960s, underpinning many breakthroughs in the control, surveillance, and understanding of vector-borne diseases in the developing world.

LSHTM researchers are now looking closer to home. They have established the UK’s first laboratory colony of Aedes vexans mosquitoes, a species native to the British isles, to study whether they could harbour diseases like West Nile virus, Rift Valley fever, Zika or Japanese encephalitis.

News.title: What I saw in a week on the front line of Afghanistan’s hunger crisis
News.content:
May 15 and 16, 2026

It is the weekend, a small moment to rest, although there is still a lot of work waiting for me. A week in the field does not mean that work in Kabul stops. I try to catch up on my emails and have a planned online interview for an international staff position – since in Europe, Friday is a normal working day. I also review parts of new proposals for donors and our financial planning.

On Saturday, however, I take a short break. Together with the base management team in Helmand, we visit a historical site called Qala-e-Bost, believed to have been built around 3,000 years ago. It is a rare moment to step away from work, followed by lunch with the team.

May 17, 2026

Sunday morning, the first working day of the week, we visit Basrhan Sub Health Centre, run by one of our local partners. As a nurse and former nurse trainer, I feel very much in my element in these health centres. It allows me to engage easily with the team and discuss their work.

I speak with the outreach officer and the vaccinator. They explain that this facility supports 18 outreach locations, each visited at least once a month. They provide vaccinations, raise awareness, and connect communities to the health centre. These visits often take place in simple settings, like mosques.

Immunisation is now well accepted. In the beginning, there was some resistance, but trust has grown over time. Every child is tracked, and if a child misses a vaccination, community health volunteers follow up at home. For extra polio vaccinations, this is carefully recorded by marking a finger of the child – helping ensure that no child is missed. The goal is clear: a polio-free Afghanistan.

I also speak with a mother. She is wearing a burka, so I cannot see her face. She tells me she is 22 years old and holds her 12-month-old son on her lap. She came because he has a fever, but I see a healthy child – something that stands out after my time in the TFU.

She brings her child regularly for follow-up and growth monitoring and the child has never been in a treatment program for malnutrition. She speaks positively about the services. “We are lucky,” she says. “The staff treat us well, and we have access to care in our community.”

News.title: World’s first seahorse hospital fights to protect them from extinction
News.content:
With careful precision, marine biologist Linda Albonetti extracts a 10cm-long injured seahorse – a heavily pregnant male – from an aquarium tank to apply healing ointment to its wound.

Linda, 29, coordinator at the world’s first specialist seahorse hospital, is currently caring for around 50 of these tiny creatures, all of which were brought in by local fishing crews after becoming snagged in their nets.

The seahorse will be kept for a few more days before it is released back into the Adriatic Sea, giving it time to recover from the cut to the soft, bony plates that form its outer carapace.

What the team here are doing is a literal drop in the ocean, a small attempt to fight back against the potential extinction of these remarkable fish.

In Europe and around countries like Indonesia, they are being poached in their millions for sale to a voracious Asian traditional medicine market where they are consumed as an aphrodisiac and alleged cure for impotence, asthma and kidney problems.

“There is definitely a downward trend in the overall seahorse population because they are being collected for the Asian market,” says Linda. “Technically, they cannot be exported to countries such as China, but there is no specific law preventing that trade. They do not have the same protections as sea turtles, for example.

“It is not happening in this part of Italy yet, but it is further south, off the Mediterranean coast. That is why it is so important that we monitor their numbers and maintain a good relationship with the local fishermen.”

News.title: The 13 best castle hotels in England
News.content:
Few places capture the imagination quite like a castle, and England is home to some of the most remarkable places to spend the night. If it’s not the romance of waking up in a canopied four-poster bed, or losing ourselves in centuries-old tapestries and visceral oil paintings, we are lured by tales of brave knights and plotting dignitaries, duplicitous royals and ghosts parleying secrets in the hallways.

Part of the magic is spending an afternoon wandering grounds and gardens followed by evenings in front of a roaring fire, or dining in a banquet hall that may have hosted medieval kings and queens. While not every castle has crenellated battlements, glistening moats or royal connections, each stony stronghold on our list has something special that makes it worth travelling for. In this modern age that might include a spa, fine-dining restaurant or extra touches like free admission to exhibitions and museum tours. Here’s our pick of the best castle hotels in England.

News.title: Careless Liverpool concede same goal twice in second-half capitulation against Leeds
News.content:
Soldier Field in Chicago hosts an all-Premier League tie encounter as Liverpool take on Leeds as both sides bring their US tours to a close. Both Premier League encounters between these sides last season ended in draws; a 3-3 draw at Elland Road was followed up by a 0-0 stalemate at Anfield. The draw at Elland Road was immediately followed by Mohamed Salah speaking to the media, claiming he had been thrown under the bus.

It is a new era at Liverpool as former Bournemouth boss Andoni Iraola has replaced Arne Slot at Anfield. They kicked off the Iraola era in Nashville, Tennessee, with a 4-2 win over Sunderland, following that up with another victory in New York on Wednesday night, beating Wrexham 1-0, and will be aiming to make it three wins from three on their US tour.

“I think it [the US tour] has been really, really useful,” Iraola said in an interview on the official Liverpool website. Obviously, you spend a lot of time with the players, with the staff, you get all the information you can. And I think there is also an evolution, it has to be. We start to understand each other better, what we need to do. Every game, I hope we can get closer and closer and put ourselves in a position where the few players that still are not here start to train also, they are helped by the others.”

Virgil van Dijk and Cody Gakpo resumed training back on Merseyside whilst Alexis Mac Allister, Alisson and Victor Munoz are yet to return to training following their World Cup exploits. The trio of Florian Wirtz, Alexander Isak and Ryan Gravenberch are all set to feature for the first time this pre-season.

Leeds’ pre-season campaign began with a 3-2 loss to Championship Wrexham in Tampa, Florida before beating Sunderland 1-0 in New Jersey courtesy of a long-range strike from Lukas Nmecha. Former Liverpool man Harry Wilson joined Leeds on a free from Fulham this summer.

“Really tough but that is expected,” Wilson said. That is what pre-season is for, building up a base for when the season starts, making sure you are in the best physical position you can be to attack the season. It has been good. I played against them [Leeds] twice last year when I was at Fulham. Both games were really, really tough games.

“I think when the fans have got a good team to support, I think that [the atmosphere at Elland Road] goes up a notch. I think the size of the club was a massive part of me coming. Then speaking to the guys, the chairman, the sporting director, and seeing kind of the plans and the aims for the club, it is something I wanted to be a part of.”

Team news to follow shortly.

News.title: Oil plummets as Trump calls off Iran strikes
News.content:
Oil prices have plunged after Donald Trump called off strikes and said the US and Iran would hold further peace talks.

Brent crude, the international benchmark, sank as much as 9.5pc early on Monday to less than $82 a barrel after the US president said he had halted plans for “disastrous” strikes.

Mr Trump said: “Obviously, they don’t want to be attacked. They knew the extent of the attack because they saw it forming.

“Now what we’re doing is we’re talking to them in the form of a negotiation. It begins tomorrow afternoon.”

Mr ‌Trump also ordered oil companies to lower petrol prices for American ‌consumers ‌and criticised ⁠Chevron’s chief executive for not crediting his administration for supporting the fossil fuel industry.

The president said that he had been asked by Iran as well as US partners Saudi Arabia, the United Arab Emirates and Qatar to hold off on strikes. He halted plans for a major attack against Iran on Saturday, which he said would have been the biggest since the Second World War.

Mr Trump claimed the sides were on the “perimeter” of a peace deal.

Oil’s sharp fall also sent the cost of government borrowing lower on Monday over hopes that it would ease inflation.

The yield on 10-year UK gilts, a benchmark for what the Treasury pays to borrow money, dropped from 5.05pc to 4.98pc, while the equivalent US bonds dropped from 4.74pc to 4.69pc.

Stock markets in Europe also rose, with the FTSE 100 up 0.2pc, the Cac 40 in Paris up 0.3pc and the Dax in Frankfurt climbing 0.1pc.

Sports.title: Arsenal vs Real Betis DELAYED after Spanish side caught in Dublin traffic
Sports.content:
ARSENAL’S pre-season clash with Real Betis was unbelievably delayed by 15 minutes due to traffic.

Spanish club Betis had their team bus stuck in congestion on the way to the Aviva Stadium, causing kick-off to be delayed from 7:30pm to 7:45pm.

Betis arrived at the stadium less than an hour before they were due to kick off and needed the kick-off to be adjusted to allow for their preparations.



Manuel Pellegrini’s side, who earned Champions League qualification last season, presents Arsenal’s toughest task of their pre-season so far.



The Gunners breezed past second-tier Spanish outfit Girona 4-1 on Saturday, thanks to goals from Kai Havertz, Max Dowman, Gabriel Jesus and new arrival Christos Tzolis.

Mikel Arteta’s squad also won 3-0 last month in a behind-closed-doors friendly against MK Dons.

Arteta has opted for an unchanged XI from the team that beat Girona at the weekend.

Arsenal are unchanged from the XI that started their 4-1 win over Girona on Saturday night.

The only change involves two additions to the bench. Brazilian duo Gabriel Magalhaes and Gabriel Martinelli are available after returning to training late last week.

Last time out the Gunners’ boss withdrew all of his World Cup returnees after just half an hour, but the likes of Piero Hincapie, Kai Havertz and Viktor Gyokeres are expected to get more minutes this evening.

There’s also another chance for Dowman to shine after his impressive goal and assist in Spain at the weekend.

Sports.title: Arsenal dealt huge transfer blow as Real Madrid ‘offer Vinicius Jr MORE money in bid to snub Gunners and sign contract’
Sports.content:
ARSENAL have been dealt a major transfer blow by Real Madrid reportedly offering Vinicius Junior more money and a new contract.

The Gunners are chasing a major deal to land the Brazilian winger, who is into the final year of his current contract at the Bernabeu.



But now The Athletic report Real have made a swoop to cling on to Vinicius.

It is said they have made a serious offer to reflect his importance to the team.



However, it remains unclear if it matches the £25million annual packet – including base salary, add-ons and a renewal bonus – Vinicius was after earlier in the year.

The Brazil international, 26, had his representatives meet with Real Madrid’s hierachy on Wednesday – including general director Jose Angel Sanchez and chief scout Juni Calafat.



Previously, the two parties’ financial expectations have been way off – negotiations have been going on since January 2025 – especially over the renewal bonus.

But it is claimed Wednesday’s talks progressed and Real have upped their offer after their previous offer of around £360,000 per week was allegedly turned down as he seeks to be paid a similar amount to £500,000-a-week Kylian Mbappe.

However, with another contract seemingly on the table, Vinicius must now decide whether he will sign the contract extension, reject it and somehow eek out even more cash, leave for Arsenal or run his current deal down until next summer.

Los Blancos, though, are desperate to avoid the latter option as that would see the superstar walk away for nothing in 2027.



BEST ONLINE CASINOS – TOP SITES IN THE UK

Arsenal’s top brass, meanwhile, have given the green light for their negotiators to try and secure Vinicius’ services.

Reports earlier before the latest development suggested the 54-cap Brazil man is closer to a transfer than a contract renewal.

And many Arsenal players are said to believe Vinicius will sign for the club this summer.

Spanish outlet Diario claim Emirates sporting director Andrea Berta has informed some squad members that they are indeed securing the transfer.



Vinicius spoke publicly for the first time this week since the speculation became public – but insists he is focused on pre-season under new boss Jose Mourinho.

The forward – who has 128 goals in 376 games for Real Madrid across eight seasons – said: “Very well, getting to know the new manager, the new players and working really hard in training.

“He wants me to be just as I’ve always been – happy, positive and playing my own style of football.”

Sports.title: ‘Life can be cruel’ – EFL manager and colleague of Mark Hughes’ son close to tears as he opens up on his sudden death
Sports.content:
THE head coach of Grimsby Town revealed his heartbreak following the tragic loss of Alex Hughes, the son of Man Utd legend Mark.

David Artell, 45, spoke publicly for the first time following the death of Alex, who worked in player recruitment for the League Two club.



The boss pulled back the curtain on the shockwaves that had passed through players and staff in Lincolnshire.

Welling up, Artell spoke to BBC Humberside, saying: “He was a lovely guy, top guy. He was good at his job, very humble.



“In those kind of roles, (people) tend to have a high opinion of themselves, rightly or wrongly.

“I’m not saying that for every kind of head of recruitment, but they tend to really back their own judgement.



“He was really happy to listen to everyone in the room.

“Life can be really cruel. He’s a good guy.”

Alex, who died aged 38, was a former football agent and player who joined the Mariners last year.

In June, the club called his passing “sudden and unexpected”.



BEST FREE BETS AND BETTING SIGN UP OFFERS

But when asked how Artell was coping, he said: “It’s not easy. You have to pull your big boy pants on and get on with it.

“You have to understand that whatever I’m feeling, the family’s going through it 1000 times worse.

“I still miss him, obviously. It’s just sad. Really sad.”

Hundreds turned out for his Prestbury funeral in July, with huge names like Sir Alex Ferguson, Bryan Robson and Ryan Giggs arriving to pay their respects.



An inquest heard that Alex tragically died from sudden adult death syndrome.

The report told how Alex died after collapsing on the floor of his bedroom in his home and was found by his two sons on June 19 at around 7am.

The Cheshire Coroner’s Court inquest was told that the condition usually occurs in young men – with four key signs – and there are around 800 cases per year in England.

Area coroner Victoria Davies concluded that the death was down to natural causes.

Sports.title: Popular ex-Arsenal star Takehiro Tomiyasu, 27, on brink of transfer back to Premier League a year after Gunners exit
Sports.content:
FORMER Arsenal defender Takehiro Tomiyasu is on the brink of a sensational return to the Premier League with Crystal Palace.

The 27-year-old Japanese international is expected to have his medical in London and is expected to sign his contract within the next 48 hours after agreeing to join the Eagles as a free agent.



Tomiyasu is set to return to England just a year after bringing the curtain down on his spell with Arsenal.

Following his departure from the Gunners, the defender signed for Ajax in the hope of getting his career back on track.



But his time in Amsterdam was derailed by injury problems, restricting him to just seven league appearances before he left the Dutch club this summer.

Since becoming a free agent, Tomiyasu has been looking for the right opportunity to relaunch his career.

Crystal Palace offered him the chance to prove his fitness after inviting him to train with the squad on trial.

The experienced defender is understood to have impressed manager Pierre Sage during that spell.

His displays convinced Palace to press ahead with a deal, with the South London club now set to complete the signing.

Tomiyasu’s versatility is expected to be a major asset, with the Japan international capable of operating at right-back, left-back and centre-half.



SUN VEGAS WELCOME OFFER: GET UP TO £100 BONUS

He enjoyed four seasons at Arsenal after arriving from Bologna in 2021 and quickly became a popular figure among supporters thanks to his consistency and ability to fill a number of defensive roles.

However, recurring injuries hampered his progress in North London and ultimately limited his appearances during the latter stages of his Arsenal career.

Now Tomiyasu has the chance to make a fresh start in the Premier League, with Palace hoping his experience and quality can strengthen their defensive options ahead of the new season.

The move represents another significant addition for Pierre Sage as he continues shaping his squad, with Tomiyasu expected to complete the remaining paperwork once his contract is signed over the next 48 hours.



An official announcement is expected from Crystal Palace once the formalities have been completed.

Sports.title: ‘Sure that’s not Messi’ – Man Utd fans in meltdown as academy kid leaves team-mates on the floor with ludicrous goal
Sports.content:
MANCHESTER UNITED fans have likened an academy player to Lionel Messi after watching his stunning solo goal.

Jay McEvoy, 17, twisted and danced through several diving bodies before slotting a goal home in recent training footage.



Gathering the ball in a tight space, McEvoy lured in his team-mates and slipped between five of them to create a window to shoot.

Mimicking a Cruyff turn, the youngster sold three feints and slipped the ball cleanly past two sliding defenders.



And it was even more impressive that McEvoy is a deep lying midfielder by trade.

It left United fans excited about what’s to come, with one writing: “Wow. Are you sure that’s not Messi?”



Another said: “That was nasty!”

McEvoy played for Darren Fletcher‘s Under-18s last season and is set to step up to the Under-21s under Adam Lawrence this term.

While United are considering loans for most of their Under-21 stars, a loan for McEvoy appears unlikely at this stage.

He played a huge role on Fletcher’s side’s quest to two major finals and the league battle with City, when United finished runners up.



BEST ONLINE CASINOS – TOP SITES IN THE UK

But McEvoy dropped out of the squad for the Youth Cup final against City as Amir Ibragimov returned from injury.

He did feature in the U18 Premier League Cup final, scoring his penalty in the shootout before United were beaten by Crystal Palace.

An aggressive midfielder who loves to win tackles and is excellent on both feet, McEvoy showed his quality with two goals against Liverpool U18s in April.

The midfielder has represented Northern Ireland and Republic of Ireland in youth international fixtures.

Sports.title: Arsenal vs Real Betis live stream: How to watch as Gunners continue pre-season in Dublin
Sports.content:
ARSENAL continue their pre-season prep against Spanish side Real Betis in Dublin.

The Gunners make a short trip across to Ireland to clash LaLiga side Betis, as they continue to prepare to defend the Premier League title.



ARSENAL VS REAL BETIS LIVE

Sports.title: Premier League legend Martin O’Neill, 74, in hospital as Celtic issue health update on boss after medical procedure
Sports.content:
MARTIN O’NEILL is in hospital, Celtic confirmed.

The Hoops boss, 74, needed to have a minor surgery.



And his club put out a statement to reassure fans and show their appreciation to supporters for their messages.

Celtic posted on X on Wednesday afternoon: “In response to speculation, we can confirm that Martin O’Neill has undergone a small procedure in hospital.



“We would envisage Martin being released from hospital in the next day or two and on behalf of Martin, we would like to thank supporters for their kind wishes.

“We would ask that the privacy of Martin and his family is respected.”



Fans flooded the replies with further best wishes.

One said: “Get well soon legend.”

Another wrote: “God bless him and hopefully he’s okay.”

A third added: “Get well soon Martin, love and prayers to you and your family.”



And a final user commented: “Wishing the boss a speedy recovery.”

Celtic drew with Shelbourne, Middlesbrough and AC Milan and lost to Sporting in pre-season, then kicked off the new Scottish Premiership campaign on Monday with a 1-0 win over Dundee.

The champions have only brought in Camilo Duran and Kasper Hogh so far in the summer transfer window.

O’Neill first managed Celtic from 2000 to 2005 after five successful years at Leicester City.

He then took charge of Aston Villa, Sunderland, Ireland and Nottingham Forest before returning to Celtic Park after six years away from the dugout in an interim role last October.



He departed when Wilfried Nancy was appointed in the December – but he lasted just 33 days.

And O’Neill returned in January and spearheaded a domestic double before getting the job permanently in June on a one-year contract.

Sports.content:
Arsenal 'prepare second offer' for England star as Morgan Rogers deal causes complication

Arsenal are looking to formalise their pursuit of a third marquee signing of the summer window in addition to Bruno Guimaraes and Vinicius Jr

View 2 Images Ezri Konsa is still wanted by Arsenal but a Morgan Rogers transfer problem could be repeated (Image: (Photo by Eddie Keogh - The FA/The FA via Getty Images))

Aston Villa are expecting Arsenal to submit a second offer for Ezri Konsa after an opening bid fell short of their £60million valuation. Sporting director Andrea Berta is believed to be looking at potential defensive signings due to William Saliba's back injury that is expected to keep him out for several months.

‌



Konsa emerged as an option for Arsenal in July following a strong season at Villa Park. During the World Cup, a 'low-ball offer' was lodged to Villa and was quickly turned down with it said to have left a sour taste.

‌



His former team-mate Morgan Rogers was of firm interest to the Gunners before he completed a staggering £117m move to Chelsea. The bid for Konsa did not help Arsenal's chances of signing Rogers, and could yet impact Mikel Arteta's side in any deal for the English defender.

How Arsenal could line up after signing Bruno Guimaraes and completing Vinicius Jr transfer READ MORE :

Arsenal, however, are unlikely to give up hope of signing him as per the Daily Mail, who have also claimed that Villa are bracing for a fresh proposal from north London.

Following their first bid, Konsa is said to have remained on Arsenal's radar while Villa are hoping for him to sign a new contract, with his current deal expiring in the summer of 2028.

‌



Having acquired over £150m from selling Rogers and Youri Tielemans, Villa are not under financial pressure to sell. Those key departures also will seemingly harden Unai Emery's stance on Konsa, with an exit unlikely to be sanctioned unless a deal for a suitable replacement is lined up.

His fellow Brazilian Vinicius Jr is also being targeted with his Real Madrid future remaining uncertain as he has just 12 months remaining on his current deal.

Completing both of those transfers is seemingly Arsenal's priority this summer, with a pursuit of Konsa expected to be formalised after that - despite the difficulties in getting a deal done for the England defender.

Sports.title: Celtic manager Martin O'Neill in hospital as club issue health update
Sports.content:
Celtic manager Martin O'Neill in hospital as club issue health update

Martin O'Neill was in the dugout for Celtic's 1-0 win at home to Dundee on Monday to begin their Scottish Premiership title defence, but the manager is now in hospital

View Image Martin O'Neill has undergone a 'small procedure' (Image: Ian MacNicol/Getty Images)

Celtic manager Martin O'Neill is in hospital after undergoing a 'small procedure', the club have confirmed. Celtic said in a statement that O'Neill, 74, is expected to be discharged within the 'next day or two'.

‌



There are no details about the Northern Irishman's procedure. O'Neill was in the dugout as Celtic began their Scottish Premiership title defence at home to Dundee on Monday, winning 1-0.

‌



After two interim spells last season, the former Aston Villa boss signed a one-year contract plus the option of a further 12 months to become Celtic's permanent manager in June. Previously, O'Neill hadn't managed since 2019.

‌



Celtic announced on Wednesday afternoon: "In response to speculation, we can confirm that Martin O'Neill has undergone a small procedure in hospital," the Scottish champions posted on social media.

JOIN US ON FACEBOOK! All the best sports news and much more on our dedicated Facebook page

‌



Inside the murky world of FIFA lobbying as Jamie Carragher reveals World Cup request READ MORE :

"We would envisage Martin being released from hospital in the next day or two and on behalf of Martin, we would like to thank supporters for their kind wishes. We would ask that the privacy of Martin and his family is respected."

O'Neill led Celtic to a memorable Scottish league and cup double last season. His first spell came after the shock departure of Brendan Rodgers in October.

He then returned to Parkhead in January, with Wilfried Nancy having been sacked after just eight games. After talks with Celtic's major shareholder, Dermot Desmond, O'Neill decided to stay on for this season.

‌



Despite having the option to extend his stay for the 2027-28 campaign, O'Neill recently indicated that the new season will be his last. When asked about his initial reluctance to take the permanent job earlier this summer, the 74-year-old admitted to Sky Sports: "Well, that was genuine, really, because I wasn't sure at the time. In all honesty, I'm not even sure now!

Content cannot be displayed without consent

"But I've got the chance to come back. When we go and clinch the championship, it's euphoria you feel at the time, and then time passes on.

‌



"So you're a year further on, and I think the only thing I could really guarantee you is that, if I do survive the year, that would really be it. Time does catch up with you, and I genuinely mean this about surviving the year, because you step into it again.

"Last year gives you a bit of respite, that's all it does - but we're in the results business, and we have to win. And I'm absolutely no different to anybody else; I have to try and win some football matches, otherwise I'll find myself in trouble."

Sports.title: Gianni Infantino 'offers Morocco World Cup final' in exchange for support
Sports.content:
Gianni Infantino 'offers Morocco World Cup final' in exchange for support

Morocco will co-host the 2030 World Cup alongside Spain and Portugal and Gianni Infantino has reportedly offered them the chance to stage the final - on one condition

View 2 Images Gianni Infantino's position at FIFA may be coming under threat (Image: Nick Potts/PA Wire)

Beleaguered FIFA chief Gianni Infantino has reportedly offered Morocco the chance to host the World Cup final in 2030 in exchange for the nation's support as he desperately tries to cling to power.

‌



Infantino is in Morocco where he has held a crisis meeting of FIFA officials today as calls for him to resign over his botched plot to sell off the World Cup intensify.

‌



The 2023 edition of the tournament will be hosted across Spain, Portugal and Morocco as well as three matches played in South America.

‌



Morocco have been one of Infantino's biggest supporters over the course of his decade in charge of FIFA and were rewarded with co-hosting rights for the World Cup.

Gianni Infantino faces lengthy ban and disciplinary action as crisis meeting held today READ MORE :

They want to host the final in the new 115,000-seat Hassan II stadium in Casablanca which will be the largest football stadium in the world when it is built.

‌



And, according to The Times, Infantino has promised Morocco they will host the final of the tournament, rather than the Santiago Bernabeu in Madrid, if they publicly endorse him in the face of mouting criticism.

But Infantino is said to be concerned over the lack of support from Saudi Arabia who will host the 2034 World Cup.

Former Real Madrid and Barcelona star Luis Figo has become the latest big name to denounce Infantino with many calling for him to resign immediately.

‌



He described Infantino's conduct as “the lowest, most deceitful and cravenly self-interested behaviour” he has ever witnessed. “And believe me, I have met some rogues in my time in the game,” he added.

Figo went on: "Infantino has debased the office of FIFA President that he promised to elevate. He has lied, deceived and tried to feather his own nest of the game he is supposed to serve.

View 2 Images Luis Figo alongside Gianni Infantino in 2024

‌



“It is too late to save his dignity but it is not too late to save football. He should go. Now.”

It comes after legendary former Arsenal boss Arsene Wenger, now head of football development at FIFA, distance himself from the doomed plot to sell off the World Cup.

“At FIFA, I am the chief of global football development," Wenger said.

‌



“Together with my team, I oversee the data analysis of the game, the FIFA online training centre, the development of youth education through 60 academies across 60 countries where they are most needed, and youth competitions around the world.

“In addition, I am a technical adviser to IFAB. I was not involved in this strategic plan and first became aware of the project through media reports.

“The decision to withdraw the project was absolutely necessary and beyond question, because I firmly believe in an independent FIFA that serves our game with commitment, transparency, and integrity.”

Liverpool exploring Ibrahim Mbaye transfer as PSG star's stance on move emerges

Liverpool want to sign a winger before the summer transfer window shuts and while Paris Saint-Germain's Bradley Barcola remains their top target, team-mate Ibrahim Mbaye is also of interest

View 2 Images Liverpool are targeting Ibrahim Mbaye (Image: Jean Catuffe/Getty Images)

Liverpool are exploring the conditions of a deal for Paris Saint-Germain winger Ibrahim Mbaye, who'd reportedly be open to joining the Reds. Mbaye, 18, is being pursued separately to his PSG team-mate, Bradley Barcola, whose £145million valuation has seen the move stall.

‌



With less than a month to go until the summer transfer window closes, Liverpool are intent on signing at least one winger. It comes after Mo Salah departed Anfield earlier this summer while Cody Gakpo continues be linked with an exit.

‌



The Times report that Liverpool are interested in Mbaye, with PSG valuing him between €40m (£34m) and €50m (£42m). It's added that Bayer Leverkusen are also keen on the French-born Senegal international, who sources say would be attracted to Anfield.

‌



Mbaye, who can play on either side of attack, became the youngest player to start a game for PSG at 16 years and six months old. But his pathway appears to be blocked with Ousmane Dembele, Khvicha Kvaratskhelia, Desire Doue and Barcola still at the club, while PSG have also made offers for Monaco star Maghnes Akliouche and Ajax's Mika Godts.

In addition, Liverpool kept tabs on Anthony Gordon before Newcastle sold him to Barcelona a deal worth up to £69m. The Reds have already signed one wide forward this summer, welcoming Osasuna's Victor Munoz for £34m.

Sports.title: Luis Figo has brutally taken down Gianni Infantino - now he should succeed him
Sports.content:
Luis Figo has brutally taken down Gianni Infantino - now he should succeed him

The Portuguese legend has pulled no punches in laying into the FIFA president eleven years after briefly putting himself forward for the same role

View 3 Images Luis Figo has called on Gianni Infantino to resign immediately

It is now getting to the stage where some people of a significantly forgiving nature might actually begin to feel a little bit sorry for Gianni Infantino. Of course, he brought it all on himself - not just with his heinous scheme to sell off the World Cup but with his entire power-obsessed, egotistical tenure as FIFA president.

‌



But the tirade of criticism has been something else. And one of the most cutting character assessments has now come from the breed of ‘legend’ that Infantino has tried to ingratiate himself with over the past decade.

‌



Luis Figo referred to Infantino’s conduct as “the lowest, most deceitful and cravenly self-interested behaviour” he has ever witnessed. “And believe me, I have met some rogues in my time in the game,” Figo said, before going on to describe Infantino as “a relic of the game’s past.”

‌



Inside the murky world of FIFA lobbying as Jamie Carragher reveals World Cup request READ MORE :

Figo then proceeds to accuse Infantino of inflicting “a litany of abuses … on football’s reputation” during a “reign of terrible self-interest.” And the Portuguese legend was just warming up.

“Infantino has debased the office of FIFA President that he promised to elevate,” said the former Barcelona and Real Madrid player. “He has lied, deceived and tried to feather his own nest of the game he is supposed to serve.

“It is too late to save his dignity but it is not too late to save football. He should go. Now.”

‌



Brutal stuff. Almost certainly nothing that most right-minded football followers would disagree with, but brutal all the same.

Figo is right, of course. Infantino has to go. But what Figo - a close confidante of UEFA president Aleksander Ceferin - does not suggest, it seems, is that someone such as himself should now step forward.

View 3 Images Arsene Wenger has denouned Gianni Infantino's ill-fated scheme but not the man himself (Image: FABRICE COFFRINI/AFP via Getty Images)

‌



For a couple of months in early 2015, Figo did just that. Backed by figures such as David Beckham and Jose Mourinho no less, Figo launched his candidacy for the FIFA presidency at Wembley in February 2015.

I remember his manifesto brochure. Expanding the World Cup to 48 teams was one of his key policies, by the way. Figo was standing against Sepp Blatter - who would go on to win a fifth term - but pulled out shortly before the May election.

Which was a shame. Figo might have made a good president. And what is to stop him running against Infantino? Or more likely, what is to stop him running in a contest to succeed Infantino, who will surely not run for re-election?

‌



The main theme of the backlash to the Infantino proposal that will now go down as one of the most infamous in the game’s history has been that football belongs to the people, belongs to the fans. Well, what sort of character would the fans want as the figurehead of the world’s governing body?

View 3 Images Gianni Infantino is now under immense pressure to step aside from the FIFA presidency

They would not have wanted a Swiss lawyer in the first place, that is for sure. Ironically, they might have wanted someone like Arsene Wenger.

‌



After a few days’ silence, FIFA’s chief of global football development denounced Infantino’s FIFA Forward Enterprise Scheme but did not individually denounce the man who gave him his lucrative gig. Wenger might be too allied to Infantino, and has himself had the odd madcap idea recently.

But perhaps he should stand against Infantino or stand to succeed him. Wenger has always claimed to have the good of the game at heart.

That is unlikely to happen but the more options we have from those who know about the game rather than the politics of the game, the better. And it would be good if those options included Figo.

Sports.title: Argentina fly-half Albornoz hit with four-game ban over ugly England scenes
Sports.content:
Tomas Albornoz has been suspended for four matches after being hit with a misconduct charge following Argentina's Nations Championship defeat against England last month.

The dramatic contest saw seven yellow cards handed out before Bautista Delguy thought he had scored a last-gasp try to level the match.

However, referee Angus Gardner ruled the effort out after a TMO review, allowing England to hold on for a famous 31-24 victory.

Image: Tommy Freeman (centre) argues with Mateo Carreras (11)

Playmaker Albornoz was seen remonstrating with Gardner after the final whistle, while he also made physical contact with the match official.

Gardner also received abuse as he left the field, with an object thrown from the stands in ugly scenes inside the Estadio Unico Madre de Ciudades.

A statement from World Rugby said: "Tomas Albornoz has been suspended for four matches after admitting misconduct arising from interactions with match officials following Argentina's Nations Championship match against England on 18 July.

"In determining misconduct under Regulation 18, the disciplinary committee noted that the Argentina fly-half accepted the misconduct allegations. In particular, he accepted that his conduct, taken as a whole, was intimidatory.

"The committee accepted that contact with referee Angus Gardner, although limited in nature, occurred while disputing a match official's decision and formed part of that overall course of intimidatory conduct. The committee also noted that Albornoz approached the referee on two separate occasions and had to be restrained by team-mates.

"The committee further noted that, while Albornoz accepted that his conduct amounted to intimidation of a match official, he did not accept that his actions were abusive, insulting, offensive or threatening. That distinction was accepted by both World Rugby and the committee.

"In determining sanction, the committee accepted that the contact with the referee, while limited, occurred in the context of disputing a match official's decision and formed part of an overall course of intimidatory conduct. The committee considered that aspect of the misconduct comparable to the low-end entry point for contact with a match official under Appendix 1 to Regulation 17, which carries a six-match suspension.

"Taking into account Albornoz's early acceptance of the charge, his undertakings to issue public and private written apologies, and his previously clear disciplinary record, the committee accepted that a four-match suspension was appropriate. Albornoz is therefore suspended for the following matches:

Sports.title: Luís Figo blasts ‘deceitful’ Infantino and says Fifa president must quit to ‘save football’
Sports.content:
The Portugal legend Luís Figo has described Gianni Infantino’s ill-fated scheme to sell off stakes in the World Cup to private investors as “the lowest, most deceitful and cravenly self-interested behaviour I have ever witnessed” and called on the Fifa president to resign.

Infantino was forced to scrap his controversial proposal after a fierce backlash that was led by Uefa, with the 56-year-old now battling for his future having called an emergency meeting of Fifa staff on Wednesday as pressure on him mounts.

On Tuesday the Jordan Football Association president, Prince Ali bin al-Hussein, accused Fifa of blackmail by threatening to withhold financial assistance from his federation if it refused to back the president’s bid for re-election. That came after the former Arsenal manager Arsène Wenger, who is Fifa’s chief of global football development, issued a statement distancing himself from the plan that said the decision to withdraw it was “absolutely necessary and beyond question”.

Figo, the former Barcelona and Real Madrid winger who won 127 caps for Portugal, has now joined the chorus of criticism and accused Infantino of having “debased the office of Fifa president that he promised to elevate” since taking over in 2016.

“I could write 10,000 words on the problems at Fifa. But the solution needs only three: Infantino must go,” he wrote in the Daily Mail.

“He has lied, deceived and tried to feather his own nest at the expense of the game he is supposed to serve. He has lost the support of his senior staff, his closest advisers, the vast majority of people who devote their lives to this sport and even, it would seem, the Fifa Peace Prize winner [Donald Trump]. It is too late to save his dignity but it is not too late to save football. He should go. Now.”

skip past newsletter promotion Free newsletter | Every weekday Sign up to Football Daily Kick off your evenings with the Guardian's take on the world of football Preview latest Enter your email Sign up after newsletter promotion

Figo, who has been a football adviser to Uefa since 2017, cited Infantino’s lack of transparency over his attempts to push through the private equity deal that would have reportedly led to an increase in his salary to $30m a year as more evidence he is unfit to govern world football.

“It’s not honest when you fail to mention that, after you have delivered the head of the World Cup on a platter to your mates in DC, they are going to give you a job worth five times your current salary,” he wrote.

“None of this comes as a surprise when you consider the litany of abuses he has inflicted on football’s reputation; from suspending and reversing disciplinary decisions to breaking the laws of the game over a half-time show, nothing gets in the way of pleasing his friends.”

Sports.title: ‘Dream come true’: Eva Olid delighted after being named Manchester United’s new head coach
Sports.content:
Eva Olid has described being appointed as the Manchester United Women head coach as a dream come true after signing a two-year contract until 2028 with the option of a further year.

The Spanish coach will replace Marc Skinner, whose surprise departure came on Monday.

Olid led Hearts to their first Scottish Women’s Premier League title last season and departing the Edinburgh club by mutual agreement in a five-year spell during which she oversaw a remarkable period of progress.

The 40-year-old’s arrival comes as United are understood to be prioritising developing homegrown players rather than spending large transfer fees rather than spending large fees.

In a statement, the club said: “Olid’s appointment marks the start of an exciting new era for Manchester United Women as the club embarks on a clear vision for long-term, sustainable growth and success.

“Important foundations have already been put in place to further support the development of homegrown talent and young players, as well as senior internationals, and establish a clear football identity. Significant investment has been made into the academy infrastructure and facilities, underlining the ambition to build the leading youth development system in the country.”

Olid told the club’s website yesterday: “The opportunity to become head coach of Manchester United Women is a dream come true. The club has outstanding infrastructure and everything we need to achieve our ambitions. We have an excellent training facility, an academy that is already producing players capable of performing in a competitive first team, and an exceptional group of support staff.

View image in fullscreen Eva Olid signs up for Manchester United. Photograph: Manchester United/Getty Images

“There is already so much talent within our squad and I am excited to work with the players to support them to fulfil their immense potential. I am joining Manchester United at a really exciting time. There is a clear alignment in our shared vision for long-term success. I cannot wait to begin preparing a team that will make our incredible supporters proud.”
