World.title: Malawi President travels to South Africa after wave of Malawian returns
World.content:
Malawi President Arthur Peter Mutharika has travelled to South Africa on a private visit, weeks after Malawi intensified efforts to assist citizens returning home amid heightened immigration enforcement and anti-foreigner tensions in South Africa.

According to a statement issued by Malawi’s Office of the President and Cabinet on Wednesday, Mutharika departed from Kamuzu International Airport for what the government described as a private visit to South Africa.

“The plane carrying the State President will depart Kamuzu International Airport this afternoon,” the brief statement said, without disclosing the purpose of the visit or how long the President is expected to stay.



Private visit comes after wave of Malawian returns

The President’s trip comes after Malawi recorded a wave of citizens returning from South Africa in recent weeks.

The Malawian government has been coordinating the repatriation of nationals who opted to return home following increased immigration enforcement operations and incidents of anti-foreigner unrest in parts of South Africa.

Authorities have arranged transport for returning citizens while urging Malawians living in South Africa to use legal immigration channels and remain calm.

Although the presidency has not linked Mutharika’s visit to the migration situation, the timing has attracted attention given the recent movement of Malawian nationals back home.

No official details on South Africa programme

The Office of the President and Cabinet did not indicate whether Mutharika will meet South African President Cyril Ramaphosa or other government officials during his stay.

The statement described the trip solely as a private visit, with no official programme or itinerary released.



Private presidential visits are typically not accompanied by detailed public schedules unless official engagements are planned.

Malawi continues monitoring citizens abroad

The Malawian government has repeatedly said it remains committed to supporting its citizens affected by developments in South Africa.

Officials have been monitoring the situation while working with diplomatic missions and other government agencies to facilitate the safe return of nationals who choose to go back to Malawi.

South Africa remains home to one of the largest Malawian migrant communities, with many working in sectors such as agriculture, hospitality, construction and domestic services.

World.title: Fikile Mbalula denies BUYING his way into ANC secretariat
World.content:
ANC Secretary-General Fikile Mbalula has strongly denied allegations that he used money to secure his election at the party's 55th National Conference. Image: Flickr

ANC Secretary-General Fikile Mbalula has strongly denied allegations that he used money to secure his election at the party’s 55th National Conference, saying he has instructed his lawyers to seek clarity from fellow ANC National Executive Committee (NEC) member Dr Nkosazana Dlamini-Zuma.

The allegations emerged during an episode of the Renaissance Podcast hosted by former EFF MP Dr Mbuyiseni Ndlozi, which aired on Monday.

Money played a significant role

During the interview, Dlamini-Zuma claimed that money played a significant role in the ANC’s 2022 elective conference and alleged that Mbalula openly distributed cash in a bid to secure support for his election as secretary-general.



“And also, Mbalula was dishing the money in the clinic, so money has played a role in the ANC,” Dlamini-Zuma said.

When Ndlozi asked whether the money was handed out openly, she replied: “Openly, yeah, it wasn’t like a secret.”

Asked whether the alleged payments were intended to secure Mbalula’s election as secretary-general, she responded: “To be elected and for the president to be elected.”



Dlamini-Zuma further alleged that the ANC’s current top seven officials were effectively elected through the use of money.

When Ndlozi pointed out that the ANC’s rules prohibit the use of money to influence conference outcomes, Dlamini-Zuma said: “Money was used clearly. We all know. We all saw it. At least in 2022, we saw it.”

“If you ask anyone who worked at the clinic at the time, they’ll tell you. Even the media reported it… I’m not revealing a secret. The media reported it at that time.”



Fikile Mbalula rejects claims

In a statement issued on Tuesday, Mbalula dismissed the allegations as false and damaging.

He said he had instructed his legal team to formally seek clarity from Dlamini-Zuma regarding what he described as “very damaging and painful allegations.”

The ANC secretary-general has rejected any suggestion that he bought support during the conference, where he was elected to one of the party’s top leadership positions.



The allegations have once again thrust the issue of money in ANC internal elections into the spotlight, although Dlamini-Zuma has not publicly produced evidence to support her claims. Mbalula’s legal response could set the stage for a further public or legal confrontation between two senior members of the governing party.

STATEMENT ON THE REMARKS MADE BY CDE DR NKOSAZANA CLARICE DLAMINI-ZUMA. https://t.co/QjWYW5PulA pic.twitter.com/vym6a0OAi1 — ANC SECRETARY GENERAL | Fikile Mbalula (@MbalulaFikile) August 5, 2026

World.title: BREAKING: Impeachment committee to request Ramaphosa
World.content:
President Cyril Ramaphosa addresses Parliament during a sitting of the National Assembly. Parliament's Section 89 impeachment committee has agreed to request his appearance before its inquiry. Image: Flickr

Parliament’s Section 89 Impeachment Committee has agreed to request President Cyril Ramaphosa to appear before its inquiry.

The committee reached the decision during a meeting on Tuesday, where members considered a legal opinion on the president’s appearance, the appointment of an evidence leader and the draft terms of reference for the inquiry.

Ramaphosa will not be the first witness

The committee agreed that Ramaphosa will not testify first. Instead, it will first hear evidence and establish a case before inviting the president to respond.



Published on Wednesday, 5 August, the statement read: “The Impeachment Committee met today to consider, among other things, the legal opinion on the appearance of the President, its recommendation for the appointment of the evidence leader and the draft terms of reference that will guide its work.

“In considering the legal opinion, the committee agreed that the President will not be the first witness to appear before the committee. It must first establish a case to which the President can respond.”

Committee chairperson Makashule Gana said the committee hoped Ramaphosa would appear voluntarily.

“We hope that the matter will not reach the point where the President must be summoned. However, if he refuses to appear, the committee will have to summon him,” Gana said.

Evidence leader recommended

The committee also resolved to recommend the appointment of Advocate Thandazani Madonsela SC as evidence leader.

The recommendation will now be sent to Parliament’s Secretary, who will oversee the administrative process required to formalise the appointment.



Terms of reference nearing completion

Members also considered the committee’s draft terms of reference and proposed further amendments.

The revised document will now be referred to Parliament’s Legal Services Division to refine the wording and ensure consistency before it returns to the committee for final consideration.

Gana said the committee is now close to finalising the framework that will guide the Section 89 inquiry.

World.title: Teenage African World Cup star to complete R2 billion Real Madrid move
World.content:
Real Madrid generally gets what they want in the market. They’re moving mountains to sign Ivorian World Cup star Yan Diomandé.

Real Madrid land World Cup star Diomandé

19-year-old Ivorian winger Yan Diomandé is on the brink of a €120m (R2,26 billion) move from RB Leipzig to Real Madrid. The Spanish giants, now under the tutelage of Jose Mourinho, who starts his second stint in the capital, made Diomande their number one target. He starred for the Ivory Coast at the World Cup in June and July, showing flashes of the brilliance which convinced Los Blancos to make him their latest Galactico. European champions PSG also expressed interest in the talented left-sided attacker. He struck 12 goals and provided eight assists in 33 Bundesliga appearances last season.

RB Leipzig managing director Marcel Schäfer has denied that the ongoing battle between Roc Nation and former Ivory Coast international Max Gradel could derail the deal to take Diomandé to Madrid. There still remains ambiguity as to which of Roc Nation, owned by Jay Z, and Gradel’s agency, Maxidel, possesses rights to the player.



What does this all mean for Vini Jr and his Real Madrid future?

The future of 26-year-old Brazilian star Vinicius Junior is a matter of intense debate. If Diomandé makes his long-awaited move to Real Madrid, Vini could be on his way out. There are several reports suggesting he could be on his way to Arsenal, although another theory is that these rumours have originated out of the player’s camp in order to leverage an improved deal with Madrid. He’s out of contract in mid-2027, and club president Florentino Perez has no desire to lose him on a free transfer. A big-money switch to the Gunners is still on the cards, especially with Diomande virtually through the door.

Latest Pirates, Kaizer Chiefs transfer news

What does Pirates new boy Sebastian Pedersen’s arrival mean for Evidence Makgopa? One man who seems to be staying put is Oswin Appollis. This, despite rumours of an approach from FC Porto. Khanyisa Mayo has signed permanently from CR Belouizdad for a reported fee close to R9.8 million following a prior loan spell. Adolf Mtasingwa is a 27-year-old defensive midfielder signed from Azam FC. Langelihle Phili is also expected to join the club imminently.

MTN8 quarter-final weekend

Orlando Pirates meet Durban City on Saturday, 8 August at 15:00. Sundowns tackle Polokwane later that day at 18:00. Meanwhile, Chiefs face Golden Arrows at FNB Stadium on Sunday, 9 August at 18:00.

World.title: Leon Schuster meets with Gayton, promises exciting news [video]
World.content:
Leon Schuster appeared in good spirits and good health after meeting with Gayton McKenzie in a video posted on social media.

The South African comedian – who has experienced a series of health setbacks in recent years – has teased a film comeback.

He’s also released a Springbok-inspired song ahead of the 2027 Rugby World Cup.



LEON SCHUSTER MEETS WITH GAYTON MCKENZIE

On his social media platforms, Gayton McKenzie posted a video clip of him chatting to Leon Schuster and Alfred Ntombela.

The Minister of Sport, Arts and Culture and the comedy actors appeared in good spirits, laughing and joking about rugby and the Springboks’ latest jersey.

Gayton shared: “It was such a privilege and a joy to spend time with the legends. They both gave us so much over careers that made everyone happy and feel uniquely South African”.



The minister added that both Leon and Alfred would be honoured with a special award later this month.

BACK TO BUSINESS?

In recent years, Leon Schuster has suffered a series of health setbacks that have limited his mobility and left him with chronic pain. He has also spoken out about living with depression and loneliness.

However, the veteran entertainer – known for his iconic films like You Must Be Joking, Oh Schucks, I’m Gatvol, and Mr Bones, among many others. – has hinted that a comeback is on the cards. 

In May, Leon teased a new project with fellow comedian Kevin Fraser. Last month, he surprised his fans after releasing another rugby-inspired song, titled Miljoene Hande vir Rassie, in honour of Springbok coach Rassie Erasmus.

Leon also recently celebrated his 75th birthday in good spirits while surrounded by loved ones.

World.title: ‘I don’t qualify for rates rebate’: Pensioner reveals why her savings work against her
World.content:
Commenting on a recent The South African article, 65-year-old Patti Wright shared details of why she doesn’t qualify for a rates rebate, despite her age. She explained that having retirement savings worked against her application. “I don’t qualify for the rates rebate as I ‘have money saved for my retirement’,” she wrote, quoting the reasoning she says she was given.

Wright said the same savings she relies on for retirement income are already taxed, meaning she faces financial strain from two directions: taxation on her savings, and disqualification from a rebate designed to support pensioners with living costs.

Rebate criteria under scrutiny by pensioners

Wright’s experience raises questions about how rates rebate eligibility is assessed for pensioners, particularly those who saved independently for retirement rather than relying solely on a government grant. Her comment suggests that having private retirement savings, even modest ones intended to cover basic living costs, can disqualify pensioners from rebates that are otherwise aimed at easing financial pressure for older South Africans.



This tension points to a broader gap in how rebate systems account for pensioners who fall between two categories: not wealthy enough to comfortably absorb full rates costs, but seemingly too “resourced” on paper to qualify for relief.

Reader reactions remain mixed

Wright’s comment drew a mix of reactions, including surprised and shocked emoji responses from other readers. It appeared alongside other comments in the same thread debating pensioner taxation and grant funding more broadly, with readers split on how the financial burden of supporting older South Africans should be distributed.

Her account adds a personal example to an ongoing conversation about whether current rebate and taxation policies adequately support pensioners who have saved independently, rather than penalising them for doing so.

World.title: ‘Courts don't play with human life’ - Lawyer on intentional HIV infection
World.content:
JOHANNESBURG - The case of a Pretoria man who was accused of intentionally infecting his 38-year-old girlfriend with HIV has sparked conversation.

Not just on reactions, but the legal consequences of knowingly exposing someone to the virus.

The 47-year-old man, who is currently in custody, faces an attempted murder charge.

It is alleged that the man had intentionally infected her because he did not want her to be with anyone else.

READ | Pretoria man accused of intentionally infecting lover with HIV appears in court

While the court has not yet determined his guilt or innocence, the allegations have already raised questions about how the South African law treats cases where a person knowingly infects another with HIV.

Ayanda Gwabeni of Ayanda Gwabeni and Partners said the law recognises HIV as a chronic infection that presently has no cure and is likely to eventually lead to the death of a person or even reduce that person's lifespan, even if by an uncertain margin.

As such, he said, intentionally infecting a person with HIV can be legally found to constitute the necessary intention to murder.

“This is no different from a person who poisons another person while knowing that the victim can or probably will die from that poison, either now or eventually in the distant future. The difference here is just the type and the method of tool used to cause the possibility of death; the result is otherwise the same.”

Gwabeni said the law acknowledges two types of intention: Direct and indirect.

Indirect Intention applies to a person who knows they are HIV positive, foresees the possibility of infecting the other with a chronic, but does not take preventative measures.

While direct intention is aware of their HIV status as positive, risks associated with their act and has the intention to infect the person.

Gwabeni warned that the sanctity of human life is not a game in courts and any attempt to end or compromise it is an extremely serious offence which carries significant consequences, such as direct imprisonment.

“It is a criminal offence to intentionally expose a person to the HIV infection. Responsibility is not an option but a must in order not to find yourself languishing in prison because of your moment of madness," he said.

Gwabeni pointed to the case of Mphikeleli Lovers Phiri, who was convicted of attempted murder and sentenced to 6 years’ imprisonment.

The charge stems from having had unprotected sex with the complainant while knowing that he was HIV-positive.

READ | HIV prevalence up since 2002: Expert explains why

He said six years could be in line for the suspect; however, he said, with each case, the gravity of the offences is considered during sentencing.

In the same breath, Gwabeni acknowledged the fact that “HIV is no longer the 'certain death' type of chronic infection it was many years ago, and as such, that could be a factor that will work towards reducing the gravity of the offence."

Even so, he believes six years' direct imprisonment remains.

READ | Pretoria man returns to court in alleged intentional HIV infection case

Beyond the courtroom, Gwabeni believes the case carries a message about responsibility.

He said people who know they are HIV-positive should disclose their status to sexual partners before engaging in sexual activity so that the participant accepts and takes the risk voluntarily,
