Polish swimmer Bartłomiej Kubkowski has become the first person in history to swim across the Baltic Sea between Sweden and Poland, covering a distance of just over 160 kilometres (99 miles). On Sunday evening, an exhausted Kubkowski clambered onto the beach in the town of Dziwnów on Poland’s northern Baltic coast, around 56 hours after he had set off from Kaseberga in Sweden on Friday. The achievement marks a personal triumph for Kubkowski, for whom this was the fifth attempt to complete the route. His effort this year has raised over 715,000 zloty (€166,000) for children’s cancer treatment so far, with donations to his fundraiser still coming in. View this post on Instagram A post shared by PURELY ATHLETICS (@purelyathletics) During the crossing, Kubkowski was unable to sleep and, although a support boat accompanied him and provided food and drink, he was not allowed to touch the vessel itself. His journey of around 160km was not far off the longest-ever continuous, unassisted open-water swim ratified by the Marathon Swimmers Federation, which was the 168.3 km swum by American Sarah Thomas in 2017 in Lake Champlain, between the US states of New York and Vermont. Kubkowski has been attempting to swim the route between Sweden and Poland since 2022, getting progressively closer to achieving the goal. Last year, he came within 11km of the Polish coast before extreme exhaustion and deteriorating weather forced him to give up, reported Eurosport. However, Kubkowski, a former competitive swimmer who now devotes himself to ultraswimming, did last year manage to break the world record for the longest distance swum in a swimming pool over 24 hours, after he managed to cover 103.6 km (64.5 miles). Another Polish swimmer, Karolina Szczepaniak, is also currently attempting to swim from Sweden to Poland along a slightly different route to Kubkowski’s. At the time of writing, she is around 110km into the 172km journey, and has raised almost 400,000 zloty for charity. Szczepaniak, a former Olympic swimmer, also attempted the feat last year, but was forced to give up after 57 hours amid worsening weather. However, the 146.7km she swam set a new record for the longest distance covered by a female swimmer in the Baltic Sea and a Polish record for open-water swimming by a woman. A Canadian multinational operator of convenience stores, Alimentation Couche-Tard, has announced plans to acquire Poland’s Żabka Group, which runs Europe’s largest chain of convenience stores. The company has offered 32 zloty per share, valuing Żabka at 32.6 billion zloty (€7.56 billion). Żabka’s main shareholders have agreed to sell their stakes, with final approval still required from stock market investors. If the transaction is completed, Żabka is likely to be delisted from the Warsaw Stock Exchange just two years after its market debut. Właściciel Circle K chce przejąć 100% Żabki. Cena w wezwaniu ma wynieść 32 zł za akcję =>https://t.co/61XEGuQnnB via @PawelBiedrzycki https://t.co/61XEGuQnnB — Strefa Inwestorów (@strefainw) July 31, 2026 The acquisition will be carried out through Alimentation Couche-Tard’s Polish subsidiary, Circle K, which runs petrol stations, and will cover all of Żabka Group’s more than one million shares. Alimentation Couche-Tard has already secured commitments to acquire at least 57.2% of the company. Heket, an entity linked to CVC Capital Partners owning 37.6% of Żabka’s shares, and PG Investment Company, holding 10%, have agreed to sell their entire stakes. A group of major individual shareholders, together controlling 9.6% of Żabka’s shares, has also agreed to sell its holdings to the Canadian buyer. The investors include members of the company’s management and former executives. They have also agreed to reinvest part of the proceeds from the sale into Alimentation Couche-Tard shares. The tender offer for the remaining shares was announced on Friday by Ipopema Securities, which is acting as the intermediary in the transaction. Alimentation Couche-Tard and Żabka expect subscriptions for the offer to open around 26 August, following a review of the tender document by the Polish Financial Supervision Authority (KNF). The companies foresee the transaction closing by the end of the year. The Canadian company expects Żabka to continue operating independently, under the leadership of its current management team, and to retain its brand. Żabka shares jumped after the announcement, rising from 29.26 zloty to around 31.60 zloty on Friday afternoon, an increase of about 8%. Żabka, which runs Europe’s largest chain of convenience stores, has made its stock market debut in one of Europe’s biggest listings this year. Its IPO was the fourth largest in the history of the Warsaw Stock Exchange and valued the firm at €5 billion https://t.co/fmqLteZjdR — Notes from Poland 🇵🇱 (@notesfrompoland) October 18, 2024 If completed, the acquisition would be the largest takeover in the history of Alimentation Couche-Tard, which already owns 17,300 stores across 27 countries. Alex Miller, Alimentation Couche-Tard’s CEO, said the company is “committed to supporting the continued growth of the Żabka business while drawing from its strengths in areas such as food, digital engagement, customer loyalty, private brand, supply chain, logistics and innovation”. Żabka made its debut on the Warsaw Stock Exchange in 2024 in one of Europe’s largest initial public offerings that year, with a valuation of around €5 billion. The company is Poland’s largest convenience store operator, with about 13,000 locations nationwide run by around 11,000 franchisees. It has also expanded internationally, opening its first stores in Romania and reaching 100 outlets there last year. Poland’s largest convenience chain, Żabka, has opened the 100th store of its Romanian brand, Froo, one year after launching there. “We are learning from local consumers and laying the groundwork for a long-term presence in Romania,” says Żabka’s VP.https://t.co/0CaZTaVhlB — Notes from Poland 🇵🇱 (@notesfrompoland) June 13, 2025 In mid-July, Japanese retailer Seven & i Holdings, which operates the global 7-Eleven chain among other businesses, also emerged as a potential investor in Żabka. World.title: The split in Poland’s opposition could help them unseat Tusk’s government [Opinion]
World.content: Keep our news free from ads and paywalls by making a donation to support our work! Notes from Poland is run by a small editorial team and is published by an independent, non-profit foundation that is funded through donations from our readers. We cannot do what we do without your support. By Daniel Tilles If Mateusz Morawiecki cuts his final ties with PiS and forms a new party, it may help broaden the opposition’s appeal by offering voters a more moderate, centre-right option. While the strings have not yet been fully cut, Poland’s main opposition party, the national-conservative Law and Justice (PiS), is splitting in two. A group of 40 MPs led by former Prime Minister (and PiS deputy leader) Mateusz Morawiecki have now formed a separate parliamentary caucus of their own, after last week refusing to sign a pledge of loyalty and quit the association they had formed – as had been demanded by PiS leader Jarosław Kaczyński. Former Polish PM @MorawieckiM says 41 lawmakers aligned with him will form their own parliamentary caucus, deepening a split in conservative opposition party @pisorgpl. The proposed group would become the third-largest bloc in Poland's Sejmhttps://t.co/coOdpS7pia — Notes from Poland 🇵🇱 (@notesfrompoland) July 29, 2026 The move means that Morawiecki’s caucus, known as Development Plus (Rozwój Plus), is now the third largest in parliament, while PiS, which is down to 147 MPs, has lost its status as the biggest. For now, most of Morawiecki’s followers officially remain members of the PiS party, a situation that will only change if they either resign or are thrown out following a disciplinary process that could take weeks. But unless either or both sides make major concessions, it seems only a matter of time before Development Plus becomes a separate party. A lot of international reporting has suggested that these developments will harm Poland’s right-wing opposition and boost the re-election chances of Prime Minister Donald Tusk’s more liberal coalition at next year’s parliamentary elections. In fact, PiS’s split could well help the opposition win a majority. Over the last year, PiS has found itself in an increasingly difficult position. Its support in the polls has fallen below 25%, the party’s lowest level in 14 years. Meanwhile, combined support for two far-right opposition groups – Confederation (Konfederacja) and Confederation of the Polish Crown (KKP) – has risen to over 20%, threatening PiS’s longstanding dominance on the right. In response, Kaczyński has pushed his party in a more rightward direction, picking a hardline figure, Przemysław Czarnek, as PiS’s prime ministerial candidate in March. That signalled that PiS was aiming to compete head to head with the far right on many issues, taking tougher positions on Ukraine, the EU, migration and climate policy. In many cases, that meant disowning the legacy of the PiS government led by Morawiecki from 2017 to 2023. It also meant that the party was ceding the centre ground, something Morawiecki, who represents the more moderate, technocratic side of PiS, was particularly concerned about (alongside his own waning influence). When in power, PiS launched a revolution in Poland's energy transition. But now, in opposition, it has disowned those achievements and returned to an emphasis on coal. This could be a missed opportunity to win back centrist voters, writes @OrzelBartlomiej https://t.co/8cGvubn7N2 — Notes from Poland 🇵🇱 (@notesfrompoland) June 29, 2026 Should Morawiecki now, as expected, launch his own centre-right party, focused on economic development, it would appeal to moderate conservatives who are opposed to the Tusk government but put off by the far right and PiS’s own hardline turn. Inevitably, some of the support for Development Plus would come at the expense of PiS – but not all of it, and possibly not even most of it. An example of something similar happening can be seen elsewhere among the opposition. Until last year, KKP was part of Confederation. However, its leader, Grzegorz Braun, was expelled after announcing a run for the presidency against Confederation’s official candidate, Sławomir Mentzen. In June 2025, KKP formed its own parliamentary caucus. Since then, support for Confederation has remained stable at around 13-14%, while KKP has risen to over 9% in the polls. So, by splitting, the two groups actually increased the size of their potential electorate, with KKP successfully appealing to an even more radical pool of voters than Confederation. It is possible that Morawiecki could do the same in the opposite direction – his new party winning over moderate conservatives while PiS continues to appeal to its most loyal supporters as well as competing with the far right. There certainly seems to be fertile ground for such a party. Regular polling by the state research agency CBOS shows that the proportion of Poles with a negative view of Tusk’s government rose to its joint-highest level this month, at 48%, while only 29% have a positive view. The last time that positive views outnumbered negative ones was in February 2024, the second full month of the current ruling coalition’s time in power. Among those who voted for Tusk and his allies in 2023, dissatisfaction is strongest among moderate conservatives. Both Tusk’s centrist KO and one of his coalition partners, The Left (Lewica), are polling only slightly below the proportion of votes they received in that year (30.7% and 8.6%, respectively). However, the most conservative part of the coalition, the centre-right Third Way (Trzecia Droga) alliance, has fallen from 14.4% of the vote in 2023 to only around 4-5% today for the two parties that constituted it, Poland 2050 (Polska 2050) and the Polish People’s Party (PSL) (which last year decided to go their separate ways). An IBRiS poll for Polsat News in April this year found that, whereas 84% of KO voters and 57.1% of Left voters have a positive view of Tusk’s government, that figure falls to 42.5% for Third Way voters, a majority of whom (51.6%) have a negative opinion. PSL and Poland 2050, the two parties that make up the Third Way alliance, have confirmed that they are splitting and will stand separately at the next elections. They will, however, remain part of @donaldtusk's ruling coalition https://t.co/NduEJY25eE — Notes from Poland 🇵🇱 (@notesfrompoland) June 18, 2025 Moderate conservatives’ disillusionment with the government, combined with PiS’s shift away from the centre ground, gives a clear opportunity for Morawiecki. And Tusk’s coalition itself showed in 2023 the advantages for the opposition in offering a broader set of options. While some – in KO in particular – had pushed for centrist and left-wing parties to stand jointly on a single list at that year’s elections, instead they campaigned as three main blocs. That gave voters opposed to the PiS government a genuine choice, and likely played a big part in the record turnout that helped bring Tusk’s coalition to power. It is similarly possible now that a four-branched opposition, ranging from Morawiecki on the centre right, through PiS and Confederation, to Braun on the radical right, could together win a parliamentary majority. Polls currently show those four groups with combined support of around 50% (though polling regarding support for Morawiecki’s prospective party should for now be treated with caution). Jestem dumny z tego, co wspólnie zrobiliśmy dla Polski. I wiem jedno – nasza misja wciąż trwa💪🇵🇱#RozwojPlus pic.twitter.com/xOnxKDoroS — Mateusz Morawiecki (@MorawieckiM) July 31, 2026 However, even if they do win a majority, it is far from certain what would happen then. In 2023, the three opposition blocs were, although standing separately, clearly aligned with one another and focused on removing PiS from power. When they together won a parliamentary majority, it was absolutely clear they would form a coalition government. By contrast, today’s opposition is deeply divided. Confederation and KKP regularly attack PiS. It is not at all clear that Confederation would be willing to form a coalition government with PiS, while Kaczyński has explicitly ruled out working with the pro-Russian, anti-American Braun. Meanwhile, Morawiecki’s split has followed months of bitter infighting within PiS, which has often been carried out in public. The manner in which he and his allies are now departing the party means that relations with PiS are likely to remain difficult. The national-conservative opposition PiS party's newly named candidate for prime minister has made overtures to the far-right Confederation. But he also ruled out Grzegorz Braun, an even more radical far-right figure, serving in a PiS-led government https://t.co/i3zOZJWdUN — Notes from Poland 🇵🇱 (@notesfrompoland) March 9, 2026 It would therefore be hard for the opposition to form a government, even if they do win a majority. In this situation, the role of President Karol Nawrocki may be vital. Though elected with the support of PiS last year, he was technically an independent and maintained good relations with Confederation and even, to some extent, Braun (who endorsed Nawrocki after being eliminated in the first round). When Morawiecki this week announced the “ten pillars” of Development Plus’s programme, he made clear his loyalty to Nawrocki: the second of those pillars is “respect for the president”. Nie ma silnej Polski bez wielkich ambicji. Nie ma wielkich ambicji bez ludzi, którzy je zdefiniują i będą gotowi wziąć odpowiedzialność za ich realizację. Bezpieczeństwo. Rozwój. Suwerenność. Ambicja. Tożsamość. Patriotyzm. To nie hasła wyborcze, ale fundamenty państwa, które… pic.twitter.com/G0YBbfhLye — Mateusz Morawiecki (@MorawieckiM) July 28, 2026 Many on the right hope that Nawrocki can play a role next year in helping the opposition present a more united front during the election campaign. It is also the president who decides who gets the opportunity to try to form a government after the elections. That role would be of particular significance if, as is very possible, Tusk’s KO emerges as the biggest individual party but the opposition together may be able to form a parliamentary majority. Given that we are still over 14 months away from the elections, and Morawiecki has not even yet officially split from PiS, it is still far too early to make confident predictions. However, while Morawiecki’s likely departure is clearly a personal blow to Kaczyński – and a sign of the 77-year-old’s waning influence over not only the Polish right but even his own party – it may conversely provide a boost to the opposition as a whole. World.title: World of Warcraft Film Ibelin to Shoot in Prague
World.content:
Production of Ibelin, a new film based on the life of Norwegian World of Warcraft player Mats Steen, is moving to Prague this summer.

Filming is expected to take place at Barrandov Studios from early August through early October, following the production’s spring shoot in Norway.

The film is not connected to the 2016 Hollywood movie Warcraft. Instead, it tells the real-life story of Steen, who lived with Duchenne muscular dystrophy and built friendships, relationships and a social life inside the online world of World of Warcraft.



The Prague production is reportedly seeking extras for roles including blacksmiths, guards and innkeepers. The casting suggests that parts of the film set in the game’s fictional world could be filmed in the Czech Republic. The producers have not yet officially confirmed which scenes will be shot in Prague.

Charlie Plummer leads the cast

American actor Charlie Plummer will portray Mats Steen. Toni Collette and Stephen Graham will play his parents, while the supporting cast includes Bill Nighy, Isabela Merced, Maisy Stella, John Bradley and Ivanna Sakhno.

The film will be directed by Norwegian filmmaker Morten Tyldum, whose credits include The Imitation Game and the science-fiction film Passengers.

At the center of the story is the difference between Steen’s increasingly restricted physical existence and the freedom he experienced online. His character, known in World of Warcraft as Ibelin, became an important figure to people he met through the game.

One of Norway’s largest film projects

The Prague shoot is part of an international production with a reported budget of CZK 1 billion.

According to the Norwegian Film Institute, the project received 20 million Norwegian kroner in production support.

Ibelin is being produced by Vendôme Pictures, Pathé and Neby-Tyldum as an international co-production. The Norwegian Film Institute describes it as an English-language drama with a planned running time of around two hours.

The film is being developed for theatrical release, with its premiere currently expected in the third quarter of 2027.

World.title: GALLERY: Time Capsule Buried Beneath Prague’s Wenceslas Square Tramline
World.content:
A time capsule containing different items, newspapers and messages documenting life in 2026 has been buried beneath Prague’s reconstructed Wenceslas Square.

The capsule was placed on Wednesday, August 5, near the statue of St. Wenceslas as work continues on the upper section of the square.

The Prague New Town Association, which is involved in activities around the statue and the surrounding area, organised the ceremony.

The date was not originally chosen for its historical significance. Construction work ultimately determined both the day and the location of the burial. But the association later discovered that August 5 also marks the 60th anniversary of the release of the Beatles’ Revolver album.

“We were wondering what made August 5 go down in history. Then we found out that it was 60 years ago that the Beatles released their famous album Revolver. So now we are leaving a message here for future generations,” said Monika Vlková, the association’s executive director.



The box, measuring 60 by 40 by 23.5 centimetres and weighing about eight kilograms, was then taken to a prepared pit beside the statue. Workers had excavated the hole to a depth of around 1.7 metres, where the capsule was placed before the site was covered.

The container had been wrapped in transparent protective film, as had its contents.

The collection includes coins, newspapers published during the first week of August 2026, T-shirts, badges and written messages. It also contains proposals submitted by architects during the competition for the redesign of Wenceslas Square.

The box reportedly also holds a hammer and a beer glass.

The objects are accompanied by a 20-page report describing everyday life in the Czech capital in 2026. The capsule also contains USB drives with digital material documenting the period of the Covid-19 pandemic and its effects on life in central Prague.

The capsule is intended to remain underground for decades. The association estimates that Wenceslas Square could undergo another major reconstruction in roughly 50 years, although nobody can predict when the next intervention will actually take place.

World.title: Czechia Tightens Temporary Protection Rules for Ukrainian Men Aged 23 to 60
World.content:
New rules affecting Ukrainian men seeking temporary protection in the Czech Republic will take effect on August 5, 2026.

Under the changes, men aged 23 to 60 applying for temporary protection will have to demonstrate that they are exempt from military service in Ukraine.

The requirement will apply to new applications and certain other applications for protection, but not to people who already hold valid temporary protection.



The Czech Interior Ministry says the new rules follow an EU Council decision published in the Official Journal of the European Union on August 4. The decision also extends temporary protection for people fleeing Russia’s war in Ukraine until March 31, 2028.

For applicants aged 23 to 60, military registration documents will be checked as part of the application process. Applicants will use Ukraine’s Reserv+ system to demonstrate their military status, with the electronic military registration document showing whether they are exempt from military service.

The rules are different for younger applicants. People aged 18 to 22 will only need to demonstrate that they are registered in the Reserv+ system.

The new requirement concerns people applying for temporary protection for the first time, as well as repeat applications and applications connected with family reunification. It does not apply to people who already have valid temporary protection.

The military-service requirement will also not be introduced as part of the regular extension process. Ukrainians whose temporary protection is already valid will therefore not have to provide this additional documentation when extending their status through March 2028.

Interior Minister Lubomír Metnar said the Czech government had pushed for stricter conditions for new applicants. According to the ministry, the change is expected to reduce the number of new arrivals and ease pressure on public services, including health care and social security.

World.title: Filming of American Spy Series to Bring Restrictions to Prague 7
World.content:
Filming for the American series Birdwatcher will take place at the Prague 7 tax office on Kapitána Jaroše Embankment from August 8 to 24, bringing temporary restrictions to the area.

The production will use the tax office building at Kapitána Jaroše Embankment 1000/7, while part of the sidewalk outside the building will be closed to accommodate filming equipment.

The restrictions will not affect the normal operation of the tax office.



Drivers should also expect temporary parking restrictions on nearby Na Ovčinách Street. Vehicles will still be allowed to pass through the street, but parking will be prohibited during the designated filming periods.

The restrictions will not be in force continuously throughout the filming period. They will apply only on specific dates, with Prague 7 publishing a map showing the affected areas and individual dates on its website.

Prague has become a major filming location

Birdwatcher is an American spy fantasy series set during the Cold War. The production is being led by Legendary and Apple TV, with Andy Goddard directing. Wyatt Russell plays the lead role.

The story follows Colonel Lee Shaw as he embarks on a covert mission behind enemy lines to prevent the Soviet Union from unleashing a new Titan capable of devastating the United States and altering the balance of the Cold War.

The series is set in the 20th century against the backdrop of the Cold War, and parts of the production are being filmed in Prague.

Czech production company Stillking Films is handling the local production. The company has previously worked on major international productions filmed in the Czech capital, including The Gray Man.

World.title: Seven Prague Rooftops to Visit Before Summer Ends
World.content:
Summer is already moving on, and Prague’s rooftop season won’t last much longer.

August is the time to make the most of the city’s terraces, sunset views and outdoor events before they disappear for another year.

Here are seven rooftops and terraces worth visiting before autumn arrives.



1. REASON at Masaryčka

Eleven floors above Masaryk Station, REASON offers one of Prague’s newest rooftop dining spots, with views over the city and the Zaha Hadid-designed Masaryčka development.

This summer, its terrace is also home to the seasonal Frerejean Frères Champagne Bar, serving champagne by the glass, cocktails, oysters and light bites. The menu includes THE REASON KIR, made with herbs grown on the rooftop.

This summer: Champagne, oysters and cocktails above Masaryčka.

2. W Prague – ABOVE Rooftop

ABOVE Rooftop at W Prague brings a Mediterranean feel to the top of Wenceslas Square.

The daily Mediterranean Hour runs from 5 to 6 PM, with two spritzes and a Taste of the Mediterranean platter for CZK 990. Oysters are also served from Thursday to Saturday, alongside a programme of summer events and pop-ups.

This summer: Mediterranean Hour, sunset drinks and oysters in the centre.

3. MINUTY Rooftop Terrace

The rooftop at Fairmont Golden Prague offers views across Pařížská, Letná and the city centre from nine floors up.

MINUTY Rooftop Terrace by Golden Eye focuses on champagne, oysters, caviar and cocktails. The terrace is seasonal and is expected to remain open until September, weather permitting.

This summer: Champagne, oysters and caviar with a view.

4. Sky Lounge 360°

For the view alone, Sky Lounge 360° is hard to beat. The rooftop looks across Prague’s historic centre and becomes livelier during the summer months, with DJs, sunset events and Prague Rooftop Festival activities.

It is more about drinks and atmosphere than a long dinner — a good option for an evening that starts at sunset and continues after dark.

This summer: Sunset events, DJs and panoramic views.

5. The Cloud One Rooftop

The Cloud One Prague on Hybernská has its own rooftop cocktail bar overlooking the Masaryčka area.

The relaxed terrace works well for an after-work drink, while summer events bring DJs and a livelier atmosphere at sunset. It has also joined the Prague Rooftop Festival programme.

And if you want to make a night of it, REASON is just a short walk away.

This summer: Cocktails, sunset events and views of Masaryčka.

6. Casablanca Sky Bar

On the sixth floor of The President Hotel, Casablanca Sky Bar looks out over the Vltava and Prague skyline.

With DJs, cocktails and regular sunset events, it has more of a party atmosphere than a traditional hotel rooftop. It is also one of the venues taking part in the Prague Rooftop Festival.

This summer: DJs, cocktails and sunset parties above the Vltava.

7. Monkey Bar

Monkey Bar at Falkensteiner Hotel Prague is a quieter alternative, with a green, jungle-style terrace close to the main railway station.

Every Thursday until the end of August, the terrace hosts BBQ & Beats, combining barbecue, live music and summer drinks. Frozen margaritas are also on the menu.

For daytime plans, there is Jungle Brunch, including a bottomless mimosa option.

This summer: BBQ & Beats every Thursday through August.

World.title: Prague Kettlebell Brand Železná Koule Opens 600-Square-Metre Gym in Karlín
World.content:
Czech kettlebell training brand Železná koule has opened its largest location yet at Danube House in Prague’s Karlín district.

The new 600-square-metre gym expands the brand’s presence in Prague and comes ahead of the next edition of its flagship Amazing 12 fitness programme.

Železná koule has built a community around kettlebell training and coached workouts rather than the traditional self-service gym model. The company says more than 20,000 people have trained through its programmes since its launch.

At its Karlín location, members train under the guidance of coaches in small groups. The approach is designed to provide more personal instruction and a structured training environment, rather than simply giving members access to gym equipment.



The new location is also the latest venue for the company’s Amazing 12 programme, a 12-week fitness and body transformation course that combines regular training with nutrition guidance and ongoing support.

What is the Amazing 12 programme?

The programme is aimed at both people who are new to structured strength training and more experienced gym-goers looking for a more organised approach to their workouts.

Although the programme itself lasts 12 weeks, participants first complete a preparation week, making 13 weeks in total. During the programme, they take part in 64 training sessions, with one-hour workouts held every weekday under the supervision of a coach.

Groups are limited to a maximum of five participants, allowing coaches to work closely with each person throughout the programme.

View this post on Instagram A post shared by Železná koule (@zelezna_koule)

The programme is designed to provide a structured routine covering exercise, nutrition and recovery, with progress tracked throughout the 12 weeks.

The next Amazing 12 programme starts on August 31, 2026, with places available at the new Karlín location as well as Železná koule gyms in Smíchov and Strašnice.

The Karlín opening is part of the continued expansion of a Czech fitness brand that has developed a following around kettlebell-based training and small-group coaching. For people unfamiliar with the name, Železná kloule roughly translates from Czech as “iron ball,” referring to the kettlebell at the centre of its training approach.

More information about the Amazing 12 programme, including registration, is available at amazing12.cz.

World.title: A New Bus Line to Prague Airport Could Launch This Autumn
World.content:
A new private bus service could soon connect Prague’s main railway station directly with Václav Havel Airport, offering passengers another option for getting between the city center and the airport.

Transport company Dinarica is planning to launch the service at the end of October. The route would run between the main railway station and the airport, providing a direct alternative to the Airport Express operated by České dráhy.

The company says it wants to address one of the main practical problems passengers face when travelling by bus to the airport — luggage storage.

Dinarica plans to use Setra and MAN buses equipped with air conditioning, seat belts and more spacious seating. Each vehicle will accommodate between 70 and 90 passengers.



The planned service would operate from morning until evening, with buses running approximately every two hours.

A one-way ticket is expected to cost around CZK 125, making the service considerably cheaper than the Airport Express. Its fare is set to rise to CZK 200 following the latest price increase.

Prague’s public transport system already offers cheaper ways to reach the airport. Trolleybus 59 and bus 100 connect Václav Havel Airport with the Prague public transport network, but neither provides a direct connection to the main railway station.

Both services are primarily designed as part of the regular city transport system.

If approved and launched as planned, the Dinarica service would give passengers another direct option between Prague’s main railway station and the airport, with a lower fare than the Airport Express.

World.title: More Than Half of Czech Households Could Be Overpaying for Electricity
World.content:
A large number of Czech households may be paying more for electricity than necessary because they are using a distribution tariff that does not match their actual consumption.

A new analysis estimates that switching to a more suitable tariff could save households more than CZK 1.3 billion a year in total.

The analysis was conducted by energy company bezDodavatele.

The company examined electricity consumption at 1,132 household consumption points using the two most common household distribution tariffs, D01d and D02d.

According to data from the Energy Regulatory Office (ERÚ), D01d and D02d are used by around 65 percent of the approximately 6.5 million household consumption points in the Czech Republic.



The analysis found that changing the distribution tariff could reduce electricity costs for more than half of the households examined.

Many households never reconsider their tariff

One reason is that households often keep the same tariff for years without checking whether it still suits their electricity consumption.

A tariff that made sense when a household first connected to the electricity grid may no longer be the cheapest option after its consumption patterns have changed. Many consumers, however, do not regularly review the distribution tariff listed on their electricity bill.

According to the analysis, 53 percent of the households examined could have benefited from a different tariff. Their average potential saving was CZK 728 per year.

For some households, the difference was considerably larger, with potential savings reaching several thousand crowns annually.

Prague households show the highest potential

The analysis found differences between the country’s main electricity distribution areas.

In Prague, where electricity is distributed by PRE, changing the tariff could have been beneficial for 68 percent of the households included in the study. That was the highest proportion recorded among the three distribution zones.

In the EG.D distribution area, which covers much of southern Bohemia and Moravia as well as parts of the Vysočina, Zlín and Olomouc regions, the figure was 51.5 percent.

The lowest share was recorded in the ČEZ distribution area, where 46.3 percent of the households analyzed could potentially benefit from a different tariff.

The picture changes slightly when looking at the size of the potential savings. Although Prague had the highest proportion of households that could benefit from a tariff change, the largest average annual saving was recorded in the ČEZ Distribuce area, at CZK 833 per household.

World.title: Hungary AI readiness ranks among global leaders, tops public adoption
World.content:
Hungary has emerged as one of the world’s most AI-ready outsourcing destinations, placing fourth in a new international ranking and achieving the highest population-level artificial intelligence adoption score among all 25 countries examined.

The 2026 Global Outsourcing AI Readiness Index gave Hungary an overall score of 69.1 out of 100. This placed the country behind only India, Brazil and Malaysia, while narrowly ahead of the Philippines, Chile and Czechia.

The result makes Hungary the highest-ranked country in Central and Eastern Europe, underlining its growing potential as a destination for technology-supported business services and outsourced work.

Hungary AI readiness stands out in everyday adoption

Hungary’s strongest result came in the population AI adoption category, where it received 86 points – the highest score among the 25 outsourcing destinations included in the study.

The country finished ahead of Bulgaria, which scored 82 points, as well as Brazil with 79 and India with 78.

According to the 2026 Global Outsourcing AI Readiness Index, the population adoption category assesses how widely AI tools have entered the daily lives of working-age residents. It considers current use, the pace of adoption and whether infrastructure such as internet access, electricity and smartphones can support further growth.

The result does not mean that 86 per cent of Hungary’s population necessarily uses AI. The figure is a comparative index score showing that Hungary performs close to the top of the selected group across the indicators examined.

Nevertheless, the ranking suggests that Hungarians are highly open to using generative AI and other artificial intelligence tools in everyday life.

Hungary leads Central and Eastern Europe

Hungary also outperformed every other Central and Eastern European country included in the ranking.

Czechia placed seventh globally with 66.9 points, followed by Bulgaria in ninth place with 62.8. Poland finished 11th with 61.2 points, while Romania ranked 13th with 59.4.

For international readers, Hungary already plays an important role in the regional business services sector. Budapest and several major university cities host shared service centres, software development teams and multilingual corporate operations serving customers across Europe and beyond.

A high level of public familiarity with AI could make it easier for Hungarian employees and companies to introduce AI-supported workflows, particularly in administration, customer service, finance, information technology and digital marketing.

If you missed it: Giant AI data centre platform planned near Paks, GLOBWISE wins mandate, targeting 2028 – visuals

Businesses are also embracing artificial intelligence

Hungary received 67 points for enterprise AI adoption, placing seventh among the 25 destinations. The category measures whether companies have moved beyond testing AI and begun integrating the technology into their regular operations.

Hungary ranked behind India, Brazil, Malaysia, Czechia, Chile and the Philippines in this area, but remained well above most countries examined.

The figures indicate that Hungarian businesses are adopting AI at a relatively rapid pace, although corporate implementation has not yet reached the same level as public enthusiasm.

Hungary’s workforce AI literacy score was lower, at 54 points, resulting in 15th place in that category. Workforce literacy covers factors such as the concentration of AI specialists, the strength of the developer community and the availability of professional AI skills.

The 32-point difference between population adoption and workforce literacy was the largest among the six highest-ranked countries. Rather than diminishing Hungary’s achievement, the gap highlights an opportunity: public interest in AI could provide a strong foundation for professional training, workplace development and education programmes.

A promising position in the AI-driven economy

The index combines four areas: population AI adoption, workforce AI literacy, enterprise adoption and the AI education pipeline. These categories account for 30, 30, 25 and 15 per cent of the final score respectively.

The authors stress that the ranking is a snapshot rather than a prediction, and that it focuses specifically on countries competing for outsourced work. Scores are relative to the group examined and should not be interpreted as absolute measures of national technological development.

Even with those limitations, Hungary’s fourth-place finish represents an encouraging result. Its strong public adoption score indicates that AI is already becoming familiar to many people, while its regional leadership could strengthen the country’s appeal to international companies.

World.title: Hungary’s MÁV is slowing trains and protecting tracks from the heat with paint
World.content:
MÁV is slowing trains and protecting tracks from the heat with paint, Transport and Investment Minister Dávid Vitézy said in a Facebook post on Wednesday.

He said that extreme heat also places a severe strain on the railway network and, in extreme cases, can even cause rail breaks, the Hungarian news agency wrote.

According to experts, the temperature of a rail exposed to blazing sun can be as much as 20 degrees higher than the air temperature, he wrote, adding that MÁV orders enhanced track inspections when rail temperatures exceed 45C, while also paying close attention to the technical condition of rolling stock.

He said that from Saturday the railway company introduced speed restrictions across 282 track-kilometres, on 73 kilometres continuously and on a further 209 kilometres during the hottest hours only.

Extreme heat may damage not only the rail tracks but also railway infrastructure. Photo: Facebook/MÁV-csoport

He added that work is under way on lasting solutions. The use of heat-reflective white paint on the Pécs railway line has produced encouraging results, with measurements showing that it reduced rail temperatures by 3C to 7C. In addition, cabinets housing level-crossing equipment are being fitted with a special coating to reduce warming caused by sunlight.

World.title: Shocking new details emerge about student worker’s fatal construction-site accident
World.content:
A 17-year-old boy fell head-first into a slicing machine at a construction company site in Szeged, after which the machine pulled him in. Paramedics arriving at the scene were unable to save his life. Police are still investigating the tragedy, which took place in mid-July, while further details have emerged about the precise sequence of events and the circumstances surrounding the fatal incident.

Head-first into machine

The tragic case happened on July 16 at the site of a construction firm in Szeged. The 17-year-old was doing summer student work there through a contract partner. As we reported at the time, he was pulled into a slicing machine used in the construction industry and died as a result of the accident. The machine was used to cut and package insulation boards.

Telex, in an article written by a Szegeder journalist, reported that the young man fell head-first into the slicing machine, after which the machine pulled him in. The emergency services called to the scene were unable to save him. The Csongrád-Csanád County Police Headquarters confirmed that they are investigating the case on suspicion of negligent endangerment causing death in the course of work, and experts have also been brought in.

Illustration – the city centre of Szeged with the iconic dome. Photo: depositphotos.com

Under-18 workers are especially protected by law

Hungarian law gives student workers under the age of 18 enhanced protection. Minors may work in industrial settings, but only if the work does not pose harmful consequences given their physical condition, development and state of health.

Their daily working time may be no more than eight hours, they cannot be employed on overtime, and they are entitled to longer rest periods. During the risk assessment, employers must also examine separately whether the workplace, work equipment or technology poses an increased danger to a minor. If so, they must also consider whether the role can be performed at all by a worker under 18.

Illustration – the student worker’s life could not be saved. Photo: depositphotos.com

Safety training is not enough

Labour lawyer Dr Alex Ember told the Szegeder journalist that in such work arrangements the host company usually bears the greater labour-law and especially occupational-safety responsibility, since it organises the work, provides the conditions and supervises the workers. In the Szeged case, however, only the conclusion of the investigation will determine whether any omission or irregularity took place.

Occupational safety training is compulsory for minors too, but on its own it does not guarantee safety. Younger and student workers typically have less experience, so they may need closer supervision. Dangerous work should be carried out by properly trained employees, and in some cases a person responsible for directing the work must also be appointed.

If you missed: Car crashes into Budapest tram stop, smashing glass shelter

The Hungarian Trade Union Confederation says serious workplace accidents are often caused by several factors at once: for example, training that is not sufficiently practical, inadequate supervision of inexperienced workers, time pressure or incomplete risk assessment. It can be particularly dangerous if a young worker is asked to carry out a task requiring greater experience without proper oversight.

Company promises tighter safety

The union says many workplace accidents could be prevented if existing rules were applied consistently. It believes a stronger occupational safety authority, more practical training, greater mentoring for minors and stricter risk assessment are needed.

Bodrogi Bau Kft., the company involved, declined to comment in detail because the investigation is ongoing. It did say, however, that it will do even more in future to prevent workplace accidents, and that its management remains in contact with the deceased boy’s relatives.

The police investigation is still under way, so it is not yet known exactly what led to the death of the 17-year-old student worker, or who will ultimately be held responsible for the tragedy.

World.title: Valuable WWII German motorcycle, human remains and explosives pulled from the Danube in Budapest – photos
World.content:
An extraordinary relic drew attention on the embankment at Batthyány Square when, thanks to the Danube’s exceptionally low water level, a German military motorcycle from the Second World War became visible among the rocks. Later, other dangerous items and human remains were also uncovered at the site.

Second World War German motorcycle emerges from Danube in heart of Budapest

Experts arriving at the scene quickly established that it was a German DKW NZ 350-1 from the Second World War. Remarkably, the vehicle was found in unusually good condition, almost complete.

Source: honvedelem.hu

But the motorcycle was far from the only wartime relic in the riverbed. During the excavation, German and Soviet infantry ammunition, remnants of hand grenades and artillery shells, as well as German TMi–35 mines, were also discovered. Because of the dangerous finds, the area was secured and bomb disposal experts began clearance work. A total of ten mines had to be removed, which also required the temporary restriction of traffic on Bem quay.

Source: honvedelem.hu

According to specialists, the variety of items suggests that a rubbish pit created after the war may have been exposed. Among the objects found were animal bones and civilian ceramics, alongside military materiel.

Source: honvedelem.hu

Mud helped preserve the motorcycle

The river mud preserved the motorcycle and several associated items in a curious way, including a German Y-strap and a bayonet frog. But the DKW, weighed down by mud and trapped water, tipped the scales at more than 200 kilograms, making it impossible to lift out easily from the rocky riverbank.

Source: honvedelem.hu

In the end, it was taken across to the Pest side with the help of a research vessel, then transported to the hangar of the Military History Institute and Museum on Kerepesi Road. It will be cleaned and conserved in the coming weeks.

There is, however, a darker side to the story: human remains were found beneath the motorcycle. Investigations showed them to be the remains of German soldiers, whose further excavation and recovery was carried out by the German war graves organisation.

Source: honvedelem.hu

If you missed: Should Budapest remove its controversial WWII monument? Public consultation begins

What is it worth today?

On the basis of market comparisons, this is an especially valuable example, all the more so because it surfaced in near-complete form, meaning there is a chance it could be restored and even displayed. Collectors buy DKW motorcycles of this type in unrestored, incomplete condition for a few thousand euros; in good, usable condition they fetch around €7,000 to €12,000. A neatly restored, original military example can command €12,000 to €18,000, and more if it is well documented.

A 1944 NZ 350-1, for instance, sold at Dorotheum in 2020 for €7,360. Its description stated that roughly 12,000 such machines had been produced for the army by 1945. A fully restored example with original paint costs €16,500, or more than 6 million forints. In Hungary, these are the examples currently for sale.

The motorcycle found in the Danube is set to be cleaned and conserved.

Declassified CIA file reveals unidentified objects flying from Budapest to Moscow in the 50’s

The source of the photos: honvedelem.hu

World.title: Lake Tisza under threat: alarm bells ring at tourist hotspot – photos
World.content:
The water level of Lake Tisza has fallen below 700 centimetres at the upper gauge at Kisköre. According to the Central Tisza Valley Water Directorate, the drop is due to an extreme lack of rainfall in the Tisza catchment area, exceptionally low river inflows and increased evaporation.

Lake Tisza exists because of irrigated arable farming

Water management specialists are working to preserve the available water resources while also meeting agricultural and ecological water demands, the water transfer in the Körös valley and the water supply for the stretch of the Tisza below Kisköre.

Lake Tisza is not a natural lake, but an artificial reservoir created in the Tisza floodplain. Its creation is linked to the Kisköre barrage, construction of which began in the late 1960s, while its hydroelectric equipment was completed by 1974. The dam primarily serves water storage, irrigation and water management tasks, while the resulting water surface has over time become home to an exceptionally rich ecosystem. The roughly 127-square-kilometre lake is fed by the Tisza, and its water level is influenced by the river’s flow and the operating regime of the water authorities.

Numerous tourism developments

In recent years, significant tourism developments have also taken place in the region. In Tiszafüred, the Lake Tisza Cycling Centre and the Tiszafüred–Poroszló cycle bridge were built, the open-water beach was renovated, and in 2024 new visitor attractions, including the Kérész Centre, also opened. Altogether 17 projects were carried out in the region in 2024, affecting tourist attractions, infrastructure and ecological conditions alike. A further 300 million forint development has also begun at Tiszafüred beach, including, among other things, a water playground, a cycling track and new services.

If you missed it: The end draws near for Lake Velence as Danube hits a record low in Budapest: will Hungary dry out this year?

Today, Lake Tisza is a favourite destination for cyclists, water tourists, anglers and swimmers. The cycle route around the lake can be completed safely, while visitors can discover the reeds, islands and channels on boat and canoe trips. In addition to swimming, there are opportunities for nature watching and fishing. The current drop in water level is therefore an important issue not only for water management, but also for tourism.

World.title: Will Fidesz split soon? A survey says the breakaway camp would have a strong chance
World.content:
Viktor Orbán’s Fidesz party seemed only a few months ago to be a monolithic bloc, unassailable at the summit of power. Now, however, it appears it could even split in two: into an Orbán party and a moderate, centre-right grouping. A fresh Medián poll may now give that scenario another push.

A new civic party would stand a good chance

Medián Research Institute is the only Hungarian polling company to have accurately predicted the results of every parliamentary and European Parliament election, and it also pinpointed the scale of Tisza’s April victory with remarkable precision, assigning Péter Magyar’s movement exactly the number of seats it ultimately won.

On the basis of the latest Medián survey, if former Fidesz politicians who represented a moderate, civic line were to found a new party, they would make it into parliament. Of course, that is meagre consolation in light of the party’s former multi-million vote hauls and two-thirds majorities: sitting in opposition in the Hungarian National Assembly under current conditions is useful at best for paying politicians and their assistants, while against governing parties armed with a two-thirds majority the chances of any real success are slim.

Having 5-10 MPs against 141 is not easy, but being in the Parliament has its advantages. Photo: Facebook/TISZA Párt

In any case, Medián says a new civic force would be able to appeal to at least 5 per cent of the total population. Had such a party existed in April, then according to the poll summarised by hvg.hu it would have been the third-largest group in parliament, ahead of Mi Hazánk.

Many Fidesz voters are only loosely tied to Orbán

Names have also been mentioned in connection with the new formation. Among public figures seen as part of Fidesz’s moderate wing — and critical of the party leadership according to both the news and their own remarks — atv.hu cited former EC commissioner and minister Tibor Navracsics, Székesfehérvár mayor András Cser-Palkovics, and former MP and government commissioner Orsolya Ferenc.

Will Orbán’s Fidesz split? Photo: Facebook/Orbán Viktor

Interestingly, according to Median, only one third of current Fidesz supporters remain firmly loyal to Viktor Orban, while 18 per cent would have no problem switching to the new party, and 15 per cent would at least consider it. The new party could therefore potentially count on roughly one third of Fidesz’s existing camp — which stands at around 19-20 per cent support — but that would indeed be enough to clear the parliamentary threshold, at least under the current rules.

Former Orbán spin doctor, Árpád Habony, appears to have left Hungary, new address reveals

A rock-solid Tisza lead

Tisza, meanwhile, has promised a new electoral law, which is also a social expectation of them. Within that framework they are already talking about a number of innovations, including limits on MPs as well. The more hardline camp would allow anyone to sit in parliament for just two terms, while the more permissive would allow three terms, or 12 years. All this also means that Mi Hazánk’s caucus could be completely replaced, while within Fidesz’s parliamentary group replacements are already under way so that those who still see a future in parliamentary work can take on the government across the chamber.

Tisza continues to enjoy support unseen before among Hungarian voters: 57 per cent of the total population would back it in an election held this Sunday.

Péter Magyar’s lead is rock-solid. Photo: Facebook/Péter Magyar

World.title: Ancient suburban rail carriages to be replaced soon, Hungarian minister vows
World.content:
As part of the Baross Gábor Rail Development Plan, the 50-year-old suburban rail carriages will be replaced, with the procurement process for the renewal of the entire HÉV fleet on the H5 Szentendre, H6 Ráckeve and H7 Csepel lines due to be launched this year, Dávid Vitézy, the transport and investment minister, wrote in a Facebook post on Wednesday.

42 new suburban rail carriages

He said 42 new, modern, 120-metre-long trainsets will be purchased using EU funds returned to Hungary. The necessary tender will be issued later this year, and the first trains could enter service in 2030.

The fleet will be upgraded with fully accessible, air-conditioned, modern vehicles, offering passengers a more comfortable, faster and more reliable service, he added.

Currently, Budapest and its surrounding areas are served by four HÉV lines: H5 (Szentendre), H6 (Ráckeve), H7 (Csepel), and H8–H9 (Gödöllő and Csömör). Photo: Kemény Máté / Wikimedia Commons

He said that in recent years hundreds of thousands of people have moved from the countryside to Budapest, and from the capital to the surrounding commuter belt and outer districts, often without adequate public transport links. As a result, traffic has continued to grow, and Budapest’s inner city has become increasingly difficult in which to live.

The only real remedy, he wrote, is high-quality public transport, and one of the key conditions is that HÉV should offer a genuine alternative to the car in terms of comfort, quality and speed.

World.title: Putin’s people take aim at PM Magyar again, this time mocking the energy crisis and Paks
World.content:
The country has spent days anxiously awaiting news of whether the entire Paks nuclear power plant will have to be shut down, or whether Unit 2, which produces 240MW, can continue operating at reduced output. While the signs are now encouraging, the Russians nevertheless appear to have decided this was the moment to take a swipe at Péter Magyar, who had previously criticised the Russian-run Paks II development as too expensive.

Russians write about difficulties at Paks and Romania’s Cernavoda

“Mr Magyar, do you still think it is too expensive?” the Russian state news agency RIA Novosti reportedly told the prime minister yesterday, according to atv.hu. Operations at the Paks nuclear plant have been hanging by a thread, but it now appears the Danube will not continue to fall, meaning Unit 2 may remain operational at half power for several more days — just when electricity is needed most to keep the country functioning.

In a longer report, the Russian state agency analyses the situation at Hungarian and Romanian nuclear plants, highlighting that both use water from the Danube for cooling. As a result, not only the amount of water available matters, but also the river’s temperature, since discharged water at high temperatures cannot be returned to the river in the interests of protecting wildlife.

Both the Paks and Cernavoda plants are operating at sharply reduced capacity, with a single unit carrying the load at both sites at lower output. The Romanians carried out a major detonation in the Danube the day before yesterday to help supply their plant, as we reported separately with video. In Paks, there is cause for optimism because the drop in the Danube’s water level appears to have stopped. In Budapest, for example, it has risen by 11cm from its low point. At one stage, the shutdown of Paks yesterday morning came down to mere millimetres.

The Danube at the Paks NPP. Photo: MTI

Russian agency takes a swipe at Péter Magyar

Against this backdrop, the Russian state news agency evidently felt it important to take a dig at the Hungarian prime minister, criticising between the lines his sceptical stance on the Paks II development. Péter Magyar had previously indicated that the project’s costs and contractual framework would be subject to a comprehensive review before any final decision is taken.

Paks II NPP extension project. Photo: Facebook/Csárdi Antal

The Russians now pointed to how important Paks is in Hungary’s energy mix — around 40 per cent — and how significant the new blocks would be in future, though it should be noted that they too would rely on Danube water, and would also have to be shut down in the event of drought. Rosatom had previously said it was ready to take part in an audit of the Paks II project so that the Hungarian side could make an informed decision as soon as possible.

If you missed – Horror over Paks II NPP overpricing: did Orbán-linked and Tisza-affiliated businessmen and politicians pocket the cash?

Shifting Hungarian-Russian ties

Hungarian-Russian relations have become rather chilly since Tisza’s election victory. The Russians signalled that they were ready to continue pragmatic ties, and Kremlin spokesman Dmitry Peskov even singled out Magyar for praise for the fact that Hungary still does not send weapons to Ukraine. The mocking tone of the latest news agency report may therefore come as something of a surprise.

Former PM Putin in Moscow with President Putin. Photo: Facebook/Orbán Viktor

During the campaign, Péter Magyar repeatedly spoke of Russian interference on the side of Fidesz — with evidence, for example, cited by journalist Szabolcs Panyi — as President Putin had previously backed Orbán. Since his election victory, however, Magyar has struck a pragmatically detached tone, emphasising his commitment to NATO and the EU, and has called on Putin to end the killing in Ukraine.

PM Péter Magyar about the “most challenging” next 48 hours, Paks NPP shutdown and extraordinary measures

World.title: Bucharest City Hall adopts 25 measures to cut electricity use during energy crisis
World.content:
Bucharest City Hall said that it introduced a package of 25 measures to reduce electricity consumption during Romania's ongoing energy crisis, including dimming public lighting, restricting the charging of electric buses, and switching off ornamental and advertising lights. The measures will apply particularly during the critical 8 p.m.-11 p.m. period, with some restrictions extending throughout the night.

The plan was agreed following a meeting on Monday, August 3, between Bucharest mayor Ciprian Ciucu and the main electricity-consuming entities under the municipality, City Hall said.

As such, public transport operator STB will stop charging its electric buses between 7:30 p.m. and 11 p.m. and restrict maintenance and other energy-intensive activities during the evening. Lighting at parking facilities will only be switched on after 10 p.m., while lighting inside maintenance halls will be reduced between 7:30 p.m. and 11 p.m.

STB will also switch off unnecessary lights and air conditioning systems and disconnect chargers overnight.

Meanwhile, the municipal heating company Termoenergetica will stop pressure-boosting pumps, with domestic hot water supplied using pressure from the cold-water network. It will also reduce or reschedule the operation of recirculation and pressure pumps, limit air conditioning at administrative offices, and switch off non-essential lighting.

The city's public lighting company will also reduce the brightness of LED streetlights connected to its remote management system by around 30%.

Bucharest Local Police will notify private advertising operators to switch off digital screens and illuminated advertising between 8 p.m. and 11 p.m. throughout August, the City Hall also said.

At the City Hall's headquarters, ornamental lighting on the building and in the inner courtyard will remain off throughout the night. The building's cooling system will also be reduced during August, while electric vehicles will no longer be charged during the critical evening period or overnight.

Energy consumption will also be reduced at municipal cemeteries, crematoriums, and parks, while the city's social assistance authority will limit administrative and exterior lighting, switch off non-essential electronic equipment, and schedule energy-intensive activities outside peak hours.

Cultural institutions under Bucharest City Hall, including museums, theaters, the Metropolitan Library, ARCUB, and the Comic Opera for Children, will switch off interior and exterior lighting overnight and limit air conditioning in areas not being used by staff or the public. Electronic and IT equipment will also be disconnected at the end of the working day rather than left on standby.

The measures come as Romania remains under an energy state of alert throughout August amid reduced electricity production caused by drought and historically low Danube water levels. The government has called on public authorities, companies, and households to voluntarily reduce electricity consumption, particularly during evening peak hours.

World.title: AmCham: Romania still needs to pass test of reforms, political stability
World.content:
The sustainability of Romania's fiscal consolidation path, the still high budgetary deficit, and persistent macroeconomic imbalances remain key areas of concern, AmCham Romania has warned.

The recent decision by Fitch to maintain the country's investment-grade rating at BBB- highlights vulnerabilities in the Romanian economy that remain unaddressed. The organization pointed to the causes of Romania's macroeconomic fragility, as identified in the Fitch report: political instability, uncertainty in decision-making, and the risk of a slowdown in reforms.

“Companies have paid the cost of reducing the budget deficit, are investing, paying taxes, sustaining jobs, and supporting the economy during a difficult period, yet they cannot compensate for the lack of policy predictability, a criterion closely scrutinized by clients, shareholders, and institutional investors,” AmCham said.

The organization said that the current context calls for less political confrontation and greater institutional responsibility, and that investor confidence and Romania's credibility depend on stable governance, predictable public policies, and the ability of public institutions to deliver on their reform commitments.

“The priorities are clear: combating tax evasion and improving tax collection, restructuring public spending, professionalizing the public administration, accelerating the reforms needed to fully absorb NRRP funding and resources available under the next EU Multiannual Financial Framework, and making full use of the opportunities offered by the SAFE instrument. These priorities can no longer be postponed or subordinated to electoral cycles,” it said.

At the same time, the organization called on decision-makers and the administration “to stop tolerating corruption, incompetence, and the stalling of strategic projects in key sectors such as energy, the digitalization of public systems, defense, healthcare, and education.”

“The current crises in the energy and cybersecurity sectors have exposed systemic vulnerabilities that would have been avoidable had the necessary reforms and investments been undertaken in time. As economic, energy, climate, and security challenges become more frequent and complex, delays in reforms and investment in critical infrastructure, along with prolonged political instability, create systemic bottlenecks, increase economic costs, erode trust in public institutions, and fuel social tensions, ultimately weakening the state's ability to respond effectively to crises,” AmCham said.

Given that financing needs remaining acute and the global economy is undergoing significant transformation, Romania's priority “should be to encourage investors to strengthen their operations in the country, the organization argued. The country should also attract new large-scale investments with a strong multiplier effect across the economy. Preserving, and ideally improving, the country's sovereign credit rating, together with accession to the OECD and the euro area, is a concrete way to signal this commitment to international markets,” it said.

AmCham currently gathers more than 600 American, international, and Romanian companies with cumulative investments of over USD 30 billion in the country.

World.title: Râșnov Film and Histories Festival opens with concerts, outdoor screenings
World.content:
The Film and Histories Festival in Râșnov (FFIR) opens this weekend its 18th edition, showcasing an extensive program of film screenings, concerts, debates, theatre performances, and other events.

The festival kicks off at Feldioara Fortress, where children are invited to take part in interactive workshops, followed by concerts, performances, and open-air film screenings throughout the opening weekend. On August 7, the public will be able to attend a concert by Grupul Om Bun, before watching Andrzej Wajda's classic Katyn, according to a release quoted by News.ro.

In Brașov, the festival begins on August 7 with FFIR Pop-Up: Coresi Edition, a family-oriented program covering sports games, workshops and cheerleading demonstrations by Râșnov Stars. The evening program includes a concert by Watzzy.

On the same day, Codlea hosts a concert by the Romanian Youth Jazz Orchestra at the Evangelical Church, followed by a screening of the Romanian documentary The -escu Family Diary, directed by Șerban Georgescu.

On August 8, the Weavers' Bastion in Brașov (pictured) hosts a solo concert by Radu Almășan (Bosquito), followed by a screening of The Last Viking, the latest feature by Danish director Anders Thomas Jensen.

The opening weekend marks the start of the program running through August 23, bringing together more than 100 events and around 100 guests from the fields of culture, history, journalism and public life across the festival's four host towns.

This year's edition features more than 50 film screenings, 18 debates and lectures, 20 concerts, three theatre performances, four special events, and the FFIR Summer School, which will bring together more than 70 high school and university students. Events will take place in Râșnov, Brașov, Feldioara and Codlea.

The festival will take place August 7-9 in Feldioara, August 7-13 in Brașov, August 8 in Codlea, and August 14-23 in Râșnov.

World.title: Wolt launches split payments for group orders in Romania
World.content:
Wolt announced that it launched its Split Payments feature in Romania, allowing customers placing group orders to pay individually for their own items directly through the app. The feature went live at the end of July and is set to be rolled out to other markets in the coming period.

Previously, group orders required one person to cover the full cost and collect money from the other participants afterwards. Under the new system, each member of the group can add their items and pay their share separately.

Shared costs, including delivery and service fees, are automatically divided among participants. If the person who creates the group order has an active Wolt subscription, eligible benefits such as free delivery or discounts can apply to the entire order.

To use the feature, one customer starts a group order, selects Split Payments, and shares an invitation link or QR code. Other participants can then join, select their items, and pay directly through the app, the company said.

Once everyone has completed their part of the order, the person who created it confirms the purchase, with all items delivered to a single address. Each participant receives a separate payment confirmation and can see their purchase in their personal order history.

Wolt said the feature can also be used for workplace orders, with participants able to use eligible meal benefits for their individual share.

Split Payments joins other features available through the platform, including Gifting, which allows customers to send orders with a personal message, and Scheduled Orders for arranging deliveries in advance.

Wolt has operated in Romania since May 2025 and is currently present in 34 cities and surrounding areas.

World.title: Romania's industrial, logistics demand rises 11% in H1 as developers resume speculative projects
World.content:
Demand for industrial and logistics space in Romania increased by 11% year-on-year in the first half of 2026, reaching 569,000 sqm, according to a report by real estate consultancy Cushman & Wakefield Echinox. Leasing activity accelerated particularly in the second quarter, when around 329,000 sqm was transacted.

New demand accounted for 58% of the total volume in the first half, while developers have also begun resuming speculative projects after several years in which new developments were generally launched only after securing significant pre-leasing.

Romania's stock of modern industrial and logistics space reached 8.14 million sqm at the end of the second quarter, of which approximately 4 million sqm was in Bucharest and the surrounding area. Another 532,000 sqm was under construction nationwide.

The return of speculative development contributed to an increase in the nationwide vacancy rate to 6.7%, from 5.4% at the end of 2025. Bucharest's vacancy rate stood at 6.3%.

"The H1 results confirm that Romania's industrial and logistics market remains one of the most dynamic segments of the commercial real estate sector," said Ștefan Surcel, Head of Industrial Agency at Cushman & Wakefield Echinox.

"Another positive sign is the return of speculative developments, following several years during which most new projects were launched only after securing a high level of pre-leasing," he added.

Bucharest continued to account for the largest share of leasing activity, with 386,000 sqm transacted in the first half, including 255,000 sqm in the second quarter alone.

Timișoara recorded 73,600 sqm of leasing activity during H1 and had a total modern stock of 807,700 sqm. Meanwhile, Ploiești had 574,500 sqm of industrial and logistics space and a vacancy rate of just 0.8%.

Among the larger transactions signed during the second quarter were FM Logistic's pre-lease of 10,300 sqm at CTPark Bucharest, Novaintermed's 6,300 sqm lease at VGP Park Bucharest A3, and Lift Banat's 5,900 sqm lease at VGP Park Timișoara A1.

Prime headline rents in Bucharest edged up to EUR 4.80 per sqm per month in the second quarter, while rents in regional logistics hubs remained broadly stable at EUR 4.30-4.65 per sqm per month.

World.title: A new major seismic retrofitting project in Bucharest: the "Bulandra" Theatre building at 1 Schitu Măgureanu Street to be reinforced and modernized
World.content:
News from Companies

Concelex, a leading Romanian construction company, will design and carry out the reinforcement, rehabilitation and modernization works for the building at 1 Schitu Măgureanu Street, which houses the "Lucia Sturdza Bulandra" Municipal Theatre and premises belonging to the University of Bucharest. Listed under seismic risk class I (RsI), the building is managed by the Municipal Administration for the Consolidation of Buildings at Seismic Risk (AMCCRS) and is located in a protected area.

"By signing this contract, we are taking another concrete step forward in the Municipality of Bucharest's seismic reinforcement program. No. 1 Schitu Măgureanu is a complex project, in which we must strike a balance between three essential objectives: seismic safety, protection of built heritage, and bringing the building up to current standards of operation and energy efficiency. We are not just reinforcing a structure, we are protecting a place that is part of Bucharest's cultural and academic memory. For AMCCRS, the signing of the contract marks the beginning of a stage in which our responsibility is to ensure the investment is implemented rigorously, respecting quality, deadlines and the building's architectural value." said Răzvan Munteanu, Executive Director of the Municipal Administration for the Consolidation of Buildings at Seismic Risk.

"This is a special project, not only because of its technical complexity, but also because of the building's architectural and cultural significance, for students, professors, actors, theatre lovers and the Bucharest community, as a whole. Our mission is to bring it up to modern standards of safety and energy efficiency while preserving its identity. Concelex's experience with integrated solutions, as well as with similar projects, gives us the tools we need to manage a project of this scale." said Cătălin Vișan, Deputy CEO, Concelex.

The project aims to achieve seismic reinforcement as well as improved energy efficiency, with a contract value of 98.6 million lei. Up to 90% of the funding comes from the National Program for the Consolidation of Buildings at High Seismic Risk, financed by the Ministry of Development, Public Works and Administration, and implementation is carried out by the Municipality of Bucharest through the Municipal Administration for the Consolidation of Buildings at Seismic Risk. The intervention seeks not only to secure a building at seismic risk class RsI, but also to preserve its architectural and cultural value and adapt it to current requirements for operation, safety and energy efficiency.

The project adds to a broad portfolio of reinforcement works; among the historic buildings Concelex has rehabilitated or has under way are the Mihai Eminescu building of the Bucharest University of Economic Studies, the Bacău Administrative Palace, the National Bank of Romania (BNR) branch in Galați, and Buildings A and B of the interwar building at 2 Boteanu Street. The company has also recently won the reinforcement project for the Dacia-România Palace (Pinacoteca).



The building on Schitu Măgureanu has a total floor area of over 11,800 sqm and involves a complex intervention: structural reinforcement, repair and restoration of architectural elements and artistic components, modernization of building systems, and the introduction of fire safety solutions. In addition, the works will cover thermal insulation, waterproofing, window and door replacement, and the installation of energy-efficient equipment, with an impact on energy consumption and greenhouse gas emissions. The project also involves partial demolitions, ground improvement works for the foundation, as well as utility connections and disconnections.



Through an integrated approach to the intervention, structural reinforcement, restoration, modernization of building systems and improved energy performance, the Municipality of Bucharest and AMCCRS aim for the investment to generate long-term benefits, both in terms of user safety and in terms of heritage preservation and reduced building operating costs.



Located at the intersection of Schitu Măgureanu Boulevard and Calea Plevnei, the building is one of the most important architectural landmarks of the Cișmigiu area, with a 100-year history. The complex was built in stages, with construction of the main building beginning in 1926 as the Palace of the League for the Cultural Unity of Romanians. Between 1950 and 1977, it housed the Institute of Theatrical and Cinematographic Art, and today it serves the "Lucia Sturdza Bulandra" Municipal Theatre and the University of Bucharest, with lecture halls, amphitheatre, library, archive and offices.
