World.title: Interior minister: Estonia's crisis preparedness not entirely in line with threats
World.content:
The Ministry of the Interior tasks police, the Internal Security Service (ISS) and the Rescue Board with presenting annual recommendations in the field of internal security.

Interior Minister Igor Taro (Eesti 200) said the new internal security recommendations the three agencies will be required to present annually are a logical complement to the military advice provided by the commander of the Estonian Defense Forces, which outlines what the state must do and what the military needs to win a war if one occurs.

"Our crisis preparedness still does not fully match the security threats facing Estonia," Taro said. He added that while the current threats are nonmilitary, their impact on Estonia's security is significant.

ISS/KAPO Director General Margo Palloson said Russia's hostile activities will remain the greatest threat over the next three years. He said hybrid activity is currently the primary concern.

According to Palloson, threats are becoming increasingly digital. Risks related to cyberattacks and cyberespionage are growing and Estonia must also be prepared for an escalation in sabotage.

Palloson said the threat posed by Russia could increase if the war in Ukraine comes to a halt, as Russia could then have more resources available for activities directed against Europe and Estonia.

To strengthen the ISS, Palloson said it is necessary to expand technological capabilities, place greater emphasis on prevention, find a comprehensive solution to the issues surrounding the retention and use of communications data and pass a background check law to allow basic vetting of people entering critical positions.

ISS Director Margo Palloson. Source: ERR

Police and Border Guard Board Director General Egert Belitšev said the agency has enough funding to cover its day-to-day operations but lacks resources for development. He added that the Police and Border Guard Board currently does not have sufficient resources to address all internal security threats.

"We are in a situation where we have enough money to pay this year's bills. We do not have the funding needed to carry out the necessary development projects," Belitšev said. He said his main recommendation for improving internal security is to provide the agency with stable, long-term funding.

Belitšev said this includes funding for crisis reserves, drone surveillance and counter-drone capabilities, as well as the capabilities of specialized units. "These are critical issues that require action today," he said.

The Police and Border Guard Board wants to develop its crisis reserve because personnel shortages are likely to be the first problem in a crisis. Belitšev said long-term funding is needed for a 1,000-member police crisis reserve. He also called for expanding special operations and rapid response capabilities, ensuring aviation capabilities and establishing an effective investigative framework and the necessary legal framework for investigating modern large-scale crimes.

The Police and Border Guard Board also considers the creation of a nationwide drone surveillance network a priority. Belitšev said Estonia needs the capability to distinguish dangerous drones from ordinary aircraft and to ensure it can neutralize hostile drones.

Rescue Board Director General Margo Klaos said one-third of the agency's rescue stations are understaffed. "Life-saving capability must be ensured across Estonia," Klaos said. He added that Estonia must be prepared for natural disasters, industrial accidents, sabotage and a possible military crisis.

Egert Belitšev and Margo Klaos. Source: Priit Mürk/Siim Lõvi/ERR

The Rescue Board also considers improving public crisis preparedness to be essential. The agency has sufficient resources to provide crisis training and public awareness activities through the end of 2027, but Klaos said efforts to improve public preparedness must continue after that.

Klaos said additional resources are needed to adapt, for example, the basements of apartment buildings to protect residents in the event of a military attack.

The Rescue Board also said a 1,500-member crisis reserve should be established and that volunteer rescue services should receive stronger funding than they do now.

The heads of all three agencies emphasized that implementing these development projects will require more reliable, long-term funding. Project-based financing makes it more difficult to prepare for crises.

On Wednesday, Interior Minister Taro, Police and Border Guard Board Director General Belitšev, ISS Director General Palloson and Rescue Board Director General Klaos presented the internal security recommendations of the three agencies at a press conference.

World.title: Analysis: Ida-Viru County residents' expectations for the future
World.content:
Nearly half of young people in Ida-Viru County plan to leave in search of better education and employment opportunities. According to researchers, the outflow could be slowed by a well-designed starter package that seamlessly links vocational education, a first job and access to independent housing.

At the beginning of this year, social scientists from the University of Tartu led a large-scale survey of Ida-Viru County residents to gain insight into people's expectations for the future and their concerns. Below, we highlight several issues that are important for shaping the county's future and that political parties hoping to appeal to local voters in the upcoming elections should keep in mind.

The survey, conducted at the start of the year and involving more than 1,200 respondents, provided a representative snapshot of the mood among Ida-Viru County residents. The findings confirmed that preserving a sense of normalcy and strengthening the region's ties with the rest of Estonia remain major challenges.

Many residents of Ida-Viru County feel that the changes of recent years have had a largely negative impact on their daily lives, undermining their confidence in future opportunities. While the media and the political arena are consumed by debates over ideology and who should serve as mayor, local people's concerns lie elsewhere. For example, there is a shortage of dentists and psychiatric care. In Ida-Viru County, the dividing lines in people's personal aspirations and attitudes toward change do not run solely along language or ethnic lines and appealing only to "one's own side" is not enough.

As Estonia finalizes its national plan for the European Union's new budget period and prepares for the upcoming Riigikogu elections, it is also necessary to ask uncomfortable questions. How can policymakers reach people who are uncertain whether to remain in their home region and have not yet decided whether to stay or leave? What specific forms of engagement and dialogue can reduce polarization and increase trust? How can policymakers avoid a situation in which treating Ida-Viru County primarily through the lens of security policy creates more "internal outsiders" and deepens the divide between "us" and "them"? What decisions and measures can reduce the vulnerability of local communities when the region is affected by external shocks?

Drawing on the survey findings, we examine several issues below that have received less attention than jobs, industrial investment and the transition to Estonian-language education. We also offer recommendations for policymakers and local community leaders.

The principle of health in all policies

Between 2004 and 2022, self-rated health improved among people in Estonia, including residents of Ida-Viru County. However, an analysis of data from the Estonian Health Behavior Survey of the Adult Population shows that income and employment inequality have increased significantly across the country. Both factors strongly influence how people assess their own health. The situation is further compounded by the survey finding that one-quarter of Ida-Viru County residents have generalized anxiety disorder. Nearly half experience mild anxiety, while one-quarter of survey respondents are predisposed to moderate depression.

The economic and social changes associated with the transition can create uncertainty that adversely affects both mental and physical health. For example, the restructuring of the 1990s had a dramatic impact on the health of people in Estonia. Life expectancy for both men and women fell by several years, with those having lower levels of education suffering the most. Those mistakes must not be repeated in Ida-Viru County today.

Hermann Castle, or Narva Castle, is home of Narva Museum. Source: Narva Muuseum SA

In interviews, healthcare experts identified limited access to mental health services — especially those for children — and dental care as particularly serious problems. They also pointed to residents' low level of health literacy and limited capacity for self-management. The experts emphasized that health promotion efforts must be adapted to the local language and culture.

These shortcomings can be addressed through a strong healthcare system focused on prevention. Above all, access to mental health care must be improved and the stigma associated with seeking help must be reduced, as it can discourage people from using these services. More mental health professionals are needed. They must be trained more quickly and supported in every possible way so that these services are available to those who need them.

Alongside retraining and employment programs in Ida-Viru County, health and mental well-being counseling should also be offered. Because people's health is closely linked to their income and employment, efforts should also focus on improving residents' socioeconomic conditions and reducing uncertainty. Adopting a "Health in All Policies" approach would encourage policymakers to systematically assess the health impacts of all major regional development and transition policy decisions.

Starter package for young people

Recent survey data shows that young people in Ida-Viru County are voting with their feet. Nearly one in two residents ages 18 to 24 plans to seek opportunities elsewhere. This likely reflects a belief that other places offer better prospects for education, employment and starting an independent life. For young people in Ida-Viru County, it also matters in what linguistic, cultural and value-based environment those opportunities exist and what the future holds for the county itself.

What can be done to reduce youth outmigration or at least ensure that those who currently plan to stay actually do so? Young people need a coherent local education-to-employment pathway that integrates vocational or higher education, internships, a first job, counseling and long-term career prospects. It is also important to expand preparatory and remedial education to improve not only language skills but also other essential knowledge and competencies. A first job and affordable housing should be combined into a single starter package. In addition, young people need a vibrant public space that supports initiative, culture and opportunities for self-fulfillment.

Local governments, the state and employers must jointly determine how to provide comprehensive support for young people in Ida-Viru County as they begin independent adult lives and what tools should be used to achieve that goal.

Fragile communities in need of spokespeople

Experience to date shows that community-led initiatives in Ida-Viru County are more fragile than elsewhere in Estonia. At the same time, the survey indicates that people there are willing to help one another. More than half of residents have voluntarily and spontaneously helped neighbors or other members of their community.

However, only about half as many people participate in organized volunteer work or civic organizations. This suggests that people's willingness to support one another does not often develop into sustained collective action. One of Ida-Viru County's distinguishing characteristics is its internal diversity: levels of civic engagement, trust and the challenges communities face vary considerably across different parts of the county.

Kohtla-Järve Cultural Center. Source: Dmitri Fedotkin/ERR

To turn informal mutual assistance into organized community action, support must be provided to those willing to initiate and lead such efforts. Ida-Viru County has relatively few experienced community leaders and those who do exist are often overstretched. New leaders are discouraged by the significant responsibility that comes with project-based funding, as unsuccessful projects can result in financial liabilities. For that reason, new initiatives need low-risk seed funding and simple microgrants that do not carry the threat of repayment if a project falls short. More stable, long-term support is also needed to retain community leaders and develop the next generation of local organizers.

Dignified work and study

Two-thirds of Ida-Viru County residents believe that the ongoing economic changes will worsen their chances of finding suitable employment in the future. At the same time, most people who are currently employed are satisfied with their jobs.

In the eyes of Ida-Viru County residents, a good, dignified job is defined above all by security. That means confidence that one's job will remain stable, colleagues will be supportive and the work itself will not endanger one's health. Having a say in how work is organized and maintaining a healthy work-life balance are also important. In other words, people are not motivated to devote time and effort to learning new skills simply for the sake of any job or retraining program. What motivates them is the prospect of securing a stable, dignified job.

Systematic mentoring can help strengthen the sense of security surrounding a current or future job. Support should be provided for instructors and educational programs that allow people to study while working. Employers should also be encouraged to value lifelong learning, for example by linking eligibility for support measures to employee training.

The University of Tartu's Narva College. Source: Sergei Stepanov/ERR

Our previous research shows that employers in the region tend to be skeptical about long-term training for their employees. One-third expect workers who are already employed to find the time and resources to improve their skills on their own. Only then are they willing to discuss promotions and pay raises. Supporting entrepreneurship is another promising approach, as it allows people to create jobs that suit their own needs. Interest in entrepreneurship is also considerable in the region.

Interest in entrepreneurship

According to the survey, about 13 percent of Ida-Viru County's working-age population is currently engaged in entrepreneurship, including as sole proprietors. Interest, however, is much higher: One-third of residents ages 18 to 34 and one-sixth of those ages 35 to 54 plan to start a business. To do so, they primarily need suitable premises and training.

Most respondents did not yet have a clearly defined business idea. Instead, they wanted the opportunity to explore what might be a good fit and what could find a market. For example, many respondents repeatedly mentioned social services as a potential field. A region with an aging population has growing demand for a wide range of services, meaning there are market niches to be filled. According to the survey, many young people would also like to start businesses in engineering. Combining engineering education with entrepreneurial experience could therefore provide young people with additional motivation.

Ida-Viru Country as a critical case of Estonia's balanced development

For many years, Ida-Viru County was perceived as an internal outsider that could simply be ignored. The investments and attention brought by the Just Transition Fund (JTF) put the county back in the spotlight. This time, however, it was not because it was seen as unusual or problematic, but because of its untapped development potential.

The fund directed substantial investment into businesses. Universities launched new academic programs and a number of research groups began work with the aim of strengthening the local innovation ecosystem. Regional initiatives also supported community activities with millions of euros in funding. The benefits of such efforts are long-term. Completing a university degree takes three to five years, while developing new technologies requires even more time. Although the JTF initiated many important developments, one question remains: What happens when the funding ends?

As work proceeds on Estonia's new national plan, there are signs that the special attention paid to Ida-Viru County will also fade once the JTF funding period comes to an end. The proposed "polycentric Estonia" initiative aims to direct more investment outside Harju County. That objective is, in itself, commendable.

Rüütli bog in Alutaguse National Park, Ida-Viru County. Source: Rene Kundla/ERR

At the same time, the discussion increasingly suggests that there are struggling peripheral regions elsewhere in Estonia as well and that there is nothing particularly unique about Ida-Viru County. It is true that Valga, Võru and Hiiu counties — as well as every other county in Estonia — deserve care and attention. Even so, Ida-Viru County's distinctiveness extends well beyond differences in language and culture. It also encompasses the region's unique socioeconomic characteristics.

Investing in Ida-Viru County's diversity and social resilience strengthens the resilience of Estonia as a whole, much like reinforcing a critical link in a chain makes the entire chain stronger. A vision of the region's industrial future in which only a handful of factories are built and forced to recruit workers from abroad because efforts to develop the local workforce have failed is uncomfortably reminiscent of what happened in the 1950s.

If the region is supported and developed strategically, the benefits will extend to all of Estonia. Directing additional resources to Ida-Viru County and other areas along the country's eastern border would create added value for the entire nation by increasing its resilience and capacity to withstand crises.

World.title: US dollar slightly rises against Iraqi dinar
World.content:
Baghdad (IraqiNews.com) – The exchange rate for the US dollar compared to the Iraqi dinar rose on Wednesday in the Iraqi capital, Baghdad, and the capital of the Kurdistan region of Iraq, Erbil.

The US dollar exchange rate slightly rose in Baghdad’s al-Kifah and al-Harithiya stock exchanges, reaching 1,521.5 Iraqi dinars compared to 1,519.5 Iraqi dinars on Wednesday morning.

The exchange rate in currency exchange shops in Baghdad ranged between 1,525 Iraqi dinars and 1,515 Iraqi dinars, Shafaq News reported.

In Erbil, the US dollar exchange rate also rose, fluctuating between 1,524 and 1,523.5 Iraqi dinars.

The Central Bank of Iraq (CBI) said in February 2023 that it has begun using the new US dollar exchange rate of 1,300 dinars to every US dollar.

The previous official exchange rate was 1,450 dinars to one US dollar, which was being exchanged in the parallel market at a rate of 1,550 dinars.

While the official exchange rate was 1,450 dinars per dollar in January 2023, the US currency was being exchanged at 1,610 dinars during the same month in the parallel market in Iraq. This variation indicated a difference of over 10 percent in the exchange rates.

World.title: Iraq, Jordan, Egypt discuss cooperation mechanism, energy partnerships
World.content:
Baghdad (IraqiNews.com) – Iraq, Jordan, and Egypt highlighted on Wednesday the importance of activating the trilateral cooperation mechanism via specialized committees and enhancing coordination in the economic, investment, industrial, and energy sectors.

Iraqi Foreign Minister Fuad Hussein, Jordanian Foreign Minister Ayman Safadi, and Egyptian Foreign Minister Badr Abdelatty met in Amman, the capital of Jordan, to discuss the trilateral cooperation mechanism.

The meeting was held on the sidelines of the foreign ministers’ participation in the Arab ministerial meeting on Jerusalem, according to a statement released by the Iraqi Foreign Ministry.

The three parties agreed to activate the tripartite system through specialized technical committees and organize periodic discussions at various levels to monitor the progress of joint projects.

The three ministers reviewed cooperation in the energy sector, including oil and electricity interconnection projects, as well as measures to broaden partnerships in these areas to enhance economic integration and improve energy security.

The meeting addressed the latest developments in the region, particularly efforts to reopen the Strait of Hormuz to strengthen regional stability.

The foreign ministers highlighted the need to halt military operations, reduce tensions, and adopt diplomatic means to resolve crises in the region.

World.title: Graham Arnold extends Iraq contract ahead of Gulf Cup and AFC Asian Cup 2027
World.content:
Baghdad (IraqiNews.com) – Iraq national team head coach Graham Arnold has officially signed a contract extension with the Iraq Football Association (IFA), ensuring he will remain in charge of the Lions of Mesopotamia for the country’s upcoming major international tournaments.

The renewal secures Arnold’s position on the sidelines as Iraq prepares for the Gulf Cup and the 2027 AFC Asian Cup, providing continuity as the national team continues its long-term development.

According to a source within the Iraq Football Association, Arnold finalized the agreement on Wednesday, extending his tenure as head coach of the Iraqi national football team.

The new deal confirms that the Australian manager will oversee Iraq’s preparations and participation in the upcoming Gulf Cup before leading the team into the AFC Asian Cup 2027.

The contract extension reflects the federation’s confidence in Arnold’s leadership and its desire to maintain stability ahead of two of the region’s most important football competitions.

Keeping the same coaching staff allows Iraq to continue building tactical consistency, squad cohesion, and long-term planning without interruption.

The upcoming Gulf Cup will provide valuable competitive experience before the national team shifts its focus to the AFC Asian Cup, where Iraq will aim to compete for continental honors.

Coaching continuity is considered an important factor in international football, particularly as teams prepare for major tournaments.

By extending Arnold’s contract, the Iraq Football Association signals its commitment to maintaining the current technical project while continuing preparations for future regional and Asian competitions.

Further details regarding the duration and financial terms of the renewed agreement have not yet been officially disclosed.

World.title: Iraq, Jordan, and Egypt agree to boost trilateral cooperation
World.content:
Amman (IraqiNews.com) – Iraq, Jordan, and Egypt have reaffirmed their commitment to strengthening trilateral cooperation by activating specialized technical committees and expanding coordination across key economic sectors, including investment, industry, and energy.

The agreement was reached during a trilateral ministerial meeting held in Amman, where the three countries also discussed regional developments, the situation in the Strait of Hormuz, and the importance of diplomatic efforts to reduce tensions across the Middle East.

According to a statement from Iraq’s Ministry of Foreign Affairs, Iraqi Foreign Minister Fuad Hussein participated in the meeting alongside Jordanian Deputy Prime Minister and Foreign Minister Ayman Safadi and Egyptian Foreign Minister Badr Abdelatty.

The meeting took place ahead of the Arab ministerial meeting on Jerusalem and focused on accelerating implementation of the Iraq-Jordan-Egypt cooperation mechanism.

The ministers agreed to activate the partnership through specialized technical committees and hold regular meetings at various levels to monitor the progress of joint initiatives.

The three countries emphasized expanding cooperation in strategic sectors that support long-term economic growth.

Discussions focused on increasing collaboration in:

Economic development

Investment projects

Industrial cooperation

Trade facilitation

Infrastructure development

Officials said stronger coordination would help deepen regional economic integration while creating new opportunities for sustainable growth.

Energy cooperation was a central topic during the talks, with ministers reviewing ongoing and future projects involving:

Oil cooperation

Electricity interconnection

Regional energy security

Cross-border energy infrastructure

The three governments stressed that expanding joint energy initiatives would contribute to improving energy security and strengthening economic ties between Iraq, Jordan, and Egypt.

The ministers also exchanged views on regional developments, particularly the situation surrounding the Strait of Hormuz.

They welcomed ongoing efforts aimed at reopening the strategic waterway as quickly as possible, highlighting its importance for regional stability, international trade, and global energy markets.

The meeting concluded with a joint call for an end to military escalation across the region, emphasizing that dialogue and diplomatic engagement remain the most effective means of resolving regional crises.

The ministers reiterated their shared commitment to peaceful solutions and closer regional cooperation in addressing common political and economic challenges.

World.title: Al Qaim Cement Plant expands exports to Syria
World.content:
Baghdad (IraqiNews.com) – Iraq’s Al-Qaim Cement Plant has reached its full designed production capacity of 840,000 tonnes annually, strengthening domestic cement supplies while increasing exports to neighboring Syria, the Ministry of Industry and Minerals announced on Wednesday.

The achievement marks a significant milestone in Iraq’s efforts to boost local industrial production, reduce reliance on imports, and expand the country’s non-oil exports.

According to the ministry, the Al-Qaim Cement Plant is now operating at its full design capacity, producing approximately 70,000 tonnes of sulfate-resistant cement each month.

The output is sufficient to meet demand across Anbar Province and other Iraqi governorates while supporting the government’s strategy to enhance domestic industrial self-sufficiency.

In addition to serving the local market, the plant currently exports around 7,500 tonnes of cement per month to Syria, reflecting growing cross-border trade and regional demand for Iraqi construction materials.

General Company for Iraqi Cement Director General Zuhair Dawood Ahmed said the facility is operated through a partnership with Al-Maysarah Cement Industry Company.

He explained that the plant features a fully modernized production line equipped with advanced machinery and internationally sourced equipment, alongside a modern centralized control system that manages production processes efficiently.

The factory also includes advanced laboratories for testing both raw materials and finished products, ensuring quality standards are maintained throughout the manufacturing process.

To ensure uninterrupted production, the Al-Qaim Cement Plant operates its own 30-megawatt power station, providing stable electricity independent of the national grid.

This dedicated energy supply enables the plant to maintain around-the-clock production, minimizing operational disruptions and supporting consistent output.

Officials said continuous operations are essential to meeting domestic demand while expanding Iraq’s presence in regional cement markets.

The Ministry of Industry said increasing production at state-owned industrial facilities remains a key objective in supporting economic diversification beyond the oil sector.

By achieving full operational capacity and maintaining exports, the Al-Qaim Cement Plant contributes to strengthening Iraq’s manufacturing base, creating greater industrial resilience, and expanding opportunities for Iraqi products in foreign markets.

The ministry added that efforts will continue to increase cement exports while supporting the country’s infrastructure and construction sectors through reliable local production.

World.title: Iraq lawmakers scrutinize Karbala Refinery contracts amid government anti-corruption drive
World.content:
Baghdad (IraqiNews.com) – Iraqi lawmakers have begun reviewing government contracts suspected of containing inflated costs, as Prime Minister Ali Al-Zaidi intensifies efforts to tighten oversight of public spending and prevent corruption before contracts are approved.

The renewed scrutiny comes a day after Al-Zaidi ordered the Federal Board of Supreme Audit to establish a specialized team responsible for conducting pre-contract financial audits within 10 working days. The initiative aims to identify high costs before agreements are finalized, marking a shift from investigating corruption after it occurs to preventing it at the contracting stage.

MP Haider Mohammed Al-Mutairi, a member of the Ishraqat Kanoun bloc, called on the prime minister to review several contracts related to the Karbala Refinery, arguing that some agreements warrant immediate investigation due to their financial burden on the state.

Al-Mutairi urged the formation of a high-level investigative committee to examine a consultancy contract involving 49 advisers, claiming it costs the Iraqi government approximately $52 million annually.

He also highlighted an operational contract for the refinery valued at $180 million per year, which he said amounts to nearly 750 million Iraqi dinars in daily expenditures.

The MP called for greater transparency in reviewing major state contracts, particularly those involving strategic infrastructure projects.

The parliamentary review follows a broader government campaign to strengthen financial oversight across ministries and state institutions.

Prime Minister Al-Zaidi directed the Federal Board of Supreme Audit to implement mandatory pre-audit procedures for government contracts, including setting financial thresholds that determine which agreements require advance scrutiny.

According to the prime minister, inflated contract values and weak oversight have long been among the primary channels through which public funds were lost.

He stressed that Iraq’s next phase of anti-corruption efforts should focus on preventing irregularities before contracts are signed rather than relying solely on post-contract investigations.

The government says the new oversight framework is intended to improve transparency, accelerate contract reviews, and safeguard public finances without delaying legitimate development projects.

The initiative forms part of a wider reform agenda aimed at enhancing accountability, improving governance, and restoring confidence in public procurement procedures.

No official findings regarding the Karbala Refinery contracts have been announced, and any investigation would be subject to the legal and auditing procedures established by Iraqi authorities.

World.title: Iraq studies oil pipeline network to Turkey, Syria, Jordan
World.content:
Baghdad (IraqiNews.com) – The Iraqi Oil Ministry is working on diversifying oil export outlets by constructing a pipeline network that will be extended to ports in Turkey, Syria, and Jordan.

The spokesperson for the Iraqi Oil Ministry, Salim al-Rikabi, told the state-run Iraqi News Agency (INA) on Sunday that the government is studying the construction of the Basra-Haditha-Kirkuk-Ceyhan pipeline as a new route, with branches from Haditha to the Syrian port of Baniyas and the Jordanian port of Aqaba.

Fluctuations in the global oil market have a significant impact on Iraq’s revenue. However, the most significant impact is the decline in daily export volumes, which have been severely affected by the ongoing war in the region, according to al-Rikabi.

The current conflict in the region has led to the closure of the Strait of Hormuz, which is a strategically important waterway that transports the majority of Iraq’s oil shipments.

Al-Rikabi explained that the pipeline from southern Iraq to the port of Ceyhan on the Mediterranean will raise oil export volumes via Turkish territory.

The Iraqi official said earlier that the Basra-Haditha oil pipeline needs to be carried out first to transport crude oil to Haditha in the western province of Anbar, and then preparation for the alternate pipeline takes place.

The project’s feasibility study is presently underway, and if completed, the pipeline will serve as an alternative for oil tankers now transporting oil to the Syrian port of Baniyas.

The Iraqi cabinet decided in April to move forward with the implementation of the Basra-Haditha oil pipeline.

According to reports, the project is an Iraqi venture estimated at $4.6 billion aiming to transport crude oil from the southern Iraqi province of Basra to Haditha.

The pipeline’s capacity is projected to be approximately 2.25 million barrels per day using 56-inch diameter pipes. This design aims to enhance domestic transportation and establish connections to future export facilities.

The pipeline will be 685 kilometers long and will serve as the initial phase in the construction of a pipeline network that might eventually extend to Jordan and Syria.

The state-owned Basra Oil Company (BOC) and State Company for Oil Projects (SCOP) are building the project, which is funded by the Iraq-China Framework Agreement.

The pipeline provides a direct path to both the Mediterranean and the Red Sea and, subsequently, to European markets.

Once completed, the project will improve flexibility, as Iraq studies alternative routes to its present seaports to expand export capacity.

World.title: Iraq in talks with Iran to facilitate vessel transit through Hormuz
World.content:
Baghdad (IraqiNews.com) – Iraqi Oil Minister Basim Khudair said on Tuesday that discussions are taking place with Iran regarding the transit of oil tankers via the Strait of Hormuz, with an anticipated agreement in the near future.

In a statement to the Iraqi News Agency (INA), Khudair stated that the economic and political discussions held during Prime Minister Ali al-Zaidi’s visit to Tehran addressed approaches to expand cooperation and resulted in signing several agreements.

The Iraqi delegation held talks with Iranian counterparts to ensure the safe transit of vessels across the Strait of Hormuz and protect oil shipments, according to Khudair.

The oil minister stressed that the policy of the Iraqi government is based on building communication channels and partnerships with neighboring countries to support the national economy.

The two parties’ discussions aim to avert future interruptions to Iraqi oil exports amid growing regional maritime concerns.

As Baghdad depends heavily on the Strait of Hormuz, it seeks to secure a deal for the safe passage of oil shipments through the waterway.

While Iran has previously shown a willingness to make exceptions for friendly or non-hostile neighbors, practical implementation and approval processes remain a primary focus of continuing discussions.

World.title: ‘Miles to go before I sleep...’: Omar gets poetic, says ‘wounds of Art 370 abrogation yet to heal’
World.content:
SRINAGAR/JAMMU: Striking a poetic note on the seventh anniversary of the abrogation of Article 370 and bifurcation of the state of Jammu & Kashmir into two Union Territories, chief minister Omar Abdullah invoked celebrated American poet Robert Lee Frost as he said the wounds caused by the move had still not healed, and vowed that âthe injustices done to us will be correctedâ.

â7 years, we havenât forgotten & we havenât reconciled far less accepted our current circumstances. My party & I remain committed to reversing all that was done to J&K that took away our rights & threatens our identity. âThe woods are lovely, dark & deep. But I have promises to keep. And miles to go before I sleepâ...â Omar said in a post on X, quoting from the poem âStopping by Woods on a Snowy Eveningâ by Frost, before he left for an inspection of flood-hit areas in Jammuâs Poonch district.

Speaking to reporters in Poonch, the CM said, âThe wounds of the abrogation are still there. We had hoped that at least some balm would be applied to those wounds and the promise of restoring statehood would be fulfilled...Seven years have passed, but the promise remains unfulfilled.â

Barring BJP, which celebrated the abrogation of Article 370, all major political parties in Kashmir held protests and demonstrations, carrying banners and raising slogans describing Aug 5, 2019, as a âblack dayâ.





However, security forces foiled attempts by various parties to take out marches in Srinagar.

Senior functionaries of governing NC and Congress remained absent from the protests held by their parties, which focused on seeking restoration of statehood. The PDP march was led by Iltija Mufti, who accused cops of manhandling her during Tuesdayâs attempted protest.

âItâs on this day we were caged like animals while a govt drunk on power stripped our state of its special status, flag, residuary powers and constitution.

Our peaceful fight for it will continue till the day we get every bit of it back,â Iltija said.

Lt governor Manoj Sinha, on the other hand, hailed the decision, saying it had âdismantled the terror ecosystem to a large extent, strengthened law and order, restored equal rights and created opportunities that allow families to rebuild their lives with confidenceâ. âThe transformation we witness today in J&K is due to the historic changes of Aug 5, 2019. That day marked a constitutional correction and a new beginning for the UT,â he said.

World.title: Terrorist hideout busted in Poonch, ammo seized; search ops launched in Jammu, Kathua
World.content:
Joint teams carried out cordon-and-search operations based on intelligence inputs about suspicious activity

Join conversation View All Comments â Share your thoughts in the comments Insightful Agree Disagree Skeptical Concerning Promising Worth Reading Big Development Post Comment Be respectful Â· TOI community guidelines

JAMMU: Security forces busted a terrorist hideout in a remote village in J&Kâs Poonch district, while joint teams carried out cordon-and-search operations in Jammuâs Akhnoor sector and Kathuaâs Hiranagar sector based on intelligence inputs about suspicious activity, officials said Wednesday.Officials said the hideout, set up in a cave, was unearthed during a joint search operation by the Armyâs Rashtriya Rifles and J&K Police in Bhoriwala dhok of Surankote tehsil on Wednesday morning. Troops seized two magazines of an AK assault rifle, 117 rounds of ammunition, and 17 rounds of 9mm pistol ammunition from the spot.Around 2pm Tuesday, a suspected Pakistani drone allegedly entered Indian airspace and was spotted hovering over the forward villages of Shukhmal, Devindera and Tapan in Bobiyan area of Kathuaâs Hiranagar sector. BSF personnel tried to shoot it down, but the UAV, flying at a high altitude, managed to return across the border. A subsequent search of the area did not yield anything suspicious, officials said.A joint team of CRPF and J&K Police conducted another search operation from Parshuram Temple to Jandi Nallah in Hiranagar as part of an area-domination exercise.Separately, the Army and J&K Police launched a combing operation in Sunail Panchayat area of Jammuâs Akhnoor sector after a resident reported suspicious movement Tuesday.Meanwhile, separate cordon-and-search operations launched Tuesday in two locations in J&Kâs Poonch district continued without any sighting or contact with terror suspects allegedly present in the area. Three suspects were allegedly seen near Gujjar Naar area, and four more were spotted close to Kherowali dhok in the remote Dhara Sangla village in Surankote sector.

World.title: Unelected Bihar minister Deepak Prakash nominated as MLC days after SC questions cabinet continuance
World.content:
NEW DELHI: Bihar minister Deepak Prakash was on Tuesday nominated to the state Legislative Council, days after the Supreme Court

his continuance in the cabinet without being a legislator.

According to a gazette notification, governor Lt Gen Syed Ata Hasnain (retd.) nominated Prakash to the vacant seat left by BJP MLC Devesh Kumar's resignation.

Prakash was first inducted into the then Nitish Kumar-led Bihar cabinet in November last year and was recently re-inducted into the BJP-led government headed by Samrat Choudhary. On both occasions, he was not a member of either House of the state legislature.

His father, Upendra Kushwaha, whose Rashtriya Lok Morcha is a constituent of the BJP-led ruling National Democratic Alliance (NDA), thanked the BJP leadership but insisted the nomination was unrelated to the court proceedings.

âI express my gratitude towards Prime Minister Narendra Modi, Union home minister Amit Shah and BJP national president Nitin Nabin. We shall work to take Bihar forward," Kushwaha told reporters, according to PTI.

Join conversation Commentsâ Share your thoughts in the comments Insightful Agree Disagree Skeptical Concerning Promising Worth Reading Big Development Post Comment Be respectful Â· TOI community guidelines





"People file petitions for all sorts of things. When Deepak Prakash had first become a minister, the NDA had in principle decided that he would be sent to the Legislative Council in due course," he added.

BJP sources, however, admitted Kumar had "sacrificed" his seat to accommodate Prakash. Kumar, whose tenure had less than a year left, resigned on July 31, saying it was a "voluntary decision".

Last week, while hearing a petition challenging Prakash's continuance as minister, the Supreme Court raised the "legal question" of "how long can you have an unelected minister".

Under constitutional rules, a person appointed as a minister must become a member of either House of the legislature within six months.

World.title: BJD opposes proposed nuclear plant in Odisha, warns of mass agitation
World.content:
The Biju Janata Dal (BJD) on Wednesday opposed the proposed setting up of a nuclear power plant in Odisha, alleging that the BJP government was putting public safety at risk to benefit private companies.

The party also warned of a statewide agitation if the project moved forward.

The criticism came days after a representative of a private company met Odisha deputy chief minister KV Singh Deo, who also holds the state's energy portfolio. According to the BJD, the company has proposed establishing a 3,000 MW nuclear power plant in Odisha.

Addressing a press conference, BJD senior general secretary Lekhashree Samantsinghar claimed that a nuclear power plant would pose a serious threat to the health and safety of people living in the state.

She accused the BJP's "double-engine government" of ignoring public welfare in favour of corporate interests.

"Whenever the subject of nuclear or atomic energy arises, it naturally creates fear in people's minds. In 1945, the nuclear bombings reduced the Japanese cities of Hiroshima and Nagasaki to ruins. In 1986, the Chernobyl Nuclear Power Plant suffered a catastrophic explosion, and in 2011, a similar disaster occurred at the Fukushima Nuclear Power Plant," she said.





Samantsinghar added that the consequences of those disasters were still being felt and argued that nuclear power carries significant risks to human life.

She further claimed that nuclear energy has traditionally remained under government control in most countries because of its strategic importance. However, she alleged that the BJP government was now changing that approach by opening the sector to private companies.

"However, under the BJP government, this long-standing principle is being altered by transferring nuclear energy into the hands of private companies. For its own interests, the BJP government is showing complete disregard for the lives and safety of the people of Odisha," she alleged.

The BJD leader also questioned the Centre's decision to amend rules governing the nuclear sector. She claimed that Parliament passed legislation in December 2025 allowing greater private participation, following which private companies began exploring projects in Odisha.

According to Samantsinghar, India currently has about 8.8 GW of government-owned nuclear power capacity, and increasing it to 100 GW by involving private players would be unsafe. She argued that sectors linked to national security should remain under government control.

Join conversation Commentsâ Share your thoughts in the comments Insightful Agree Disagree Skeptical Concerning Promising Worth Reading Big Development Post Comment Be respectful Â· TOI community guidelines

The opposition party also alleged that the Odisha government was acting on directions from the Centre rather than taking independent decisions.

"Since the formation of the BJP government in Odisha, the state government has been functioning under the directions of the Centre and is unable to take any independent decisions without instructions from Delhi. Acting on the directions of the central government, the state is determined to establish a nuclear power plant in Odisha by compromising the interests of the people," she alleged.

The BJD urged the state government to abandon the proposal, warning that it would launch a mass movement if the project went ahead.

"Otherwise, the Biju Janata Dal would launch a mass agitation to safeguard the interests of the people of the State," she told reporters. The Odisha government had not responded to the allegations at the time of filing the report.

World.title: NHRC summons Delhi police chief after failure to answer summon over CSAM content on Instagram
World.content:
NEW DELHI: The National Human Rights Commission has issued summons to the Delhi police commissioner to appear before it taking a serious view of a lack of response to its notice and later a reminder directing an investigation into allegations of paid s on Instagram (owned by Meta) promoting child sexual abuse material (CSAM).

The NHRC had sought an action taken report within 15 days but is still awaiting a reply.

The NHRCâs bench presided over by member Priyank Kanoongo in the summons issued on Wednesday has directed the police chief Anurag Kumar to appear in person before the commission on September 7 along with the reports and explanation for non-compliance. However, summons state that if the ATR is submitted by August 31, the personal appearance will not be required.

The commission in its July 8 notice had asked the Delhi Police to hold an inquiry as to whether âmandatory reportingâ provisions under Protection of Children from Sexual Offences Act have been invoked by Meta to inform the police in time and if any FIRs have been lodged after reports of CSAM on its platforms came to light.

Taking cognisance of media reports published by the BBC World Service, Kanoongo said in the notice that since the concerned office of the BBC in India is situated in Delhi, the Commission thought it to be appropriate to entrust the matter to Delhi Police for investigation.





In another notice dated Aug 3 addressed to secretary of the ministry of electronics and information technology and Metaâs director responsible for south Asia, the commission has highlighted that as per the complaint received from a non-profit organisation, it is stated that the complainant foundation received an anonymous complaint alleging the availability of certain online links on Meta platforms (Instagram/Facebook) that are pornographic in nature, age-inappropriate for children and may potentially contain CSAM.

Kanoongo has asked secretary MeitY and head of law enforcement of Meta Platforms to inquire into the allegations contained in the complaint and to submit ATRs within one week from the date of receipt of the notice.

World.title: With all eyes on delimitation & FCRA, Parliament monsoon session sinks deeper into deadlock
World.content:
NEW DELHI: Parliament remained paralysed for the 13th consecutive day on Wednesday as relentless protests by Opposition parties forced repeated adjournments in both Houses, even as the government pushed through key legislative business.

Amid the deadlock, efforts to break the impasse gathered pace with Parliamentary Affairs Minister

holding meetings with Lok Sabha leader of the opposition

and Union home minister

, while Prime Minister Narendra Modi separately met BJP MPs over breakfast.

Opposition marches to Parliament

Opposition MPs led by Rahul Gandhi and Priyanka Gandhi Vadra marched from Prerna Sthal to Makar Dwar, demanding accountability from Amit Shah over the alleged police action against CJP protesters on July 20.

They also raised the alleged Ram Temple donation embezzlement issue and other matters. Priyanka Gandhi said those responsible for ordering the alleged use of pellet guns, tear gas and lathi charges against students must be held accountable, asserting that "This is a democracy, not a dictatorship; it is not someone's royal court."

No special session

Rijiju dismissed speculation that the Monsoon Session could be extended or that a special session might be convened later this month.





He said there was no proposal before the government to either prolong the current session or hold a separate sitting in mid-August.

His clarification came amid continued disruptions that have prevented the Lok Sabha from completing Question Hour since the session began on July 20.

Despite the logjam, the Lok Sabha passed the Bankers' Books Evidence Bill, 2026, by voice vote without discussion after Opposition members refused to end their protest.

Rijiju accused Opposition parties of deliberately stalling the House despite time being allotted for debate. He also criticised the Congress, CPI and Samajwadi Party over their protests relating to the alleged Ram Temple donation theft, alleging they had disrespected Lord Ram through demonstrations inside the Parliament complex.

Rahul-Rijiju meet

In a significant political development, Rijiju met Rahul Gandhi in his Parliament office for nearly 50 minutes in what sources described as a confidence-building exercise aimed at ending the parliamentary deadlock.

Congress MP Priyanka Gandhi Vadra was present throughout the meeting, while Gaurav Gogoi and K C Venugopal joined later.

According to sources, discussions covered the proposed Delimitation Bill, the Foreign Contribution Regulation Act (FCRA) Bill and other contentious issues that have fuelled the ongoing standoff. It was Rijiju's second meeting with Rahul Gandhi in the past 10 days, signalling continued backchannel engagement between the government and the Opposition despite the public confrontation inside Parliament.

Amit Shah likley to speak on FCRA

Soon after meeting Rahul Gandhi, Rijiju met Amit Shah at Parliament House. Sources said the government is preparing to engage the Opposition on the proposed FCRA Bill and Shah is expected to address the issue in Parliament.

Rijiju is also expected to reach out to leaders of other Opposition parties, including Samajwadi Party chief Akhilesh Yadav, in an effort to build consensus and restore normal functioning of the House.

The proposed FCRA amendments have emerged as one of the key flashpoints of the session alongside the protests over NEET, police action against students and the Ram Temple donation controversy.

Derek blames govt disruption

Trinamool Congress leader Derek O'Brien accused the government of being responsible for the continued disruption in Parliament, alleging that Amit Shah's prolonged absence from the House had worsened the situation. O'Brien maintained that Opposition MPs continued to perform their parliamentary duties despite the protests by raising public issues through Zero Hour notices and starred questions.

He highlighted his own notices seeking national recognition of the 75th anniversary of Mother Teresa's Missionaries of Charity and raising concerns over the proposed FCRA Bill. TMC sources said the party had submitted more than 100 questions during the session on issues ranging from MGNREGA dues and manual scavenging to air pollution, bank frauds, the UDAN scheme and the Nirbhaya Fund.

PM meets BJP MPs

Prime Minister Narendra Modi hosted a breakfast meeting with 37 BJP MPs at his official residence as part of his regular outreach during Parliament sessions.

The gathering included MPs associated with the NDA as well as former AAP leaders who later joined the BJP. Senior BJP leaders Tarun Chugh, Vinod Tawde and party chief Nitin Nabin also attended.

Sources told news agency PTI said the Prime Minister shared personal experiences and discussed governance, parliamentary strategy and constituency feedback with the MPs. The interaction forms part of Modi's practice of meeting smaller groups of BJP parliamentarians during every session to strengthen coordination and receive direct feedback from lawmakers.

Bill on Supreme Court judges passed

Despite the disruptions, the Rajya Sabha passed the Supreme Court (Number of Judges) Amendment Bill, 2026, completing Parliament's approval of the legislation. The Bill raises the sanctioned strength of the Supreme Court from 34 to 38 judges, including the Chief Justice of India.

He said the expansion would improve disposal rates and help ensure quicker access to justice. Meghwal also highlighted the government's ongoing investment in expanding Supreme Court infrastructure and reiterated its commitment to judicial reforms and the independence of the judiciary.

World.title: 'No special session of Parliament': Govt on Women's Reservation and Delimitation Bills
World.content:
NEW DELHI:

The government on Wednesday rejected media reports claiming that Parliament would convene a three-day special session from August 16 to 18 to consider the Women's Reservation and Delimitation Bills.

"No proposal to extend the dates of the Parliament session and no special session from August 16 to 18 on Women's Reservation and Delimitation Bills," Union minister

told ANI.

The Monsoon Session of Parliament commenced on July 20 and will conclude on August 13.

Rijiju's announcement came on a day when he reportedly held a one-on-one meeting with Lok Sabha leader of opposition Rahul Gandhi in an effort to break the ongoing Parliament deadlock.

During the meeting, which lasted around 50 minutes, Rijiju is said to have discussed the possible reintroduction of the Delimitation and Women's Reservation Bills. However, Rahul Gandhi is not believed to have given any commitment on the proposals.

World.title: IMA threatens nationwide strike over Maharashtra move to register CCMP-trained Homeopaths
World.content:
IMA Headquarters termed the governmentâs August 3 Government Resolution (GR) âillegalâ.

NEW DELHI: The Indian Medical Association (IMA) has threatened a nationwide strike if the Maharashtra government does not withdraw its recent decision permitting registration of BHMS graduates (Homepathy) who have completed the Certificate Course in Modern Pharmacology (CCMP) with the Maharashtra Medical Council (MMC).In a letter to Maharashtra Chief Minister Devendra Fadnavis on Wednesday, IMA Headquarters termed the governmentâs August 3 Government Resolution (GR) âillegalâ and urged its immediate cancellation, arguing that it undermines medical education, violates established legal principles and poses a risk to public health.The controversy centres on the stateâs decision to allow CCMP-qualified BHMS doctors to register with the Maharashtra Medical Council. The IMA has objected both to the CCMP course and to what it calls âdual medical council registration.ââThe CCMP course has not been approved by the erstwhile Medical Council of India (MCI), the National Medical Commission (NMC), or the National Commission for Homoeopathy (NCH). Such a course cannot be considered valid and should be discontinued immediately,â the association said in its representation.The doctorsâ body also argued that allowing practitioners to hold registrations under two different medical councils is unprecedented in India and could mislead patients regarding a doctorâs qualifications and scope of practice.The IMA further pointed out that the issue is already pending before the Bombay high court in a petition challenging amendments to the Maharashtra Medical Council Act. It said the government should not proceed with registrations while the matter remains sub judice.Questioning the stateâs justification of addressing rural doctor shortages, the association claimed the circumstances have changed significantly since similar provisions were introduced over a decade ago.âThe Maharashtra government has already done away with the compulsory rural bond system for MBBS graduates because of the non-availability of vacant posts, indicating that there is no longer a shortage of qualified allopathic doctors,â the letter stated.The association also said equating MBBS graduates, who undergo years of full-time medical education, with CCMP-trained practitioners who complete a part-time course would be unfair to students pursuing modern medicine.Citing the Supreme Courtâs landmark judgment in Poonam Verma vs Ashwin Patel (1996), the IMA reiterated that practitioners registered in one recognised system of medicine cannot prescribe medicines or practise another system without recognised qualifications and valid registration in that system.The IMA warned that if the GR is not withdrawn and the CCMP course is not discontinued, it will call for a nationwide strike involving doctors of modern medicine, including medical students, resident doctors and interns across the country.Copies of the representation have also been sent to the Prime Minister, Union Home Minister, Union Health Minister and the Chairperson of the National Medical Commission.

World.title: ‘Wings of Will’ get-together programme held
World.content:
The 15th edition of Amar Seva Sangam’s ‘Wings of Will’ get-together programme, which brings together persons treated for spinal cord injuries, was held recently at its campus in Ayikudi in Tenkasi district.

According to a press release, the programme brings together persons with spinal cord injuries who received rehabilitation and vocational training at Amar Seva Sangam. The programme aimed to address the rehabilitation, healthcare, and social needs while providing a platform for mutual support and encouragement.

The special gathering was conducted on August 1, 2, and 3 at the campus. A total of 147 beneficiaries along with their family members participated in the programme. Free accommodation, food and other arrangements were made for all three days. Free diagnostic scan services were also arranged for the participants.

An awareness rally on spinal cord injury was flagged off at Courtallam. The entire programme was conducted under the leadership of Padma Shri awardee S. Ramakrishnan, Founder-President of Amar Seva Sangam, and S. Sankara Raman, promoter co-chairman.

World.title: Ukraine accuses Russia of war crime after video shows drone attacking vegetable seller in Kherson
World.content:
Ukraine on Tuesday (August 4, 2026) accused Russia of committing a war crime after a ​video was released showing a drone chasing down and wounding a vegetable seller in ⁠the southern Ukrainian city of Kherson.

Footage released by Ukrainian police shows the drone pursuing a man around a van being used as a street stand before exploding as he dives for cover behind the vehicle. Police said the man in his ‌50s survived but suffered shock and shrapnel injuries.

Ukrainian officials later identified him only as a 52-year-old called Yurii and released a video interview with him from a hospital ward.

Click here to view the video posted by Mr. Zelenskyy. Trigger warning: The visuals may be disturbing to some people. Please avoid if you are distressed by violence

“Today, many ‌were shocked by yet another video of the drone ‘safari’ Russians are carrying out against civilians ‌in Kherson,” ⁠President Volodymyr Zelenskyy wrote on X, saying that “Russia has gone mad” and calling ⁠for more pressure on Moscow and strong security guarantees for Ukraine.

“We must act and support life in ways that force Russia to think seriously about peace rather than expanding the range of its drones.”

Reuters verified the location using buildings, the road layout and vegetation ​that matched satellite and archive imagery. The date ‌could not be independently confirmed, but Ukraine’s police and Foreign Minister Andrii Sybiha said the incident happened on Tuesday (August 4, 2026).

Russia’s Defence Ministry did not immediately respond to Reuters request for comment on the incident.

‘It was terryfying’

The vegetable seller went to Kherson in the morning to sell produce, said Oleksandr Prokudin, head ‌of the Kherson regional military administration. Prokudin released the video interview with the man on the Telegram ​app.

“I only just put up the umbrella and started unloading the boxes. My wife was there, too. Then we heard it buzzing but could not even see it. ⁠It came from somewhere behind the market, from those bushes over there, and flew in very low,” said Yurii, sitting in a hospital ward.

“It is open steppe. There is nowhere to go. It is terrifying, of course. ‌Really terrifying.”

On the video, Yurii showed his wounds on both legs and also on his back. His wife ran off and was not injured, he said.

Mr. Sybiha said the attack formed part of a deliberate Russian campaign to intimidate civilians. “This barbaric Russian war crime in Kherson demands international condemnation and justice, but thousands of similar crimes never come to the public eye,” he wrote on Telegram. In July, the U.N. Human Rights Monitoring Mission in Ukraine said it had documented 1,396 civilian deaths and 7,978 injuries in the first six ‌months of 2026, marking a 37% increase from 2025 and more than double the figures from 2024.

It said that the ​surge in civilian casualties was primarily driven by intensifying Russian long-range missile and drone strikes targeting cities far from the front lines.

Ukraine is also attacking Russia with drones and ⁠long-range missiles, many of which have caused civilian casualties, Russian authorities say. Russia on Monday (August 3, 2026) accused Ukraine of terrorism after ⁠seven people, including three children, were killed at its Black Sea holiday resort of Gelendzhik in what it said was a deliberate Ukrainian drone attack on civilians.

A Ukrainian official said that the ‌drone only fell on the beach in Gelendzhik because it was shot down by Russian air defences, adding that “Ukraine uses its weapons exclusively against the Russian military-industrial complex and economic infrastructure facilities”.

Both Russia and Ukraine ​deny targeting civilians in the war triggered by Russia’s invasion of Ukraine in February 2022.

World.title: Law college, river projects, welfare schemes: Budget unveils plans for Madurai
World.content:
The Tamil Nadu government has presented its Revised Budget highlights for 2026–27, bringing a series of direct infrastructure, educational, and environmental announcements for Madurai alongside major State-wide welfare initiatives.

Leading the direct allocations for the temple city is the establishment of a new special government law college in Madurai, scheduled to open its doors in the 2027–28 academic year with an initial intake of 300 students.

Environmental and tourism development also takes center stage, backed by a significant financial push.

To tackle ecological concerns, an allocation of ₹25 crore has been made for a feasibility study and the preparation of a Detailed Project Report aimed at controlling pollution in Cauvery, Vaigai, and Tamirabharani Rivers.

A total of ₹53 crore has been earmarked for river tourism development across Cauvery, Vaigai, and Tamirabharani River basins to boost regional tourism.

Further, the district stands to gain from broader developmental rollouts, including the creation of 10 Olympic special training centers and the deployment of 1,000 mobile geriatric care centers across Tamil Nadu.

World.title: Bihar Governor appoints Upendra Kushwaha’s son Deepak Prakash as MLC
World.content:
Bihar Governor Lieutenant-General (Retd) Syed Ata Hasnain on August 5, 2026 nominated Deepak Prakash to the Bihar Legislative Council to fill the vacancy following the resignation of nominated member Devesh Kumar on July 31, 2026. Mr. Prakash is the son of Rashtriya Lok Morcha (RLM) president and Rajya Sabha member Upendra Kushwaha, an ally in the National Democratic Alliance (NDA).

On July 30, 2026, the Supreme Court, while hearing a petition, had asked the Bihar Government how Mr. Prakash, an unelected Minister, could hold the position even six months after assuming office. Following this, Bharatiya Janata Party (BJP) MLC Mr. Kumar resigned, making way for Mr. Prakash’s appointment as MLC.

Mr. Prakash, 36, has been the State’s Panchayati Raj Minister since November 20, 2025 without being a member of either House of the State Legislature. Even after the BJP’s Samrat Choudhary replaced Mr. Nitish Kumar as the Bihar Chief Minister on April 15, 2026, and Mr. Choudhary expanded his Cabinet on May 7, 2026, Mr. Prakash remained the State Panchayati Raj Minister.

On May 30, 2026, a petition was filed in the Supreme Court by one Rakesh Kumar Singh seeking the invalidation of Mr. Prakash’s appointment as Minister as a “fraud upon the Constitution”. Article 164 (4) of the Constitution grants Ministers a period of six months to get elected to either House after being appointed a Minister.

Mr. Kushwaha expressed his gratitude upon his son’s nomination in a post on social media platform X. “I express my heartfelt gratitude to the nation’s Prime Minister Narendra Modi, Union Home Minister Amit Shah, JD(U) (Janata Dal-United) national president Nitish Kumar, BJP national resident Nitin Nabin, Bihar Chief Minister Samrat Choudhary, LJP (Lok Janshakti Party) (Ram Vilas) national president Chirag Paswan, and Union Minister Jitan Ram Manjhi for nominating Deepak Prakash — a youth leader of the RLM and Bihar’s Minister of Panchayati Raj — as a member of the Bihar Legislative Council,” Mr. Upendra Kushwaha said.

“I am fully confident that Deepak Prakash will further strengthen the development of Bihar and the interests of its people with complete dedication and a spirit of public service,” he added.

Mr. Prakash, an engineering graduate, entered politics as a member of the RLM in 2025, and was appointed as Minister of Panchayati Raj by the then CM Mr. Nitish Kumar. His mother, Snehlata Kushwaha, is the RLM MLA from the Sasaram Assembly constituency in Rohtas district.

World.title: Two persons murdered in Madurai
World.content:
Two persons were murdered in separate incidents under Madurai City Police limits since Tuesday night.

In the first incident, one ‘Crime’ Mani, who was a noted property crime suspect, was found murdered under Jaihindpuram police station limits around Tuesday midnight.

The police said the deceased, along with one more person, was intercepted by a night patrol police team, when the two were riding a bike around 11 p.m. Since the duo were drunk, the police did not take them to the police station.

The police seized Mani’s motorbike and mobile phone and asked them to report at Jaihindpuram police station the next morning.

However, within a few minutes Mani was murdered by some unidentified persons who used a boulder for the crime, the police said.

Jaihindpuram police are investigating.

In the other incident, a history-sheeter, Murugan, was hacked to death by an armed gang in Chintamani on Wednesday afternoon.

When Murugan was standing near his house at Kannan Colony, he noticed some strangers around and tried to take refuge in his house. However, they chased him and attacked him with lethal weapons, killing him on the spot.

The police suspect it to be a revenge murder. Chintamani police have registered a case.

World.title: Road rage controversy: Karnataka High Court transfers Malur judge to Humnabad
World.content:
The High Court of Karnataka on Wednesday transferred Gayathri, Principal Civil Judge and JMFC, Malur in Kolar district, to Humnabad in Bidar district, citing “administrative reasons and in the interest of public service”.

The transfer comes on the heels of her alleged conduct in a road rage case involving her private car in Malur, a video of which went viral on social media. After registering a complaint against a youth, his mother and grandmother, she herself passed a judicial order permitting the jurisdictional police to delete from social media the viral videos containing a squabble involving her, her husband, the youth and his family members.

As the youth and his family filed a petition challenging the First Information Report (FIR) registered on the basis of her complaint, a single-judge Bench of the High Court last week stayed the FIR and made scathing remarks against her for acting as “a judge in her own cause” by adjudicating proceedings in the criminal case initiated on her complaint. The single judge also directed that the matter be placed before the Chief Justice for taking action against her on the administrative side.

World.title: Bangladesh pro-uprising groups turn on each other on second anniversary
World.content:
Two years after a mass uprising forced Sheikh Hasina to flee the country, Bangladesh’s campuses and streets are once again witnessing political violence, this time not between the ousted Bangladesh Awami League and its opponents, but among the very parties and student groups that led the movement against her.

Bangladesh’s Prime Minister Tarique Rahman, who leads the Bangladesh Nationalist Party (BNP), had pledged during February’s election campaign to end the pattern of state-backed violence that marked Ms. Hasina’s rule before her ouster in the 2024 uprising. Six months into BNP-led rule, the country’s first elected government since the uprising, that promise is being tested on campuses nationwide, with rights groups blaming political rivalries, weak law enforcement and a culture of impunity for the continuing bloodshed.

The anniversary week itself has been marked by a fresh wave of clashes between the Bangladesh Jatiotabadi Chatra Dal (JCD), the BNP’s student wing, and the Bangladesh Islami Chhatra Shibir, the student wing of the Opposition Jamaat-e-Islami.

On Wednesday (August 5, 2026), at least 30 activists of the two organisations were injured in confrontations in several areas in the country, including Barishal University and Govt. Tolaram College.

A day earlier, on August 4, clashes between the two groups left more than 100 people injured across at least three institutions in the capital, including Jagannath University and Dhaka College. Within two days, the violence spread from Begum Rokeya University in Rangpur to different universities and colleges in the capital, prompting the university authorities to launch investigations and deploy additional police. A clash at Begum Rokeya University two days earlier had set off the chain of confrontations.

Deepening fracture

Political analysts say the clashes underline a deepening fracture within the coalition of parties, student groups and activists that came together to remove Ms. Hasina in August 2024 — one in which control of campuses, rather than ideology alone, has become the central battleground as Bangladesh marks two years since the uprising that reshaped its politics.

The most serious flashpoint was Jagannath University in Dhaka, where the trouble began during an official event to mark July Mass Uprising Day 2026, attended by University Grants Commission chairman Professor Mamun Ahmed as the chief guest, when student leaders of Chhatra Shibir tried to display placards listing their demands before the chairman. Two rounds of clashes followed, the first on the campus and the next outside the National Medical College Hospital where the injured had been taken. Both the JCD and the Shibir claimed that more than 30 of their activists and students, including the university students union’s vice-president, general secretary and assistant general secretary, were hurt. JCD activists were also seen entering the hospital’s emergency ward to assault the injured undergoing treatment. Accompanied by BNP loyalists, they also attacked the activists of the Chhatra Shakti, the student wing of the National Citizen Party (NCP), and on those of the Socialist Students’ Front at Jagannath University. The JCD and the Shibir have accused each other of instigating the violence.

The unrest also spilled over into an official state function at the China-Bangladesh Friendship Conference Centre, where Bangladesh Acting President Hafiz Uddin Ahmad was the chief guest at a programme marking the anniversary of the July uprising. The event was attended by senior government officials, diplomats and political leaders. A controversy erupted after a documentary screened during the programme reportedly credited BNP acting chairman Tarique Rahman with announcing the uprising’s one-point demand for Sheikh Hasina’s resignation. Student leaders objected to the portrayal, maintaining that it was Mr. Nahid Islam, convener of the NCP, who had announced the demand during the uprising. The disagreement led to commotion inside the venue. One student leader of the uprising alleged that he was assaulted by activists of the ruling party inside the programme in front of the President. The disruption prompted several diplomats attending the event to leave before the programme concluded.

Mob violence

Addressing the gathering, the President later expressed regret over the developments. He said that he felt “ashamed and pained” after witnessing the incident that happened in front of him. “This is a national event, but after witnessing what happened today, I lost interest in delivering my speech. I feel ashamed and painted.”

The President said the incident had exposed the divisions in the country’s national unity. He added that he had intended to deliver his speech in English for the benefit of the foreign guests, but decided against it after many foreign guests had left the venue, describing the situation as “unexpected”.

According to the Human Rights Support Society (HRSS), at least 17 people were killed and 51 injured in incidents of mob violence across the country in July 2026, while six more people died and 164 were injured in 45 separate incidents of political violence. The organisation noted that political violence had in fact declined compared with June when nine people were killed and 346 injured in 58 incidents.

In July’s political violence, two people were killed and 48 injured in 14 clashes within the BNP’s own ranks; six BNP-Jamaat confrontations left 44 injured; three clashes between the BNP and the Awami League loyalists left 13 injured; five clashes between the BNP and the NCP, the party formed by former student leaders of the uprising, left 38 injured; and 14 clashes between the BNP and other parties left 16 more injured. Three people were killed in three other incidents. Separately, 9,157 people were arrested in 193 political and other incidents in July, including 318 Awami League members, 28 BNP members, seven NCP members and one Jamaat member.

Meanwhile, the second anniversary of the uprising was marked in the midst of political tensions rather than celebrations. While the government inaugurated the July Mass Uprising Memorial Museum in the capital, opposition parties held separate programmes in the capital.

‘Another revolution’

Addressing a rally organised by an 11-party alliance near the Baitul Mukarram National Mosque, opposition leader and Ameer of Bangladesh Jamaat-e-Islami, Dr. Shafiqur Rahman, said, “We will not sit back and do nothing while the country is heading towards disaster.” He also claimed that, judging by the current situation, “another revolution is imminent”, and urged the people to be prepared.

On the other hand, after the inauguration of the July Mass Uprising Memorial Museum at Sher-e-Bangla Nagar in Dhaka, Prime Minister Rahman cautioned against attempts to create instability in the country. He said some people were “creating issues without reason” in post-authoritarian Bangladesh and urged them to consider whether such actions could inadvertently pave the way for the return of the ousted autocratic regime.

The museum, established by converting the official residence of ousted Prime Minister Sheikh Hasina, Ganabhaban, into a memorial to the 2024 mass uprising, could not be opened earlier due to various complications. It was finally inaugurated by the Prime Minister on the second anniversary of the uprising.

World.title: Life sentence for three in IUML councillor murder case in Kerala
World.content:
The Additional District and Sessions Court-III, Manjeri, on Wednesday sentenced three persons to life imprisonment for the murder of former Indian Union Muslim League (IUML) councillor Abdul Jaleel.

The convicts, Shuhaib alias Kochu, Abdul Majeed P.T., and Shamseer, were also fined ₹1 lakh each. Additional District and Sessions Judge Sooraj S. pronounced the verdict.

The incident took place at Kuttippara near Manjeri on March 29, 2022. The prosecution said Shuhaib and Abdul Majeed had stopped Jaleel and his friends following a dispute over giving side to their motorcycle. They allegedly assaulted them, damaged the car windshield with a helmet and threatened them.

Later that night, while Jaleel was checking the damage to the vehicle, Shamseer allegedly informed the other accused about his location. Shuhaib then attacked Jaleel with a granite stone, hitting him on the head.

Jaleel, who suffered serious injuries, died while undergoing treatment on March 30, 2022.

The court ordered that if the fine is paid, ₹3 lakh should be given to Jaleel’s legal heirs and ₹25,000 to Abbas, a witness in the case.

Then Manjeri Inspector C. Alavi investigated the case and arrested the accused. Inspector Riyas Chakkeeri later submitted the chargesheet.

The prosecution examined 45 witnesses and produced 98 documents and 12 material objects before the court. Special public prosecutor K.V. Sabu appeared for the prosecution.

The three convicts were shifted to the Kannur Central Jail after the verdict.

World.title: Pakistan, Iran agree to keep border crossings open round the clock to boost trade
World.content:
Pakistan and Iran on Wednesday agreed to further expand trade ties by keeping border crossings open round the clock, improving logistics and harmonising customs procedures.

The development came during a meeting between Prime Minister Shehbaz Sharif and a six-member Iranian delegation, led by Iran’s Minister for Industry, Mine and Trade Mohammad Atabak, in Islamabad, according to a statement issued by the Prime Minister’s Office (PMO).

During the meeting, the prime minister said that Pakistan highly valued its relations with its close, brotherly neighbour Iran, the PMO said.

“Pakistan will continue its sincere efforts for peace in the region,” PM Shehbaz was quoted as saying.
